Her father, Robert, expressed the family's deep grief, noting the tragedy of her life being cut short when she had much to look forward to. The venue for her wedding was transformed into a tribute site, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers in her memory.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman aims to strengthen his squad by signing Feyenoord's 20-year-old midfielder Tonny Vilhena and teammate Jordy Clasie, valued at £10 million. Koeman also seeks to make Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent, as the club targets a Europa League spot.

The National Trust has replaced antique furniture from 1820 with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House in Suffolk as part of an experiment to engage visitors, sparking outrage among heritage experts. The Trust plans similar experiments at nine other venues, arguing that the approach aims to enhance visitor experience by encouraging them to dwell and appreciate the atmosphere, though critics like art historian Bendor Grosvenor argue the move is misguided and patronizing.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was seen changing a flat tyre near the Sydney Conservatorium of Music, with assistance from a passerby, Felicity Waterford, who offered help and later took a selfie with him. Ms Waterford was waiting for her daughter at the Conservatorium when she noticed the incident. The event occurred just weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television.

Tony Pulis acknowledged Joey Barton's criticism that West Bromwich Albion's players lost their composure after leading 2-0 against Queens Park Rangers, resulting in a 3-2 defeat. Pulis admitted Barton "probably had a point," reflecting on his own experiences of leading teams that squandered leads. The teams are set to meet again, with Pulis confident in his team's improved performance and defensive resilience.

Primatologists in Ntokou-Pikounda National Park, Democratic Republic of Congo, have captured the first photograph of the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought to be extinct since the 1970s. The discovery confirms the species' survival but highlights its vulnerability to hunters in the commercial bushmeat trade. Researchers hope to study the monkey further to learn more about it.

Kim Kardashian, Kanye West, and their daughter North, along with Khloe Kardashian, visited Armenia's capital, Yerevan, for an eight-day trip. The visit, which included exploring landmarks like the Yerevan Opera House, marks their first time in the country where their late father, Robert Kardashian, was born. The celebrities stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, experiencing the city's blend of Soviet and Neo-Classical architecture.

Patrick and Valerie Jubb, British expats in southern Spain, are struggling to sell their luxury bed and breakfast in Jimena de la Frontera due to a legal dispute with the town hall over illegal additions made by a previous owner. The couple, who bought the property in 2008, face the possibility of losing their home as the town hall plans to demolish it. Despite obtaining a certificate stating there were no infractions when they purchased the estate, the alterations, including a first floor and pool, were deemed illegal.

Apple reported strong financial results for the first quarter, with over 61 million iPhones sold, accounting for more than two-thirds of its $58 billion revenue and the majority of its $13.6 billion profit. Sales in China surpassed those in the US, and despite a 29% decline in iPad revenue, the company's overall performance exceeded expectations, driven by iPhone sales which grew 40% from the previous year.

A 3-year-old's nightmares about a white van may provide clues about her mother's fatal SUV crash in Virginia. Natali Castellanos-Tyler, 30, died in a crash deemed an accident by police, but her daughter's visions suggest otherwise. Recently, there have been reports of hit-and-run incidents involving a similar white van in the area, raising doubts about the initial accident investigation.

Researchers at New York University found that the brain can enhance the recall of neutral or mundane events by associating them with emotions later on. This process, which involves brain regions like the amygdala, striatum, and hippocampus, helps in strengthening memories over time. The study highlights how emotions, whether positive or negative, can significantly improve memory retention, challenging the notion that only highly emotional events are remembered better.

Jackson Byrnes, an 18-year-old from northern NSW, was diagnosed with a stage four brain tumor, leaving him paralyzed and in need of urgent surgery. His girlfriend, Jahnae Jackson, has put her studies on hold to care for him, and they have raised over $80,000 through community support and a GoFundMe page for the surgery by Dr. Charlie Teo. Despite the surgery likely saving his life, Jackson faces a long rehabilitation period.

Hull City is interested in signing QPR centre-back Nedum Onuoha, who has 15 months left on his contract. Onuoha played a crucial role in QPR's recent win over West Bromwich Albion. Additionally, Hull City is also considering a move for Victor Anichebe, a striker from West Bromwich Albion, who could be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have mapped out unique phrases and grammatical structures across the United States, revealing regional linguistic variations. The interactive map highlights sentences like "All of my clothes needs washed" in Idaho and "I so might run this [race] with you" in California, showcasing how different states use English in distinct ways. The study, which includes some data from the UK, aims to document these grammatical differences systematically, focusing on natural usage rather than correctness.

Kalman Kallai, a Canadian man, embarked on a 2,796-mile journey from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia, transporting a free rocking chair he found online to enjoy the scenic views. Accompanied by his father for part of the trip, Kallai documented his unique adventure, posing with the chair in various settings and sharing it online.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood humorously responded to a letter from six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who had applied for the Villa manager position after Paul Lambert's departure. Sherwood revealed Charlie's requested win bonus of sweets and chocolate during a press conference, reciprocating with a Twix multi-pack, highlighting the lighter side of professional football.

World boxing champion Kell Brook attended a Premier League Darts event in his hometown of Sheffield, receiving a hero's ovation. Meanwhile, Dave Chisnall won both of his matches, defeating Gary Anderson and James Wade, to move to 17 points in second place in the league standings. Michael van Gerwen maintained his lead with an 7-5 victory over Stephen Bunting, while Phil Taylor suffered his fourth defeat in five matches against Raymond van Barneveld.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti praised teammate Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his significant off-field contributions, highlighting his role in helping young players and boosting team morale. Despite Ibrahimovic's 17 Ligue 1 goals this season, Verratti emphasized his supportive influence. Ibrahimovic, suspended for the first leg of PSG's Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona, will be available for the second leg at Nou Camp.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published sensitive details about RAF's main base on the Falklands Islands, including GPS coordinates and runway specifications, on their website. This information could aid potential invaders, particularly Argentina, in planning attacks. The incident occurred amid heightened tensions and Argentina's plans to lease Russian bombers, which could pose a threat to the islands' defenses. The MoD acknowledged the mistake but downplayed the sensitivity of the leaked information.

Huddersfield coach Paul Anderson aims to improve his team's offensive performance to match their strong defensive record, as they seek to climb the Super League ladder after dropping from third to ninth. Despite recent losses, Huddersfield boasts the league's best defense and could potentially rise to fourth with a win against Catalans Dragons, who have struggled in away games.

Windsor planners approved the opening of a second Costa cafe within 500 yards of an existing one, adding to the existing Costa Express nearby. This decision was met with mixed reactions; while some residents like Samantha Taylor criticized the oversaturation of coffee shops, others like Matt Gordon-Smith saw it as a positive sign of local economic improvement. The new Costa is set to open on the site of a former HSBC branch, with planners citing no legal grounds to refuse the application.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn its support for the shooting of free-running badgers in pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, advocating instead for trapping and then shooting them, citing concerns over effectiveness and humane treatment. The BVA maintains support for culling to control tuberculosis in cattle, a stance criticized by animal welfare campaigners. Meanwhile, Environment Secretary Liz Truss has pledged to expand culling efforts if the Conservatives win the upcoming election, despite opposition from wildlife groups.

Geoff Barrow, founder of Portishead, criticized streaming services like Spotify and YouTube for low royalty payments, receiving only £1,700 for 34 million plays. He expressed concern that this model hurts young artists' ability to establish themselves. In response, Jay-Z launched Tidal, a streaming service promising better returns for musicians, supported by artists including Rihanna and Madonna.

Game of Thrones' first four episodes of season five were leaked online before their official premiere, likely from press review copies. The episodes began appearing on torrent sites on Saturday night and had been downloaded over 550,000 times by Sunday morning. HBO is investigating the breach, which occurred within an approved group given access to the episodes. The show remains the most illegally downloaded program globally.

Daniel Buccheri, a 25-year-old Melbourne singer, composed an emotional song as his best man's speech at his brother Adrian's wedding, leaving guests in tears. The speech, performed at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, included tributes to his brother and his new wife Sarah, and has since gone viral with over 100,000 views online.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter and aspiring Team GB athlete for the Rio Olympics, has shared her fitness journey post-pregnancy. After the birth of her daughter Mia, Phillips found it challenging to regain her fitness and now adheres to a strict morning exercise routine, including cycling, and a balanced diet. She aims to qualify for the eventing team in the 2016 Olympics and hopes to instill a love for horses in Mia.

Raheem Sterling's interview about not signing a new contract with Liverpool angered many fans, who felt he was ungrateful for the club's support. Blogger David Tyrer noted the interview was ill-timed and likely changed fan perceptions, with some calling for Sterling's departure if the club gets a good deal. Despite Sterling's potential, Liverpool fans and the blogger agree the club shouldn't bend over backward to keep him, adhering to the club's mantra that no player is bigger than the team.

An old photo of Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola at Barcelona training has resurfaced, highlighting the era when many current top managers were teammates. Luis Enrique, now Barcelona's coach, and Laurent Blanc, now PSG's coach, were part of the 1996 Spanish Super Cup-winning team under Bobby Robson, alongside others who later became managers. This reveals how a single Barcelona team produced multiple influential figures in football management.

Eric Cantona, former Manchester United star, controversially declared Javier Pastore of Paris Saint-Germain as the best player in the world, praising his creativity over Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Cantona made the remarks at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai, highlighting Pastore's ability to surprise with his playmaking skills despite his relatively modest goal and assist numbers compared to Messi and Ronaldo.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murdering his tenant, Michael Spalding, whom he forced to work before killing him and dismembering the body. Simon, with the help of his girlfriend Michelle Bird, stuffed Spalding's remains into suitcases and dumped them in a Birmingham canal. The jury took 15 hours to reach a unanimous verdict at Birmingham Crown Court, while Bird was cleared of murder but admitted to assisting an offender.

Health experts and campaigners advocate for the use of 'loneliness maps' to identify areas with high risks of social isolation among the elderly and other vulnerable groups. Essex and Gloucestershire councils have already implemented these maps, which combine data on public health factors and resident surveys to pinpoint 'danger zones' of loneliness. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends this approach to other councils, emphasizing the need to address loneliness to prevent health issues like dementia and high blood pressure.

Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary as a waitress at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, declaring it her only job ever. She started working there at 15, trained by her mother who had been employed for 13 years. Eddingfield, who met her first husband at the restaurant, cherishes the family tradition and loyal customers.

Former England captain Mike Gatting argues that Kevin Pietersen shouldn't automatically return to the national team despite scoring runs for Surrey, suggesting current players like Gary Ballance and Ian Bell need to be considered. Gatting also highlights the pressure on current England captain Alastair Cook to perform well in upcoming matches, noting that Cook's recent poor form could lead to questions about his leadership if he fails to score runs against West Indies.

Caleb Benn, a 17-year-old Californian high school student, developed an iOS app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos directly from their computers, earning him $1,000 daily. However, Instagram, owned by Facebook, claims the app violates its terms of service and demands changes by Monday, threatening legal action. Benn argues that if he complies, the app's purpose would be defeated, as he was inspired by Instagram's lack of desktop uploading feature.

In South Korea, hoesik, or company dinners involving heavy drinking, are common social events where employees bond and build relationships. Foreigners often face pressure to participate in these drinking sessions, which are seen as essential for understanding colleagues and clients. Drinking etiquette is crucial, with rules dictating how and when to drink, and failure to follow them can be considered disrespectful. The culture of drinking affects daily life, influencing traffic patterns and work schedules.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was discharged from Aberdeen Royal Infirmary with a walking stick after being treated for a dislocated hip sustained during an Easter stay at Balmoral estate. Buckingham Palace confirmed his successful treatment and noted that he is expected to recover. The Duke, known for his royal duties and as President of the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club, was accompanied by his daughter Lady Helen Taylor upon leaving the hospital.

The Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of bikini-clad women managing parking meters, may be ending due to business leaders' calls for modernization. Local business owners argue the group is outdated and no longer provides a service, citing advancements in parking meter technology. However, the Meter Maids' general manager contends they are integral to the tourist experience and help maintain the area's reputation.

Greece denied it would default on a £330 million loan to the IMF, despite reports suggesting plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas confirmed the payment would be made on time, April 9. However, sources close to the Syriza party indicated the government might prioritize paying domestic obligations over loans unless the eurozone releases more bailout funds. Greece's finance ministry also refuted claims by a general secretary that the country would likely not pay the IMF tranche.

Turkey blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after they refused to remove images of prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz, who was killed during an armed siege. The court imposed the blocks because the images were upsetting Kiraz's family. Kiraz was targeted for his involvement in an investigation into the death of Berkin Elvan, a teenager who died after being hit by a tear-gas canister during protests.

Seven-year-old Colin Gilpatric, an aspiring Jedi Knight with autism, wrote to George Lucas asking if Jedi could marry without turning to the dark side. Lucasfilm responded with a letter affirming that true Jedi values include compassion and loyalty, essential for a selfless marriage, and sent Colin Star Wars merchandise. Colin was thrilled to receive the encouraging reply.

Wisconsin ended Kentucky's undefeated season in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, winning 71-64, with Frank Kaminsky scoring 20 points and grabbing 11 rebounds. Kentucky's loss means they finish the season with a 38-1 record, two wins short of becoming the first undefeated team since 1975-76. Meanwhile, Duke secured a spot in the final with an 81-61 victory over Michigan State, led by Justise Winslow's 19 points and Jahlil Okafor's 18.

Vince Neil of Mötley Crüe faced criticism for his rendition of the American national anthem before a Las Vegas game, highlighting the high stakes of performing the song. The article recalls other notable performances, including Whitney Houston's celebrated Super Bowl rendition in 1991 and Roseanne Barr's controversial performance in 1991, which President George H. W. Bush deemed "disgraceful." It also mentions Jimi Hendrix's controversial psychedelic version at Woodstock in 1969 and Michael Bolton's word-misinterpretation during a 2003 baseball game.

Security footage of a violent altercation in Sydney, where Barry Lyttle punched his brother Patrick, causing him to fall and hit his head on the pavement, leading Patrick into a coma, has been released. Prosecutor Alex Poulos called for Barry, who pleaded guilty to grievous bodily harm, to face a full-time jail term, while Patrick urged for the charges to be dropped. The incident occurred outside Hugo's Lounge in Potts Point on January 3, and Barry could face up to two years in prison.

Faith and Hope Howie, conjoined twin sisters who died 19 days after birth, were laid to rest at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney. Their family had built a memorial at the grave, but upon visiting, they found it cleared of all mementos, which were discarded in bins. The parents, Simon Howie and Renee Young, were devastated, retrieving only a quarter of the memorabilia, and criticized the cemetery for the lack of warning and respectful handling of the site.

Britain's Supreme Court President, Lord Neuberger, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear full-face veils in court, advocating for judges to respect different customs and be sensitive to cultural differences. This recommendation comes amid ongoing debates over the place of traditional Muslim dress in legal proceedings, following a 2003 case where a woman was jailed for refusing to remove her veil while testifying.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed in Missouri for killing Anthony Curtis in 1998 during a confrontation over child support payments. The U.S. Supreme Court rejected his appeals, including one regarding mental illness. Cole was executed by lethal injection at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri. Governor Jay Nixon refused clemency, highlighting the impact on crime victims.

Prince Harry will depart the UK for Australia without meeting his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped to fifth in the line of succession, had hoped to meet the new royal baby before leaving but will return in mid-May. The baby, fourth in line to the throne, was expected by Saturday, with details of the birth to be announced via press release and social media.

Justin Jackson, a Florida man, has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, her executives, and other celebrities to obtain free goods and job recommendations worth $2.4 million over eight years. Jackson allegedly tricked a jeweler by pretending to be Madonna's manager and later sent forged letters on Oprah's network's behalf to hotels and jewelry companies. He is being sued by Oprah's TV network and former Obama aide Reggie Love.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has set a €50 million price tag on star player Paulo Dybala, comparing him to Lionel Messi. Dybala, sought after by clubs including Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and PSG, could be sold to PSG if they meet the price. Inter Milan's Roberto Mancini was seen watching Dybala in a recent match, indicating the intense interest in the player.

Brazilians are protesting across the country, demanding President Dilma Rousseff's impeachment due to an economic downturn and a massive bribery scandal at state-run oil company Petrobras. The investigation reveals construction companies paid bribes to Petrobras executives and politicians for contracts, with most accused politicians belonging to Rousseff's Workers Party. Despite her approval rating plummeting to 13%, Rousseff denies involvement and claims she was a figurehead during her time at Petrobras.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has denied starring in a soft porn film, calling "You and the Night" a piece of art. The film, which includes racy scenes with Cantona in minimal clothing, has been both praised and criticized. Speaking at the Laureus Sports Awards in Shanghai, Cantona defended the film, emphasizing its artistic merit and beauty, despite its controversial nature.

Psychologists found that specific types of music can enhance flavors in food and drinks. For instance, The Beatles' music can heighten the enjoyment of fish and chips, while Pavarotti's Nessun Dorma complements bitter flavors like coffee. Professor Charles Spence from Oxford University explains that music can draw attention to certain tastes without creating new flavors, a concept he calls "digital seasoning." This research involves matching sounds to tastes, such as high-pitched music for sourness and deeper tones for bitterness.

Raheem Sterling has paused contract talks with Liverpool until the summer, despite receiving a £100,000-a-week offer. PFA chief Gordon Taylor supports Sterling's decision, arguing it's not disloyal and could be beneficial for both player and club to focus on the season's remaining competitions. Sterling, 20, has been linked with moves to Arsenal and Spanish clubs, but Taylor believes he remains committed to Liverpool.

La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, 38, from Ohio, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same company and lived just six minutes away after Ohio released birth records. Mitchell-Clark found Simmons on Facebook, leading to a reunion where she learned she has three younger biological sisters. Simmons, who gave birth at 15, expressed shock and relief at the reunion.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a gun trafficker, admitted to sending Aaron Hernandez, the convicted murderer of Odin Lloyd, three firearms a month before the killing. Oscar Hernandez, no relation to Aaron, pleaded guilty to weapons charges and described feeling 'awed' and 'grateful' when Aaron paid him $15,000 for the guns. Oscar faces up to 30 months in prison and was attacked by inmates after being incorrectly listed as a government witness.

Joel Parker, 33, was arrested in St Johns County, Florida, for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening and disrupting him during a ride. The driver, unharmed, called the police, leading to Parker's arrest for battery. Parker posted bond and received a trespass warning, banning him from using the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating his intention to keep the player beyond the summer despite previous interest from other clubs. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is expected to join England's under-21 team in the Czech Republic. Pulis praised Berahino's improved attitude and commitment, suggesting the player is content at West Brom.

Giovanni Lo Porto, an Italian aid worker, was abducted in Pakistan in 2012 while working on a reconstruction project after devastating floods. Two years later, he was killed alongside American Warren Weinstein in a U.S. drone strike aimed at an al Qaeda operation. Lo Porto, known for his humanitarian work and dedication to helping others, was working with Welthungerlife to provide clean water and sanitation in flood-affected areas.

Photographer John Massung captured a scene of hundreds of sharks swarming just 100 feet from the beach off the coast of south Florida. Experts identified the sharks as likely Blacktip or Spinner species, which migrate annually to breed. The photos were widely shared on social media, drawing attention to the shark activity near Sebastian Inlet.

Zeus, an 11-year-old retired German Shepherd K-9 officer from the Ridgefield Police Department, was honored with a farewell procession in Connecticut before being euthanized due to a degenerative hip disorder. The event, attended by fellow officers and residents, celebrated Zeus's eight-year service, during which he assisted in over 250 narcotics arrests and helped track down 50 missing or wanted individuals.

Reports of child sex abuse in the UK have surged by over 60% since 2011, following investigations like Operation Yewtree and the Rotherham scandal, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014. However, the number of arrests fell by 9%, leading to criticism of the government's handling of the issue. South Yorkshire saw a 577% increase in reported cases over five years, with only 74 cases reported in 2011 compared to 501 in 2014.

Iceland has become a favored filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters due to its stunning landscapes, with 17 production services companies now operating nationwide. Notable filming spots include Thingvellir National Park for "Game of Thrones," Svartalfheim for "Thor: The Dark World," and Svinafellsjokull glacier for "Interstellar." Europe's most powerful waterfall, Dettifoss, was used in "Prometheus" to depict the beginning of time.

In Melbourne, a 150-year-old blue and yellow bathing box sold for a record $276,000, surpassing its original asking price by $150,000. Meanwhile, in Sydney, a 1917-built fire station turned mechanic’s garage in Paddington sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. Additionally, an 1850s maximum security prison in Kilmore, Victoria, is on the market for $2 million after being transformed into a residence.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother from Morecambe, was diagnosed with a rare brain disorder called functional neurological disorder (FND) after a car accident left her with uncontrollable shaking and bladder issues. Following a series of tests, doctors confirmed her condition in September, a year after the accident. Now confined to her home and reliant on a mobility scooter, Rawcliffe struggles to walk and takes 32 different medications daily. FND is an umbrella term for neurological symptoms that cannot be explained, and effective treatments are limited.

Sculptor Dave Poulin admitted disappointment in a controversial Lucille Ball statue in Celoron, New York, nicknamed 'Scary Lucy,' and offered to replace it for free. The statue, based on a famous 'I Love Lucy' episode, has sparked a social media campaign demanding its removal due to its unflattering depiction. Poulin acknowledged the sculpture's poor representation of Ball's beauty and offered to create a new, more appealing statue at an estimated cost of $8,000 to $10,000.

David Alaba, Bayern Munich's versatile left-back, will miss around seven weeks of the season due to a torn knee ligament sustained while playing for Austria. The 22-year-old, who was previously out for three months earlier this season, expressed disappointment but aims to return for the season finale. His absence is a blow to Bayern, who are on track for a treble of titles in the Bundesliga, German Cup, and Champions League.

Beatrice Nokes, 21, and Daniel Williams, 37, appeared in court accused of running a prostitution ring in Central London. Nokes, a University College London student, is alleged to have incited three women into prostitution, while Williams, a Scotland Yard detective, faces additional charges including voyeurism and hiding profits. Both are accused of committing these crimes while Williams was on and off-duty.

A whistleblower has exposed a firm selling detailed personal health data, including information on eating disorder sufferers, for as little as 12p per record. The data, offered by Sequester, a business partner of Alchemy Direct Media, includes sensitive health conditions and financial details, prompting investigations by the Information Commissioner’s Office, the Direct Marketing Commission, and the General Pharmaceutical Council. The revelations highlight serious privacy concerns and potential risks for vulnerable individuals.

Jordan Spieth, at 21, won the Masters golf tournament at Augusta, matching Tiger Woods' 1997 record score. Post-victory, Spieth spoke about his 14-year-old autistic sister Ellie, expressing his wish to share the green jacket with her and acknowledging her influence in providing life perspective amidst professional pressures.

Dick Advocaat, Sunderland's new manager, emphasizes the importance of the Wear-Tyne Derby against Newcastle, contrasting it with his past mistake of underestimating the Old Firm derby at Rangers. Advocaat, who led Rangers to a treble despite a 5-1 loss in 1998 due to underestimating the rivalry, now stresses the significance of the game for Sunderland's fight against relegation.

Belinda Bartholomew, girlfriend of rugby player Aidan Guerra, claims she was racially abused at Sam the Butcher in Sydney when trying to change her chicken selection. The butcher denies the allegations, stating Bartholomew was rude and he was dealing with eftpos issues. The incident escalated with both parties accusing each other of inappropriate behavior, leading to a public dispute.

Cadbury is reducing the size of its Freddo Frog chocolates by 20%, from 15g to 12g, while keeping the price unchanged, due to rising manufacturing costs. This move follows a similar reduction in the size of Cadbury's family blocks of Dairy Milk chocolate. The changes have sparked anger among consumers, who have criticized the company for perceived greed and lack of value.

Hillary Clinton's campaign team met in Brooklyn to prepare for her presidential announcement, focusing on a "values statement" to guide the campaign and avoid past mistakes. The document emphasizes humility, discipline, and unity, highlighting the campaign's goal to elect Clinton as president to ensure prosperity for all Americans. Clinton is set to launch her campaign through a social media video and will soon visit key early voting states.

Kyli Wilfson, 29, from North Carolina, suffered from chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat for 18 months despite feeling hungry. Initially misdiagnosed with a mild pancreatic issue, she endured severe abdominal pain and was eventually diagnosed after a camera was inserted into her pancreas. Her condition led to rapid weight loss and reliance on a feeding tube, affecting her and her fiancé's daily life and diet routines.

The UK leaders' debate inspired numerous memes, featuring Labour's Ed Miliband and Conservative's David Cameron in humorous scenarios. Miliband was depicted as London rapper Plan B, challenging Cameron to a one-on-one debate, while Cameron and Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg were placed on the Gogglebox sofa. Other memes included SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon and UKIP's Nigel Farage, highlighting the lighter side of the political event.

Amir Khan, a British boxer, is on the verge of facing either Floyd Mayweather or Manny Pacquiao, two of the best boxers in the world. Initially, Khan was set to fight Mayweather in Las Vegas, but now there's a possibility of him facing Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi. Promoter Bob Arum, who represents Pacquiao, is considering an offer for a fight in Abu Dhabi this November or December, with Khan as the top choice. Khan's speed and recent impressive performances make him a strong contender for the fight.

A two-bedroom home in Islington, London, measuring just 5ft wide in parts, has been sold for £750,000. Despite its narrow dimensions, the property includes a kitchen, reception room, and a garden. The estate agency described it as "well proportioned," and it was put on the market by Foxtons. The buyer will pay £27,000 in stamp duty, highlighting the high cost per square foot.

Nicola Sturgeon plans to launch an SNP manifesto proposing policies aimed at forming a power-sharing deal with Labour, including slashing tuition fees and rolling back NHS competition. The manifesto also calls for increased borrowing to fund £180 billion in spending over five years, with polls suggesting the SNP could win up to 50 seats, potentially holding the balance of power at Westminster.

Rangers goalkeeper Robby McCrorie's errors led to Celtic's victory in the Glasgow Cup, with Josh Kerr scoring from a missed clearance and Mark Hill converting a dropped free kick. The match, held at Hampden Park, was largely trouble-free, with Celtic's youth team securing their fourth win in eight seasons. Ronny Deila's Celtic side dominated play, creating numerous chances, while Rangers struggled to mount a significant attack.

Tony Pulis, known for his distinctive style and gritty playing tactics, led West Bromwich Albion to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, his former club, securing crucial points that virtually guarantee West Brom's Premier League safety. Pulis, wearing his trademark cap and track suit, praised his team's resilience, contrasting with Alan Pardew's more formal attire. The win ended West Brom's 10-game away run without a victory.

Jameela Jamil spent £3,000 to remove and replace her amalgam fillings with white ones, believing they caused health issues like chronic fatigue and fainting for nearly seven years. Blood tests revealed high mercury levels, which were linked to her dental work. Despite her experience, dental experts maintain that amalgam fillings are safe and the mercury exposure from them is minimal and harmless.

Suge Knight, facing murder and attempted murder charges, appeared in court hoping Floyd Mayweather would bail him out after his upcoming fight. Despite his lawyer's optimism, Knight's bail was not reduced from $10 million, and he had to be wheeled out in a wheelchair due to health issues. Knight's trial is set to begin on July 7 unless a motion is made to postpone it.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine revealed in an interview with Puss Puss magazine that her British shorthair cat, Kimchi, has a discerning palate, enjoying human foods like poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. The cat also loves cheese, caviar, and fishy treats, leading Erskine to put Kimchi on a diet. Erskine recently adopted another cat named Ponzu, who has shown a penchant for unusual foods, including green curry.

Martin Springall, a 38-year-old living in Tokyo, took a photo of his daughter in Zushi, Japan, in 2014, which later went viral due to a mysterious pair of black boots appearing behind her. Springall claims he has no idea what the boots are and insists the photo was not altered. The image sparked debate on Reddit, with some suggesting paranormal activity or a trick of the light.

The Conservative Party plans to introduce a four-year ban on foreign workers receiving UK benefits, requiring them to pay an average of £22,000 in taxes before eligibility. This includes barring unemployed EU migrants from state support and deporting those without jobs within six months. The proposal aims to curb migration and will be part of the party's manifesto and renegotiation with the EU, with a referendum on EU membership planned by 2017.

Cody Neatis, an eight-year-old with multiple disabilities, was left to sleep on a hospital floor for seven nights at Royal Preston Hospital due to a lack of a suitable bed. Cody, who has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, and autism, requires a special high-sided cot for safety. His mother, Lynne Neatis, has slept alongside him, fearing he might injure himself or pull out his oxygen. The family's situation highlights ongoing issues with hospital accommodations for disabled children.

Sportsmail's Derek Lawrenson provides daily updates from the Masters, where Rory McIlroy aims for a career grand slam and Tiger Woods makes a comeback, accompanied by his children. Ian Poulter's excitement led him to forget his golf clubs, while Henrik Stenson competes despite recovering from flu. The article also highlights historical moments like Gene Sarazen's albatross shot and the tradition of skipping balls over the 16th hole's water.

Juventus has ruled out signing Manchester United's loan striker Radamel Falcao due to his high wages, despite Falcao's interest in joining the Serie A champions last summer. Falcao, who has struggled at Old Trafford with only four goals, is expected to leave United this summer. Juventus is now focusing on other strikers, including Paulo Dybala from Palermo and Edinson Cavani from Paris Saint-Germain, to reinforce their forward line.

David Cameron pledges to sell £4 billion of Lloyds Bank shares to the public if re-elected, offering individuals up to £10,000 worth of shares at a discount. This move, aimed at reducing national debt, echoes Thatcher-era privatizations and includes a loyalty bonus for long-term shareholders. The sale would be the largest since the 1980s and is seen as a reminder of economic challenges under the previous government.

Scientists warn that living near congested roads with high air pollution can cause 'silent strokes,' increasing the risk of dementia. A study involving over 900 people aged 60 and older found that exposure to PM2.5, tiny particles from traffic and industrial emissions, is linked to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes, which can lead to brain damage and shrinkage. Researchers used MRI scans to measure brain matter and satellite imagery to assess pollution exposure, highlighting the need for further investigation into long-term impacts.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness advocate who battled cancer for seven years, died in February. Her fiancé, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she underwent radiation treatment in her final weeks, integrating it with her natural healing methods. Ainscough initially avoided conventional treatments like chemotherapy, opting for unproven therapies. Pamenter shared her courage and grace in a heartfelt letter to her followers.

A multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale, Brisbane, involved ten people, including four children, resulting in injuries that required hospitalization. Four individuals were airlifted to hospitals, while six others with minor injuries were taken to Ipswich Hospital. The highway was closed for several hours, and diversions were implemented. Queensland Fire and Rescue used hydraulic cutting gear to free a trapped individual.

Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old Colorado resident and volunteer at the Colorado Gator Farm, walked a slackline over a pool containing over 50 alligators, some up to ten feet long. McDonald, who has been working with alligators for over a decade, said the reptiles were surprisingly unbothered by the slackline. He plans to walk over larger alligators and albino ones in the future, despite his mother's concerns about his safety.

Abdul Hadi Arwani, a Syrian imam and opponent of President Bashar Al-Assad, was shot dead in his car in London. Sources suggest he may have met his killer days before the murder when the killer, posing as a potential client, postponed a building quote request because Arwani was accompanied by his son. Scotland Yard's counter-terrorism unit is investigating, considering the possibility of a politically motivated assassination linked to Arwani's activism against the Assad regime.

In Hong Kong, a small bakery selling Jenny's butter cookies has sparked a craze, with long lines and resellers marking up prices by 70%. The popularity has led to counterfeit products and warnings from the original shop. This cookie frenzy mirrors global food crazes like cronuts and ramen burgers, though it remains a significant local phenomenon.

Kira Hollis, diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and anorexia, turned her life around through bodybuilding, gaining weight and confidence. Initially ordered by doctors to go to the gym, she became a personal trainer and credits her six-year-old daughter and boyfriend for her recovery. Her journey inspired millions after she shared her story online.

Eighteen-year-old jockey Lewis Ferguson survived a dramatic double somersault fall from his horse Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton, an incident that went viral online. Despite the frightening fall, Ferguson returned to work at Paul Nicholls' stable the next day, showing only a minor cut on his nose. He expressed no intention of letting the incident deter him from his racing career, aiming for prestigious events like the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree.

Hillary Clinton launched an unconventional campaign to rebrand and reframe her image, using a video, new logo, and a road trip to emphasize a more empathetic and forward-looking persona. Critics were harsh, but from a marketing perspective, the strategy aimed to shift public perception from "I" to "we," potentially creating a more relatable image for voters. The road trip, particularly an unscripted stop at Chipotle, was seen as an attempt to connect with everyday Americans.

Over 1,700 Chinese students from Yichuan Senior High School in Shaanxi province took an exam in their school playground due to insufficient indoor space. The freshmen organized the outdoor exam themselves, turning their desks and chairs as directed by radio announcements to avoid sunlight glare. The school viewed this as a test of organizational skills and a way to reduce cheating, while students saw it as a novel experience that could help them feel more relaxed.

Sportsmail and Gillette are offering a competition where one lucky reader can win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Joe Hart, the England and Manchester City goalkeeper. The prize also includes a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shave gel. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a one-year-old orangutan rejected by his natural and first surrogate mothers, found a loving home with Maggie, a 53-year-old experienced surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. After 10 months, Kecil and Maggie share an inseparable bond, with Maggie proving her parenting skills once again. The pair will make their first public appearance this weekend.

Noelle Baynham, 61, was found dead at her home in Winchester, Hampshire, after her body was partially consumed by her two pet dogs. A concerned friend discovered her remains when she failed to answer the door, finding her in a state where her dogs had eaten parts of her vital organs, making the cause of death undeterminable. The most likely cause was an accidental overdose of medication, given the presence of various drugs in her system.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic will face trial for fraud, accused of betting on a match where his Montpellier club lost unexpectedly after securing the title. Along with his brother Luka and 15 others, including former teammates, Karabatic denies the charges and faces potential imprisonment and fines. The case stems from an unusually high increase in betting activity during halftime, which triggered a police investigation.

Six men were jailed for a total of 31 years for sexually abusing teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The offences, including rape and inciting sexual activity with children, occurred at parties organized on social media and at the defendants' homes. The victims, aged 13 to 16, were described as emotionally immature and targeted by the gang led by Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21. Thames Valley Police's Operation Reportage helped track down the victims, leading to the convictions.

Aaron Hernandez, convicted of murder, faces additional trials including a murder case for the 2012 shooting deaths of Daniel de Abreu and Safiro Furtado in Boston. He also faces civil suits from the victims' families and another man claiming Hernandez shot him in Miami. Hernandez's legal team argues he cannot adequately defend himself during the Massachusetts trial, while his NFL union seeks to recover a disputed $3.3 million signing bonus.

Emirates Airline is set to sign a £30 million, three-year deal to sponsor the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. This move adds to Emirates' extensive sports sponsorship portfolio, which includes deals with Arsenal, AC Milan, and Hamburg, among others. The agreement with Arsenal, worth £150 million, provides Emirates with naming rights to the Emirates Stadium and a place on the club's shirt.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, announced his intention to compete in a fifth Olympics in Rio next year, despite facing a six-month suspension from USA Swimming after a second drunken driving arrest. He will not participate in the upcoming world championships in Russia as part of his punishment, emphasizing his commitment to his recovery and the team's success. Phelps, who has been undergoing treatment and attending Alcoholics Anonymous meetings, expressed remorse for his actions and acknowledged significant personal growth during his rehabilitation.

Gareth Bale is a significant doubt for Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury sustained during a match against Malaga. Real Madrid's statement revealed a muscular lesion in Bale's left leg, with his condition to be evaluated. Additionally, Luka Modric is out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain, while Karim Benzema is expected to return after missing the previous match with a knee injury. Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid were drawn 0-0 in their first leg.

Scientists at Texas Tech University found that over 50% of retirees sold their investments during the 2007-2008 financial crisis, leading to significant losses. Those who sold at the market's lowest point saw their £100,000 pension drop to £63,000, compared to £141,000 for those who held on. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, highlights how emotional decision-making, often exacerbated by cognitive decline, can lead to poor financial choices in retirement.

Stuart Pearce advocates for Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini to be given more time to improve the team's performance, following a series of poor results that have jeopardized their title and top-four positions. Pearce attributes City's decline partly to Yaya Toure's ineffective season and suggests the squad needs significant strengthening in the upcoming transfer window.

Manchester United's players, including Wayne Rooney and Robin van Persie, trained ahead of their crucial Premier League match against Manchester City. United, currently ahead of City in the league table, aim to maintain their position in the top four, with victory potentially widening their lead to four points. The derby, historically challenging for United, is seen as a game of pride and importance for both clubs and their fans.

Fiorentina's Champions League hopes diminished after losing 1-0 to Verona, conceding a late goal by Obbadi. The defeat left Fiorentina nine points behind third-placed AS Roma, in sixth place with 49 points. Coach Vincenzo Montella acknowledged the team's poor performance, noting they failed to capitalize on their dominance. Fiorentina also missed a penalty, further complicating their chances.

At the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, Miley Cyrus drew attention not for her outfit but for her visible underarm hair, sparking debate on social media. While some criticized her grooming choice, others defended her right to choose how to manage her body hair, highlighting the ongoing conversation about body hair acceptance.

Barcelona's star trio of Messi, Neymar, and Suarez reached a milestone of 100 goals collectively for the season after Barcelona's 6-0 victory over Getafe. Messi scored twice, Neymar once, and Suarez twice, bringing their totals to 49, 32, and 21 goals respectively. This achievement highlights Barcelona's dominance in La Liga, where they now lead by five points.

Andrea McVeigh, 44, was severely injured when hit by a cyclist on a pavement in Bermondsey, south London, on April 14. The cyclist fled the scene after the incident, leaving McVeigh with significant facial injuries, including two three-inch gashes on her forehead. Her husband chased the cyclist, who smiled at him before disappearing. The Metropolitan Police have released CCTV footage and appealed for witnesses to help identify the suspect.

Paul Gregory, 51, from Bedford, was fined £795 for fraudulently obtaining a blue badge by claiming he could only walk 200 meters, despite being an active member of a mountaineering club. The fraud was exposed when council officials read a newspaper article about Gregory's 191-mile hike in Cumbria. At Luton Magistrates' Court, he pleaded guilty and was also ordered to perform 150 hours of unpaid work and undergo 'thinking skills' sessions.

Apple has been awarded a patent for a facial recognition system that could unlock devices using selfies, filed in March 2011. The system involves scanning a user's face with the front-facing camera when the phone is moved into a specific position and unlocking if the image matches one on file. Unlike Android's 'Trusted face' feature, Apple's method would automatically unlock the device based on the phone's movement and face angle, without needing to press the power button.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, and her family were removed from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note to fly, despite having cancer. Sedway, who has multiple myeloma, was initially seated but was later asked to leave due to airline concerns about her health during an eight-hour flight. The incident was captured in a video posted on Facebook, showing the family's emotional departure from the plane.

On Easter Sunday night, a 1973 E-Type Jaguar and a Toyota Kluger collided head-on at a traffic light intersection on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The crash, which occurred during Operation Tortoise, left the classic Jaguar, valued over $120,000, completely destroyed, and resulted in three people being taken to hospital as a precaution. NSW police are investigating the incident.

Google has established a four-person team focused on developing advanced battery technologies for devices like phones, tablets, and electric cars. The team, led by Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj since 2012, explores flexible and wearable battery solutions, including solid-state and thin-film batteries, as revealed in a Wall Street Journal report. Google's efforts also extend to creating batteries for extreme conditions, such as subfreezing temperatures for its Project Loon internet-providing balloons.

British yacht designer Tony Castro has unveiled the 223ft Explorer, an exclusive superyacht for the ultra-wealthy, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and ample space for luxury vehicles and water toys. The yacht, priced at approximately 40 million euros to build, accommodates 12 guests and 15 crew members, offering luxurious amenities like a cinema, sauna, and gym. Designed to withstand any weather, it is a stylish and versatile vessel for globetrotting.

Ed Miliband is pushing forward with Labour's controversial plan to cap rents, despite warnings from experts and business leaders that it could backfire. The plan includes offering three-year tenancies and banning rent increases above inflation during this period, but critics argue it contains loopholes that could lead to more evictions and higher rents. Senior Tories and the Confederation of British Industry have dismissed the proposal as economically illiterate and potentially harmful to the housing market.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter, Ryan Dearnley, was removed from his role as Reading's mascot in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after expressing support for Arsenal. The decision came following outrage from Reading fans and a poll showing 85% disapproval. The Football Association moved Ryan to an England mascot role instead, offering him two tickets to watch the match in the Arsenal end, which he declined.

Astronomers propose a giant supervoid, 1.8 billion light-years across, as the cause of a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, potentially the largest structure ever found. This void, less dense than other parts of the universe, could explain the anomaly in the cosmic microwave background radiation first discovered in 2004. The research, conducted by the University of Hawaii, suggests the supervoid saps energy from passing light, leading to a colder appearance in the CMB.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, is displaying the chair in which Abraham Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre in Washington D.C. in 1865, as part of the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, believed to have an oil stain mistaken by many as blood, will be showcased in an open plaza on April 15, with a lecture by historian Doris Kearns Goodwin on April 13. The chair has been part of the museum's collection since 1937.

Jake Boys, a 19-year-old from East Sussex, mistakenly booked flights to Dublin instead of Cardiff when surprising his girlfriend Emily-Victoria Canham with tickets to see One Direction. The mix-up occurred because he thought Cardiff was in the Republic of Ireland. Both are popular YouTube vloggers, and now Boys plans to buy train tickets for the June concert in Cardiff.

A Romanian company, MB Telecom, has developed the Roboscan 2M Aeria, the world's first mobile X-ray scanner for airplanes, capable of detecting contraband, weapons, and bombs. The device, costing €3 million, can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial aircraft in about 20 minutes but emits radiation unsafe for passengers. Currently used for truck inspections, it aims to enhance security at low-security airports.

Stephen Munden, a 54-year-old convicted paedophile with a known obsession for young girls, has escaped from a psychiatric unit in Hampshire, UK. Munden, who was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl, vanished from the hospital near Hook at 6:15 pm on Tuesday. Police are searching for him, describing him as a heavyset man with dark hair, possibly without his beard.

Middlesbrough, led by Aitor Karanka, holds a strong position in the Championship, with a one-point lead over Bournemouth and a challenging match against Watford. The promotion race is tight, with seven points separating eight teams, and the psychological advantage of early match times could benefit Middlesbrough. Watford's Odion Ighalo aims to secure a win, while Bournemouth and Norwich also vie for top spots.

Grey hair is becoming a popular trend, with many women embracing their silver locks and sharing images on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend, which has been supported by fashion shows and celebrities like Rihanna and Lady Gaga, is seen as a form of feminist statement and a move away from traditional hair dyeing practices.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, an Ohio couple struggling with chronic conditions and financial hardships, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning in their home. Less than two months prior, they had launched online fundraisers pleading for help, detailing their dire living conditions and lack of resources. Despite their efforts, they received no donations, leading to their tragic end. The couple left behind two daughters and their pets.

Liberal Democrats leader Nick Clegg vowed to remain as party leader regardless of election outcomes, despite pressure to step down if the party's representation drops below 30 MPs or is left out of power. During a campaign visit in south London, Clegg emphasized his optimism for the party's future and criticized the Labour and Conservative parties for abandoning the political center. He also suggested a potential coalition with the Conservatives again, highlighting his role in forming the previous coalition government.

Terry Cooper, a 79-year-old from Somerset, narrowly escaped a badger attack in his garden, thanks to his Jack Russell, Sam. The badger, unusually large with six-inch teeth, burst through a hedge with two cubs, prompting Sam to pull Cooper indoors. The National Farmers' Union advised residents to secure their properties against badgers, suggesting narrow-spaced fencing and removing food sources that might attract them.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose 3-0 to Porto U21s in the Premier League International Cup semi-final at Motspur Park, avoiding the Champions League quarter-final matches. Joined by his son Jose Junior, Mourinho was present as Porto's Leandro Silva scored a hat-trick, while Fulham's Liam Donnelly was sent off just before half-time.

Property developer Andreas Christopheros, 29, was critically injured when corrosive liquid was thrown in his face outside his home in Truro, Cornwall, last December. David Phillips, 48, was charged with grievous bodily harm with intent and pleaded not guilty at Truro Crown Court, while his wife Nicole Phillips, 45, faces charges of perverting the course of justice. Christopheros suffered life-changing injuries, including loss of vision and facial scars.

Someone in Lastres, a Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route, has posted signs warning pilgrims not to defecate on the trail. The signs, which resemble no-littering warnings, have become an attraction for some pilgrims who pose for photos with them. Angry residents have complained about pilgrims defecating outside their homes, while the mayor criticized the lack of public facilities for pilgrims along the route.

A fire consumed a building in Flint, Michigan, formerly housing the strip club The Body Shop, on Wednesday at about 1pm. Thick smoke and large flames were reported, with only the building and nearby power lines affected. Local resident Terry Rauh mentioned a previous fire at the site. An investigation into the cause of the blaze is ongoing.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, reached a settlement in her lawsuit against the federal government, Frontier Airlines, the Transportation Security Administration, and the Wayne County Airport Authority for being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport. Hebshi, who was detained and humiliated on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks, will receive $40,000 in compensation. The settlement also includes amendments to Frontier's employee handbook and customer complaint policy to prevent future discrimination.

Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 from Seoul to Hiroshima crash-landed and skidded off the runway, injuring twenty people among 74 passengers and seven crew members. The Airbus A320 reportedly missed the landing point, spun 180 degrees, and deployed evacuation slides. The airport was closed, and emergency services responded to the incident, which occurred at 8pm local time.

Made In Chelsea star Mark-Francis Vandelli has revealed his collection of 16 expensive watches to the Evening Standard, including a Cartier white gold Moonphase worth £32,000 and a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42 he bought for £6,500. He collects a new watch annually, favoring rare pieces like the discontinued Cartier Tortue Collection Privée.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy, known for roles in "All Creatures Great and Small" and as Winston Churchill, is selling his extensive collection of over 200 antiques, including a diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, at a £100,000 auction. The auction, featuring items like a longbow and a portrait of Hardy holding it, is set to take place this Saturday at Dominic Winter auctioneers in South Cerney, Gloucestershire. Hardy, an 89-year-old military historian and former student of J.R.R. Tolkien, expressed sadness at parting with his collection but entrusted the sale to the auctioneers.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook expressing outrage at a scene on a Rio de Janeiro train platform, which was shared over 100,000 times in 24 hours. The image showed two women hugging, but Felippe's post cleverly spoofed conservative attitudes by warning about public behavior and safety regulations, ultimately criticizing those who stand on the yellow line instead of following safety rules. His post received praise for its witty approach to combating homophobia.

Jonathan Stevenson, now a director at LiveWire Sport, shared a letter from the late cricket legend Richie Benaud, responding to Stevenson's 1996 query about left-handed leg spin bowling when he was 16. Benaud's detailed advice, dated September 27, 1996, included tips on various deliveries and emphasized the differences in coaching left and right-handed bowlers.

Mark Zuckerberg discussed the future of travel through virtual reality during a Q&A on Facebook, envisioning a world where users can share and experience 3D scenes and new environments without physical travel. Facebook, which acquired Oculus, plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed, allowing users to explore locations using VR headsets like the Oculus Rift, which can capture and display scenes from multiple viewpoints.

Guo Kai fulfilled his girlfriend Dong Hui's birthday wish by having their wedding photographs taken despite her being bedridden in hospital due to bone cancer in Sichuan, China. Family and friends helped Dong put on a wedding dress, and professional photographers captured the moment, with Guo promising to support her through her treatment. The couple, who met a year ago, had planned to marry this month but had to postpone due to Dong's sudden illness.

Blaine Boudreaux, 34, was charged with intoxication manslaughter and other offenses after causing three DUI collisions in Houston on Sunday, resulting in two deaths, including a 6-year-old boy, and injuries to others. Boudreaux allegedly struck and killed a 61-year-old homeless man and fatally injured the boy, who was a passenger in his mother's car. He was arrested at the scene of the final crash after failing a field sobriety test.

Microsoft launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond, Washington campus, in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The initiative was announced by Microsoft Corporate VP Mary Ellen Smith, whose son has autism, emphasizing the company's commitment to diversity and inclusion. Smith highlighted the unique advantages individuals with autism can bring to the workforce.

Sheriff Stanley Glanz of Tulsa, Oklahoma, reassigned two deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris by Reserve Deputy Robert Bates due to threats against them and their families. The deputies were criticized for pinning Harris to the ground as he struggled to breathe, and the sheriff's office temporarily suspended its drug unit pending a review of the incident. Bates, 73, is charged with second-degree manslaughter and claims the shooting was accidental.

Katie Prager, 24, and her husband Dalton, 23, both suffering from cystic fibrosis, face a critical situation as Katie awaits a life-saving lung transplant. Diagnosed with a lung infection in 2009, Katie's health has deteriorated, and her insurance, Kentucky Medicaid, refuses to cover the out-of-state treatment needed at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Dalton is pleading for help, as Medicaid considers Katie's case financially, potentially ending their love story.

Researchers using Sleep Cycle app data found that South Africans wake up earliest on Mondays, while Americans rise at 7am on Tuesdays and report the worst mood. Slovakia had the best sleep quality, while the UK ranked 45th and the US 49th. Globally, Wednesday nights offered the best sleep quality, with more than half of surveyed countries experiencing their most restful sleep then.

A collection of 25 unpublished love letters from Mexican artist Frida Kahlo to Catalan artist Jose Bartoli, written between 1946 and 1949, are set to be auctioned at Doyle New York on April 15, expected to fetch over $120,000. The passionate correspondence, saved by Jose until his death in 1995, includes more than 100 pages of letters, drafts of responses, and personal items like a drawing of a sleeping cat.

Len McCluskey, leader of the trade union Unite, campaigned in South Wales for Labour, showcasing his popularity among activists. Despite his genial demeanor, he is viewed as a potent and potentially sinister force in British politics, aiming to exert significant influence over Labour candidates and policy. Unite, with 1.42 million members, seeks to implement socialist policies reminiscent of the 1970s, including increased public sector expansion and higher taxation, which could jeopardize the country's governance.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv filmed animals drinking water from troughs using a GoPro camera placed at the bottom, capturing 30 hours of footage. The animals, including a rhino that almost kissed the water and a lemur that delicately licked it, were initially cautious but eventually adapted to the camera's presence. Hershkowitz edited the footage into a four-minute video showcasing unique drinking behaviors of various animals.

A YouGov poll reveals that only 25% of voters believe David Cameron is most eager to win the election, compared to 43% who think Ed Miliband is the most passionate. Despite criticism of a lackluster campaign, Cameron insisted he was working hard, appearing in casual attire to demonstrate his commitment. Meanwhile, SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon was perceived as enjoying the campaign the most by 34% of voters.

Zaur Dadaev, accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemtsov, told a Moscow court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Dadaev, one of five Chechen men charged, had previously confessed but later retracted his statement, claiming signs of torture. The shooting occurred on February 27 near the Kremlin, prompting a large protest march in Moscow. Human rights activists reported injuries on Dadaev's body, though Russia Today disputed this claim.

A photo of four-month-old Sonit Awal being rescued from the rubble in Nepal after a 7.8-magnitude earthquake on April 25 has become iconic. The earthquake killed over 5,000 people and injured at least twice as many. Sonit was trapped for 22 hours in Muldhoka, Bhaktapur, before being pulled to safety by Nepalese Army soldiers on Sunday morning, completely uninjured.

Narcocon, a Scientology-affiliated drug rehab network, is contesting zoning laws to build a rehab center on Trout Run, a 40-acre property near Camp David in Maryland. Purchased for $4.85 million in 2013, the site is currently zoned for resource conservation, but Narcocon argues it has historic significance due to a fish caught by President Hoover, aiming to bypass regulations. The center would use saunas and vitamin therapy, costing over $30,000 per month, and faces criticism for its controversial methods and alleged past wrongful deaths.

Five English-speaking Afghan men previously employed by NATO are now unemployed and homeless in Kabul, fearing reprisals and unable to return to their families. The city, once bustling with NATO presence, now faces deserted streets and empty shops as foreigners leave. Neighborhoods that were once expensive and occupied by foreigners are now vacant, and the infrastructure built during the war stands idle.

A US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured on Friday while swimming in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia. The SEALS were in lap lanes without gear and were found at the bottom of the pool by a fellow service member around 3pm local time. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two, and an investigation into the incident is ongoing.

NBC, holding live rights for the Premier League in the USA, expects more Americans to watch each match live than Britons by the next season. In 2012-13, 13 million Americans watched at least one game; last season, this number rose to 32 million. NBC transported its entire production team to England for the first time this weekend, covering matches like Burnley against Arsenal and the Manchester derby, enhancing coverage with analysts and former players.

Boris Johnson verbally attacked Ed Miliband on the BBC's Andrew Marr Show, accusing him of doing more damage to the country than he did to his brother. The exchange turned into a heated argument, with Johnson claiming Labour would need SNP support to form a government, making it impossible for Miliband to govern in the UK's best interests. Miliband dismissed Johnson's comments, stating, "Come on Boris, you're better than that."

Dustin Irons, a prisoner in Oregon, was sentenced to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court after he flashed a judge via video-link during a court hearing. Despite being handcuffed, Irons managed to pull down his pants, leading to his sentence increase and potential further disciplinary actions within the jail. The incident occurred as Irons, who was facing charges including assault and criminal mischief, expressed dissatisfaction with the court proceedings.

Jenson Button of McLaren expressed optimism about the team's progress ahead of the Chinese Grand Prix, following improvements shown in Malaysia despite both Button and teammate Fernando Alonso retiring. McLaren's car demonstrated competitive pace against midfield runners like Force India and Sauber, marking a significant step forward from their poor performance in Australia. Button acknowledged the team still needs to enhance downforce and power unit performance but praised the basic car's strength, especially in high-speed scenarios.

The $2 billion Fiona Stanley Hospital in Perth was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, raising serious hygiene concerns. The hospital previously lost its medical service provider, Serco, after failing to return sterilizing equipment by an arranged date in February. Australian Medical Association WA president Michael Gannon expressed deep concern over the ongoing issues, suggesting that the problem has not been adequately resolved. These incidents, including a patient's death last month, have severely damaged the hospital's public image and morale among staff.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, from Nottingham, chose to forgo their dream wedding to afford one last round of IVF, which resulted in the birth of twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley. Weeks later, they won a wedding competition, allowing them to finally say their vows. The couple had previously spent £5,500 on two unsuccessful rounds of IVF before making the difficult decision to prioritize family over their wedding.

Scooter's Coffee in Omaha had its Facebook page hacked and filled with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link. The hackers controlled the page for nearly 24 hours, posting adult cartoons similar to those seen in previous hacks of Delta Air Lines and Crayola. Despite contacting Facebook multiple times, Scooter's regained control only after reaching out to larger businesses. The company issued an apology to its customers for the inappropriate content.

A young Shibu Inu puppy caused amusement at an American Kennel Club center by attempting to bark at a husky, making high-pitched squeaks and yaps. The video shows the Shibu Inu vocalizing loudly while the husky whines, with onlookers laughing and filming the interaction. The Shibu Inu later runs in its owner's arms, trying to get closer to the husky, before a staff member calms it down with a rub. Canine vocalization typically starts around two to three weeks old and develops into barks by seven to eight weeks, though some puppies may take up to 16 weeks.

Liam Plunkett, a 29-year-old England seamer, aims to use his pace to challenge the West Indies in an upcoming Test series. Recovering from a minor ankle injury, Plunkett seeks to make an impact in the Caribbean, where he plans to "rough up" the opposition with his speed. He competes for a starting position with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, with the first Test scheduled for April 13 in Antigua.

Paul Smith, known for his previous challenges against Arthur Abraham, will face Andre Ward in a non-title bout, serving as Ward's warm-up before a potential rematch with Carl Froch. Ward, considered one of the top five pound-for-pound boxers, has not fought for 17 months. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to unify their titles, but Ward prefers to fight in London rather than Nottingham. Meanwhile, Froch is considering a fight against Julio Cesar Chavez Jr. in Las Vegas.

Tyrus Byrd, the newly elected first black mayor of Parma, Missouri, faced the resignation of five out of six police officers, the city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor shortly after her swearing-in. The officials cited 'safety concerns' in their letters, though Mayor Byrd remains unsure of the reasons behind their departures. The city, with a population of 713, has seen recent increases in crime despite having a comparatively large police force.

Manchester City will make midfielder Yaya Toure available this summer despite his reluctance to leave, as the club considers reshaping its squad. Toure, who has helped City win two Premier League titles and other trophies since 2010, faces interest from clubs like Inter Milan, though his £220,000-a-week salary poses a challenge. Meanwhile, City insists on completing a £24 million deal for striker Alvaro Negredo from Valencia, despite Valencia's hesitation.

A new study claims that over two-thirds of people taking antidepressants do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. Researchers found that 69% of those on antidepressants, particularly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), did not have clinical depression, and 38% did not have other psychiatric disorders like OCD or anxiety. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, suggests that antidepressants are often prescribed without clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller's daughter, Natalie, 28, who suffered from bipolar disorder and psychosis, died by suicide in Baltimore, Maryland, last month. Fuller detailed Natalie's struggles with mental illness, which went undiagnosed until her early 20s, and worsened after her first psychotic episode at 22. Despite periods of stability with medication, Natalie eventually stopped taking her medication, leading to her tragic end.

Koby Hodder, a 10-year-old boy, suffered a cardiac arrest and collapsed in his school playground while playing British Bulldog. His heart stopped for 12 minutes, but teachers administered CPR until paramedics arrived and used a defibrillator to restart his heart. Koby was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as former footballer Fabrice Muamba. The incident has led to calls for the game to be banned due to safety concerns.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, deputy president of the UK Supreme Court, proposed overhauling divorce laws in England and Wales to remove the need for blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. The current system requires citing reasons such as adultery or unreasonable behavior, which critics argue encourages recriminations. Lady Hale also suggested a one-year cooling-off period to resolve issues like child custody and finances before finalizing a divorce, a move supported by campaigners and some legal experts.

Tottenham Hotspur are considering a £400 million stadium with a retractable pitch to accommodate NFL games, aiming to be ready by the 2018-19 season. The design includes a slide-out grass pitch with an NFL synthetic surface underneath and extra-large changing rooms for larger NFL squads. This move could challenge Wembley's current role in hosting NFL games, as the new stadium's design better suits American football requirements.

A group of 13 U.S. senators, including John McCain and Robert Menendez, wrote to FIFA urging the organization to remove Russia as the host of the 2018 World Cup due to its involvement in the Ukraine crisis. The senators argued that hosting the event would bolster Russian President Vladimir Putin's regime and provide economic relief during international sanctions. England, meanwhile, is considering a bid for Euro 2028 but not for the 2026 World Cup, following the FA's decision to avoid bidding under FIFA president Sepp Blatter.

Universal announced on Thursday that the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey," titled "Fifty Shades Darker," will be released on February 10, 2017, with the third film set for February 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, husband of author E.L. James, will write the script for the second film, following the first film's success, which earned $568.8 million worldwide. Sam Taylor-Johnson, who directed the first film, will not return for the sequel, and stars Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are negotiating for higher pay.

Tony Pulis, West Brom manager, faces a challenging season as he returns to Crystal Palace, where he previously saved them from relegation. Despite his expertise in keeping clubs in the Premier League, Pulis has never finished higher than 11th, making him the only manager with over a year's experience who hasn't achieved a top-half finish. West Brom's current position, seven points above the relegation zone, is precarious with tough fixtures ahead, raising concerns about Pulis's ability to avoid relegation this season.

Fenerbahce called for the suspension of the Turkish championship after their team bus was attacked by gunmen following an away match, with the driver sustaining a head wound. The attack occurred on a viaduct near Trabzon as the bus was returning to Istanbul, leaving the bus with shattered windows and blood on the driver's seat and steering wheel. Fenerbahce's general secretary described the attack as "very wrong," emphasizing they came to play football. The Turkish Football Federation condemned the incident.

A massive avalanche struck Everest Base Camp during a Nepalese earthquake, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. The disaster left hundreds of climbers stranded at higher camps due to dangerous conditions in the Khumbu Icefall. Helicopters were used to rescue climbers from Camp 1, with estimates suggesting half the people had been rescued by Monday. The earthquake claimed over 4,300 lives and injured around 8,000.
