Fiorentina, now in sixth place with 49 points, are nine points behind third-placed AS Roma, with the loss leaving them one point ahead of the Europa League qualifying spot. Coach Vincenzo Montella acknowledged his team's poor performance, emphasizing their failure to capitalize on their dominance.

Miley Cyrus caused a stir on social media for not shaving her armpits at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, on Saturday. Fans and users criticized her grooming choice, while others defended her right to choose how to manage her body hair. The incident sparked debates about body hair norms and gender expectations.

Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez of Barcelona reached a milestone of 100 goals scored collectively in all competitions this season after Barcelona's 6-0 victory over Getafe. Messi scored twice, Neymar once, and Suarez twice in the match, bringing their season totals to 49, 32, and 21 goals respectively. This achievement highlights Barcelona's dominance, with the team now five points clear in La Liga.

Andrea McVeigh, 44, was severely injured when a cyclist hit her from behind on a pavement in Bermondsey, south London, on April 14. McVeigh suffered two three-inch gashes on her forehead and other injuries, leaving her scarred and off work. The cyclist fled the scene after initially stopping to lock his bike, chased by McVeigh's husband. The Met Police have issued CCTV footage and appealed for witnesses to help identify the cyclist.

Paul Gregory, 51, from Bedford, was fined £795 for fraudulently obtaining a blue badge by claiming he could only walk 200 metres, despite being an experienced walker and mountaineering club member. The fraud was exposed when council officials read a newspaper article about Gregory's 191-mile hike in Cumbria. At Luton Magistrates' Court, he pleaded guilty and was also ordered to complete 150 hours of unpaid work and undergo 19 'thinking skills' sessions.

Apple has been awarded a patent for a facial recognition system that automatically unlocks a device when a user's face is scanned and matches a stored image. The patent, filed in March 2011, describes a method of capturing an initial image while the device is locked, monitoring its motion, and analyzing images to detect a user's face. Unlike Android's 'Trusted face' feature, which requires the screen to be enabled, Apple's system would unlock based on the phone's movement and position in front of the user's face.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California with her family because she lacked a doctor's note clearing her to fly, despite suffering from multiple myeloma. Sedway posted an emotional video on Facebook showing the incident, which has garnered nearly 10,000 shares. The airline was concerned she might collapse during the eight-hour flight.

On Easter Sunday night, a 1973 E-Type Jaguar and a Toyota Kluger collided head-on at a traffic light intersection on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The Jaguar, valued over $120,000, was completely destroyed, while all three adults involved were taken to the hospital as a precaution. NSW police are investigating the incident, which occurred during Operation Tortoise, a crackdown on reckless driving.

Google has established a four-man team to develop advanced battery technologies for devices like phones, tablets, and electric cars, according to the Wall Street Journal. The team, led by Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj since 2012, focuses on flexible and wearable batteries, including solid-state, thin-film options and subfreezing temperature technologies for Project Loon.

British yacht designer Tony Castro unveiled the 223ft Explorer, a luxurious superyacht for the ultra-wealthy, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and ample space for storing cars, jetskis, and a submarine. The yacht, designed to withstand any weather conditions and capable of circumnavigating the globe, can accommodate 12 guests and 15 crew members. With a construction cost of approximately 40 million euros, the superyacht offers a range of amenities including a cinema, beach club, sauna, and gymnasium.

Ed Miliband announced Labour's plans to impose rent controls despite warnings from experts and opposition from senior Tories, who claim the measures will backfire. The proposals include three-year tenancies and bans on rent increases above inflation during this period, but critics argue these plans contain loopholes that could lead to more evictions and higher rents. Chancellor George Osborne described the plan as "economically illiterate," while the Confederation of British Industry warned it could discourage investment and increase rents in the long term.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter, Ryan Dearnley, was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in their FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after expressing support for Arsenal. The decision followed a video of Ryan wishing Arsenal victory, which angered Reading supporters. The Football Association moved Ryan to an England mascot role instead, offering him two tickets to watch the semi-final in the Arsenal end, which he declined.

Astronomers propose a giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across as the cause of a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, first discovered in 2004. This supervoid, if confirmed, would be the largest single structure ever found and could explain the less dense region of the universe, which contains about 20% less matter and about 10,000 fewer galaxies than other areas. The research, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, was conducted by the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Hawaii at Manoa.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display the chair in which Abraham Lincoln was shot on April 15, marking the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, believed by many to have a blood stain but confirmed by historians to be oil from other visitors, will be showcased in an open plaza after being encased in the museum for 85 years. The event coincides with a lecture by historian Doris Kearns Goodwin on April 13.

Jake Boys, 19, mistakenly booked flights to Dublin instead of Cardiff for his girlfriend Emily-Victoria Canham, 18, to see One Direction's concert. The couple, both popular YouTube vloggers, planned to attend the June 5 show at Cardiff's Millennium Stadium but ended up with tickets to the wrong destination due to Boys' confusion about Cardiff's location.

Romanian company MB Telecom has developed the Roboscan 2M Aeria, the world's first airplane scanner capable of detecting contraband, bombs, and weapons. Costing €3 million, the device uses X-rays to scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial aircraft in about 20 minutes. Currently, the radiation emitted is unsafe for passengers, but the company sees it as a vital tool for enhancing aircraft security, especially at low-security airports.

Stephen Munden, a 54-year-old convicted paedophile, has gone missing after escaping from a psychiatric unit near Hook, Hampshire. Munden, who was detained under the Mental Health Act following his conviction for sexually touching a three-year-old girl, vanished at 6:15 pm on Tuesday. Police have launched a manhunt, releasing images of him with and without a beard, as he may have shaved before leaving.

Middlesbrough holds the lead in the Championship with four weeks left, maintaining a one-point advantage over Bournemouth. Seven points separate eight teams, and Boro's upcoming match against Watford could further solidify their position due to a favorable kickoff time. Watford's Odion Ighalo aims to challenge Middlesbrough's lead, while Bournemouth and Norwich also remain in contention for the top two spots.

Grey hair is trending globally, with many women posting images under the hashtag #grannyhair on social media. The trend gained momentum after Jean Paul Gaultier featured silver-haired models at Paris Fashion Week, and celebrities like Rihanna and Lady Gaga have also experimented with the look. Instagram and Twitter are filled with photos showcasing the grey hair trend, which is seen as a form of feminist statement and a fashion fad.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, a couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning in their home. Less than two months prior, they had created online fundraisers pleading for financial assistance due to living without gas, running water, and facing potential eviction. Their efforts to raise $1,000 were unsuccessful, and they left behind two daughters.

Nick Clegg vowed to remain as Liberal Democrat leader regardless of the party's performance in the upcoming General Election. Friends had suggested he would step down if the party's MPs fell below 30 or if they were left out of power. Clegg expressed optimism about the party's prospects and emphasized the importance of maintaining a centrist position in British politics. He also defended the coalition government formed with the Conservatives, highlighting the economic challenges inherited from the previous Labour administration.

Terry Cooper, a 79-year-old pensioner from Curry Rivel, Somerset, narrowly escaped a badger attack in his garden, thanks to his Jack Russell, Sam. The badger, described as the size of a large pig with six-inch teeth, burst through a hedge with two cubs. Cooper was dragged indoors by his dog, avoiding potential harm. The National Farmers' Union advised residents to secure their properties against badgers, suggesting narrow-spaced fencing and removing accessible food sources.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose 3-0 to Porto U21s in the Premier League International Cup semi-final at Motspur Park on Wednesday, while avoiding the Champions League quarter-final matches. Joined by his son Jose Junior, Mourinho witnessed a Leandro Silva hat-trick secure Porto's victory, despite Fulham's Liam Donnelly being sent off just before half-time.

Property developer Andreas Christopheros, 29, was critically injured when corrosive liquid was thrown at him outside his home in Truro, Cornwall. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, was charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear in court on April 30. Her husband, David Phillips, 48, previously charged with grievous bodily harm with intent, pleaded not guilty and is set for trial on June 8. Christopheros suffered life-changing injuries, including vision loss and facial scars.

Someone in Lastres, a Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route, has posted signs warning visitors not to defecate along the path. The signs, which resemble no-littering warnings, depict a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line. Angry residents have complained about pilgrims defecating outside their homes, while some find the signs amusing and take photos with them. The mayor of Lastres criticized the lack of public facilities for pilgrims along the route.

A fire consumed a building in Flint, Michigan, formerly housing The Body Shop strip club, on Wednesday at about 1pm. Thick smoke and large flames were reported, with only the building and nearby power lines affected. Local resident Terry Rauh mentioned a previous fire at the site. An investigation into the cause of the blaze is ongoing.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, reached a settlement in her lawsuit against the federal government, Frontier Airlines, TSA, and Wayne County Airport Authority for being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport. Hebshi, who was detained and humiliated on the 10th anniversary of 9/11, will receive $40,000 in compensation. The settlement includes amendments to Frontier's employee handbook and customer complaint policy to prevent future discrimination.

Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 from Seoul to Hiroshima crash-landed and skidded off the runway, injuring twenty people among 74 passengers and seven crew members. The plane, an Airbus A320, reportedly missed the landing point, spun 180 degrees, and overran the runway, with local media showing evidence of a hard landing and deployed evacuation slides. Emergency services responded, and the airport was closed.

Made In Chelsea star Mark-Francis Vandelli showcased his collection of 16 expensive watches to the Evening Standard, including a Cartier white gold Moonphase worth £32,000 and a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42 he bought for £6,500. His collection, which he started in his teens, also features a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée no longer made by Cartier and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy, known for roles in "All Creatures Great and Small" and as Winston Churchill, is selling his extensive collection of over 200 antiques, including a diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, at a £100,000 auction. The auction, featuring items like a longbow and a portrait of Hardy holding it, is set to take place this Saturday at Dominic Winter auctioneers in South Cerney, Gloucestershire. Hardy, a military historian and former student of J.R.R. Tolkien, expressed sadness at parting with his collection but entrusted the sale to the auctioneers.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook criticizing a scene on a Rio de Janeiro train platform, which he initially framed as a homophobic rant but was actually a clever spoof to highlight public safety regulations. The image went viral, with over 100,000 shares in 24 hours, as Felippe mocked conservative attitudes by warning against standing on the yellow line, a safety rule broken by a man in the background. Users praised his humorous approach to combating homophobia.

Jonathan Stevenson, now a director at LiveWire Sport, shared a letter from cricket legend Richie Benaud, who responded to Stevenson's 1996 query about left-handed leg spin bowling when he was 16. Benaud's detailed advice, dated September 27, 1996, included tips on various deliveries and was shared as a tribute after Benaud's recent death.

Mark Zuckerberg discussed the future of travel through virtual reality during a Q&A on Facebook, predicting that people will share 3D scenes and virtual environments. Facebook plans to support VR on its newsfeed, allowing users to explore locations using Oculus Rift headsets with multiple camera viewpoints. Michael Abrash, Oculus' Chief Scientist, emphasized VR's potential to create a range of human experiences, while Marriott hotels have already tested VR tours of American hotels.

Guo Kai fulfilled his girlfriend Dong Hui's birthday wish by having wedding photographs taken despite her being bedridden in hospital with bone cancer in Sichuan, China. Family and friends helped Dong put on a wedding dress, and professional photographers captured the moment, with Guo promising to support her through her treatment. The couple, who met a year ago, had planned to marry this month but had to postpone due to Dong's sudden illness.

Blaine Boudreaux, 34, was charged with intoxication manslaughter and other offenses after three DUI collisions in Houston on Sunday, resulting in two deaths, including a 6-year-old boy, and injuries to his mother. Boudreaux also struck and killed a 61-year-old homeless man earlier that day. He was previously arrested at a scene where he failed a field sobriety test and has a history of DUIs in Louisiana.

Microsoft launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond, Washington campus, in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The initiative was announced by Microsoft Corporate VP Mary Ellen Smith, whose son has autism, emphasizing the company's commitment to diversity and inclusion. Smith highlighted the unique advantages individuals with autism can bring to the workforce.

Sheriff Stanley Glanz reassigned two deputies involved in the fatal arrest of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, due to threats against them and their families. The deputies were criticized for pinning Harris' head to the ground as he said he was losing his breath, with police responding with profanity. Sheriff Glanz also apologized to Harris' family and suspended the agency's drug unit pending a review of the shooting. Deputy Robert Bates, charged with second-degree manslaughter, claims the shooting was accidental.

Katie Prager, 24, diagnosed with a lung infection in 2009, urgently needs a transplant to survive, as her insurance, Kentucky Medicaid, refuses to cover out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Her husband Dalton, 23, who has already received new lungs, pleads for help, as Medicaid considers her a financial burden. Katie and Dalton, both suffering from cystic fibrosis, married in 2011 and are now facing the possibility of losing their future together due to healthcare limitations.

Researchers using Sleep Cycle app data found that South Africans wake up earliest on Mondays, while Americans rise at 7am on Tuesdays and are in the worst mood. Slovakia had the best sleep quality, while the UK ranked 45th and the US 49th. Globally, Wednesday nights offered the best sleep quality, with over half of surveyed countries reporting the most restful sleep then.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo's unpublished love letters to Jose Bartoli, written between 1946 and 1949 during her marriage to Diego Rivera, are set to auction for over $120,000 at Doyle New York on April 15. The 25 letters, saved by Bartoli until his death in 1995, reveal Kahlo's passionate affair and personal insights, including drafts of Bartoli's responses and a drawing of a sleeping cat.

Len McCluskey, leader of the trade union Unite, toured South Wales to support Labour, demonstrating his popularity among activists. Despite his genial demeanor, McCluskey and Unite are seen as a powerful, potentially harmful force in British politics, aiming to revive socialist policies from the 1970s. Unite's influence over Labour candidates and its financial and organizational power within the party raise concerns about its radical agenda, including increased public sector expansion and higher taxes.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv filmed animals drinking water from troughs using a GoPro camera for 30 hours. The footage, later edited to four minutes, shows various animals, including a rhino that almost kisses the water and a lemur that delicately licks it, each with unique drinking habits. Some animals were initially cautious about the camera but eventually drank freely. Hershkowitz used protective measures, like acrylic glass, to secure the camera from curious and potentially destructive animals.

A YouGov poll reveals that only 25% of voters believe David Cameron is most eager to win the election, compared to 43% who think Ed Miliband is. Despite criticism of a lackluster campaign, Cameron insisted he was working hard, appearing in casual attire to demonstrate his commitment. Meanwhile, SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon was perceived as enjoying the campaign the most by 34% of voters.

Zaur Dadaev, accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemtsov, told a Moscow court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Dadaev, one of five Chechen men charged, had previously confessed but later retracted his statement. Human rights activist Andrei Babushkin reported seeing signs of torture on Dadaev's body during a jail visit. Nemtsov was shot four times on a bridge near the Kremlin in February, prompting a large protest march in Moscow.

A baby named Sonit Awal was rescued after being trapped for 22 hours under rubble in Nepal following a 7.8-magnitude earthquake on April 25. The earthquake killed over 5,000 people and injured at least twice as many. Sonit's father and Nepalese Army soldiers initially gave up hope but heard his cries and rescued him on Sunday morning. The baby was taken to Bhaktapur Hospital and found to be uninjured.

Narcocon, a Scientology-affiliated drug rehab network, is contesting zoning laws to build a rehab center on Trout Run, a 40-acre property near Camp David in Maryland. They argue the site has historic significance because President Hoover once fished there, aiming to bypass current zoning restrictions. Purchased for $4.85 million in 2013, the center would use saunas and vitamin therapy, costing over $30,000 per month. Opponents view the program as potentially dangerous and question its non-religious claims.

Five former NATO interpreters in Kabul, now unemployed and blacklisted, struggle to survive on the streets, fearing reprisals and isolation. The city, once bustling with foreign presence, now sees deserted neighborhoods and empty shops as the U.S. Embassy and NATO declined to comment on the situation.

A US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured on Friday while swimming in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia. The SEALS were in lap lanes without gear and were found at the bottom of the pool by a fellow service member around 3pm local time. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two, and an investigation is ongoing.

NBC, holding live rights for the Premier League in the USA, expects more Americans to watch each match live than Britons by the next season. In 2012-13, 13 million Americans watched at least one game; last season, this number rose to 32 million. NBC transported its entire production team to England for the first time this weekend, with star anchor Rebecca Lowe covering matches at Turf Moor and Old Trafford.

Boris Johnson and Ed Miliband engaged in a heated exchange on the BBC's Andrew Marr Show, with Johnson accusing Miliband of potentially doing more damage to the country than he did to his brother. The London Mayor claimed that Labour could not govern without SNP support, likening it to being "crouched on his back like a monkey." Despite the tension, Miliband dismissed Johnson's comments, stating, "Come on Boris, you're better than that."

Dustin Irons, a prisoner in Oregon, was sentenced to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court after flashing a judge via video-link during a court hearing. Despite being handcuffed, Irons managed to pull down his pants, leading to his swift removal from the courtroom by sheriffs. The incident occurred as Irons, who was already in prison since December for various charges, expressed dissatisfaction with the ongoing court proceedings.

Jenson Button of McLaren expressed optimism about the team's progress ahead of the Chinese Grand Prix, noting improvements in pace since the Australian Grand Prix. Despite retirements in Malaysia due to failures, Button highlighted that McLaren was competitive with midfield runners like Force India and Sauber. He acknowledged the team still needs to improve but praised the basic car's strength and the progress made with Honda's power unit.

The $2 billion Fiona Stanley Hospital in Perth was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, raising serious hygiene concerns. The hospital previously lost its medical service provider, Serco, after failing to return sterilizing equipment by an arranged date in February. Australian Medical Association WA president Michael Gannon expressed deep concern over the ongoing issues, suggesting the problem has not been adequately resolved. These incidents, including a patient's death last month, have severely damaged the hospital's public image and morale among staff.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, from Nottingham, chose to forgo their dream wedding to afford one last round of IVF, spending £5,500 on two previous attempts. They won a wedding competition after the treatment succeeded, leading to the birth of twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley. The couple, who had initially planned to use their savings for their wedding, celebrated both their marriage and the arrival of their children.

Scooter's Coffee in Omaha had its Facebook page hacked and filled with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link. The hackers controlled the page for nearly 24 hours, starting at 5pm on Sunday, March 29. Similar attacks had previously targeted Delta Air Lines and Crayola. Scooter's Coffee apologized to its customers and stated that the company was unable to regain control until contacting larger businesses to reach Facebook officials.

A young Shibu Inu puppy caused amusement at an American Kennel Club center by attempting to bark at a husky, making high-pitched squeaks and yaps. The video shows the Shibu Inu vocalizing loudly while the husky whines, with onlookers laughing and filming the interaction. The Shibu Inu later runs in its owner's arms, trying to get closer to the husky, before a staff member calms it down with a rub. Canine vocalization typically starts around two to three weeks old and develops into barks by seven to eight weeks, though some puppies take longer.

Liam Plunkett, a 29-year-old England seamer, aims to use his pace to challenge the West Indies in the upcoming Test series. Recovering from a minor ankle injury, Plunkett seeks to make an impact in the Caribbean, where he plans to "rough up" the opposition with his speed. He competes for a starting position with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, with the first Test scheduled for April 13 in Antigua.

Paul Smith, known for his previous challenges against Arthur Abraham, will face Andre Ward in a non-title bout, serving as Ward's warm-up before a potential rematch with Carl Froch. Ward, considered one of the top five pound-for-pound boxers, will fight in Oakland, California, as part of his return to the ring after 17 months. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to unify their titles, but Ward prefers to fight in London rather than Nottingham. Froch is now considering a fight in Las Vegas against Julio Cesar Chavez Jr.

Tyrus Byrd, the newly elected first black mayor of Parma, Missouri, faced the resignation of five out of six police officers, the city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor shortly after her swearing-in. The officials cited 'safety concerns' in their letters, though Mayor Byrd remains unsure of the reasons behind their departures. The city, with a population of 713, has seen recent increases in crime despite having a comparatively large police force.

Manchester City will make midfielder Yaya Toure available this summer despite his desire to stay, due to his high wages. Toure, who has more than two years left on his £220,000-a-week contract, has helped the club win two Premier League titles and other trophies since 2010. Inter Milan, managed by Roberto Mancini, are interested but face salary challenges. City will also proceed with a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo, rejecting Valencia's attempts to pull out.

A new study claims that over two-thirds of people taking antidepressants do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. Researchers found that 69% of those on antidepressants, particularly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), did not have clinical depression, and 38% did not have other psychiatric disorders like OCD or anxiety. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, suggests that antidepressants are often prescribed without clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller's daughter, Natalie, 28, who suffered from bipolar disorder and psychosis, died by suicide in Baltimore, Maryland. Fuller detailed Natalie's worsening condition over years, noting her first psychotic episode at 22 after leaving for college. Despite periods of stability with medication, Natalie eventually stopped taking her meds, leading to her suicide last month.

Koby Hodder, a 10-year-old boy, suffered a cardiac arrest and collapsed in the school playground while playing British Bulldog. His heart stopped for 12 minutes, but teachers performed CPR until paramedics arrived and used a defibrillator to restart his heart. Koby was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as former footballer Fabrice Muamba. Teachers have called for the game to be banned due to safety concerns.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, deputy president of the UK Supreme Court, proposed overhauling divorce laws in England and Wales to remove the need for blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. Currently, divorcing couples must cite reasons like adultery or unreasonable behavior, which critics say encourages recriminations. Lady Hale also suggested a one-year cooling-off period to resolve issues regarding children and finances before finalizing a divorce. Campaigners and lawyers supported the proposal, viewing it as a step towards a more amicable divorce process.

Tottenham are considering building a £400 million stadium with a retractable pitch to host NFL games, potentially sharing the venue with a new NFL London franchise. The stadium, set to be completed by the 2018-19 season, would feature a slide-out grass pitch and an NFL-style synthetic surface underneath, along with extra-large changing rooms. NFL officials are reportedly close to establishing a permanent franchise in London, with plans to test logistics during upcoming games at Wembley.

A group of 13 U.S. senators, including John McCain and Robert Menendez, wrote to FIFA urging the organization to remove Russia as host of the 2018 World Cup due to its involvement in the Ukraine crisis. The senators argued that hosting the event would bolster Russian President Vladimir Putin's regime and provide economic relief during international sanctions. England, meanwhile, is considering a bid for Euro 2028 but not for the 2026 World Cup, as the FA chairman Greg Dyke revealed.

Universal announced that the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey," titled "Fifty Shades Darker," will be released on February 10, 2017, with the third film set for February 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, EL James's husband, will write the script for the second film. The first film, released over Valentine's Day weekend, earned $568.8 million worldwide. Sam Taylor-Johnson, who directed the first film, is not returning for the sequel, and stars Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are negotiating for higher pay.

Tony Pulis, West Brom manager, faces a challenging relegation battle despite a hero's welcome at Crystal Palace, where he previously saved them from relegation. With only seven points above the bottom three, West Brom's upcoming fixtures against top teams leave little room for error. Pulis, known for keeping clubs in the Premier League, has never finished higher than 11th, a record that highlights his inability to secure top-half finishes despite his managerial expertise.

Fenerbahce called for the suspension of the Turkish championship after their team bus was attacked by gunmen, injuring the driver. The attack occurred on Saturday night as the bus was returning to Istanbul from a match in Trabzon. Fenerbahce's official statement emphasized the need to find and punish the attackers, describing the incident as "very wrong" since they were there to play sport.

A massive avalanche struck Everest Base Camp during a Nepalese earthquake, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. The earthquake, which claimed over 4,300 lives and injured 8,000, left hundreds of climbers stranded above 20,000 feet due to dangerous conditions in the Khumbu Icefall. Helicopters began rescuing climbers from higher camps on Monday.

Gregory Margolin, an 87-year-old Jewish veteran of World War II, survived a missile strike in Eastern Ukraine, where he lived with his family. The attack, which destroyed his house on February 10, killed his daughter Ira, prompting his family to move to Israel on March 24. Margolin, who had previously fought in the Soviet Red Army, now suffers from Alzheimer's disease. The International Fellowship of Christians and Jews has helped relocate 600 Jews from Ukraine to Israel since December.

John Carver, Newcastle's current caretaker manager, faces a crucial Tyne-Wear derby against Sunderland, aware that the outcome could significantly impact his chances of securing a permanent position. Carver recalls Ruud Gullit's controversial decision to bench key players in 1999, leading to a 2-1 defeat and Gullit's subsequent dismissal. Carver emphasizes the importance of a positive result for his case, noting that a victory, even by a narrow margin, would be a significant boost.

Reverend Al Sharpton appeared in North Charleston to address the fatal shooting of Walter Scott by a police officer and advocate for policing reform. He spoke at Charity Missionary Baptist Church, where local officials and police chiefs were present. Sharpton emphasized the need for change in policing practices and praised Mayor Keith Summey for dismissing the officer involved. He was also set to attend a vigil near the shooting site.

Brendan Rodgers will address Raheem Sterling about his off-field behavior following controversies involving nitrous oxide and a shisha pipe. Sterling scored Liverpool's first goal in a 2-0 victory over Newcastle United but faces internal investigation and potential disciplinary action. Rodgers praised Sterling's performance but noted his player's disappointment over not scoring more goals.

Labour received over £1.1 million in donations between April 6 and April 12, more than twice as much as the Conservatives, who received £492,512. Union barons contributed over £700,000 to Labour, with Unison and Unite donating significant amounts. The Liberal Democrats and UKIP received £50,000 and £8,000, respectively.

Police were called twice to a Qatar Airways flight at Birmingham airport after passengers became disruptive following a five-hour delay on the tarmac. The plane had been diverted from Manchester due to severe winds, and passengers were eventually allowed to disembark and were transported to Manchester, with some arriving as late as 7am. A Qatar Airways spokeswoman apologized, citing safety concerns and the need for a new flight crew.

Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring before his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao in Las Vegas on Saturday. The pop star, a close friend of Mayweather, has accompanied him into the ring on multiple occasions, including a press conference ahead of the May 2 fight. Bieber confirmed his participation in a video, shouting "hell yeah" when asked by reporters.

Corinthian Colleges Inc., once enrolling over 70,000 students, announced it would close all 28 of its remaining campuses. This move follows the U.S. Department of Education's curtailment of its access to federal student aid last summer. For-profit colleges, which enroll 13% of students but account for nearly half of all student loan defaults, face increasing scrutiny and calls for reform due to their high default rates and aggressive recruitment tactics.

Pep Guardiola denied a dispute with former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after "being blamed" for the defeat by Porto. Guardiola, disappointed by the Champions League loss, clarified that the doctor's departure was not due to a feud but rather his own decision, emphasizing that injuries are part of football. Muller-Wohlfahrt, who had worked at Bayern for nearly 40 years, cited a damaged "bond of trust" in his resignation.

Wladimir Klitschko reminisced about his Olympic gold win in 1996 and his rise to become heavyweight champion in 2000, ahead of his world title defense against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden. Klitschko, 39, emphasized the transformative power of sports and his belief that age is an advantage, citing his successful training camp with younger sparring partners.

Jeremy Clarkson admitted he would miss fronting Top Gear after being fired in March for attacking a producer. Clarkson, 54, expressed gratitude to supporters and said he would miss the show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, 70, expressed interest in returning to Top Gear if invited, emphasizing the show's need to evolve.

Celta Vigo's Fabian Orellana was sent off with a straight red card for throwing a chunk of grass at Barcelona's Sergio Busquets during a La Liga match. The incident occurred as Busquets attempted to waste time, leading to Orellana's dismissal after the grass hit Busquets in the neck. Barcelona secured a 1-0 victory, with Jeremy Mathieu scoring the only goal in the 73rd minute.

Federal Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors in the Dzhokhar Tsarnaev trial to avoid the Boston Marathon and related events, stressing the importance of avoiding prejudicial influences during the sentencing phase, which begins April 21. Tsarnaev was convicted on all 30 counts, including use of weapons of mass destruction and conspiracy, following a trial where prosecutors called 92 witnesses and the defense four. The sentencing phase could last up to four weeks.

Over 1.3 billion Chinese people celebrated the Qingming Festival, a three-day holiday marking the start of spring, by honouring ancestors and participating in outdoor festivities. In Shaanxi Province, a grand ceremony was held for the 'Yellow Emperor' Huangdi, with 34 drum strikes representing China's provinces. The festival, which falls in the first week of April, includes rituals like tomb sweeping and offerings to ensure ancestors' well-being in the afterlife.

Paul Simon, 73, returned to the UK album chart's top spot after 25 years with "The Ultimate Collection," surpassing younger artists like Ed Sheeran. The album includes 19 tracks from his career, including hits from his time with Simon & Garfunkel and solo work. His recent tour with Sting is believed to have contributed to the album's success, marking his first number one since 1990's "The Rhythm of the Saints."

Iker Casillas declared he will stay and fight for his position at Real Madrid despite rumors of David de Gea's potential arrival. Casillas, 33, expressed his commitment to fulfill his contract and help Real Madrid defend their Champions League title, which they have reached the semi-finals of, after defeating Atletico Madrid.

Britain reached its highest employment level in history, surpassing 31 million in the three months to February, with a year-on-year increase of 557,000. The International Monetary Fund praised Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy, commending the reduction of the fiscal deficit and the creation of two million more jobs since 2010. IMF chief Christine Lagarde and German finance minister Wolfgang Schaeuble endorsed Osborne's plans, highlighting the UK's economic success.

SsangYong, known as 'two dragons' in Korean, launched the Tivoli SUV priced from under £13,000, aiming to compete with the Nissan Juke. Available in the UK this summer, the Tivoli offers three trim levels, seven airbags, and a five-year unlimited mileage warranty, with options for front-wheel drive or 'intelligent' 4x4. SsangYong's UK sales and marketing director expects the Tivoli to double the company's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 units.

Sam Longhurst, head chef of Splendid Kitchen in Manchester, created a 10in-tall burger called "The Whole Damn Farm" containing six forms of three different meats, weighing half a kilogram and priced at £13.50. The burger includes two beef patties, a whole fried chicken thigh, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers, totaling 2,000 calories.

Yeo Valley's headquarters in North Somerset features a staff canteen offering gourmet meals prepared by a Michelin-starred chef for as little as £2. The menu, which changes daily, includes organic and locally sourced ingredients, such as vegetables from a nearby community farm and meat from Yeo Valley's own Holt Farm. The canteen, now open to the public at higher prices, has been hailed as the world's best staff canteen.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration caused by his Type II diabetes but was discharged and back home resting by Tuesday, according to his publicist. King thanked those who expressed concern and mentioned he was enjoying time with his grandchildren. No further details about his hospitalization were provided.

On Easter Sunday, Fifth Avenue in Manhattan hosted an annual parade featuring extravagant hats and headgear. Participants, including those from various religious and non-religious backgrounds, wore items like ships, flowers, and political dioramas. Local hatmaker Mary Ann Smith showcased a blue-sailed ship hat, symbolizing "sailing to new heights." The parade, which began in the 1880s, now includes diverse and creative headpieces.

East of England ambulance service detailed bizarre call-outs, including one where two ambulances were dispatched for a 'run-over person' in Epping Forest, only to find a run-over squirrel. The service reported handling 1,248 inappropriate calls in the last two years, with front-line crews attending nearly half, believing them to be genuine emergencies. Calls ranged from a man reporting a bleeding burger to someone feeling lethargic after dieting. Regional Head of Emergency Operations Centres Gary Morgan urged callers to use common sense, warning that prank calls could jeopardize life-saving responses.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake participated in Audi's football challenge, competing against Loic Remy and Willian. In the first two rounds, Hazard and Ake won with scores of 5-3 and 6-0, respectively. However, Remy and Willian secured a surprising victory in the final challenge, where they won by shooting footballs from long range into the top of a convertible Audi, despite Willian accidentally smashing the wing mirror.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, suggesting Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to his own decision. Rodgers made these comments after Liverpool's 4-1 loss to Arsenal, which ended their Champions League hopes. Sterling had rejected a £100,000-a-week contract extension and admitted to being flattered by Arsenal's interest in him. Rodgers emphasized that Liverpool is the best place for Sterling's development and financial interests.

Rachel Riley was embarrassed on a recent episode of Countdown when contestants suggested the word 'erection' in a word game, with host Nick Hewer struggling to hide his laughter. Dr Phil Hammond helped by providing the word 'recondite'. This incident follows previous instances where contestants proposed rude words, such as 'todgers' and 'm*nges', causing similar reactions from the hosts.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, was arrested for attempting to buy deadly poison on the dark web, which he claimed was for suicide. Covert counter-terrorism officers tracked his online activities starting in January, leading to his arrest on February 16. He pleaded guilty and was sentenced to a 12-month referral order at Manchester Youth Court.

Lianne Hindle, 37, died three hours after giving birth to her daughter at North Manchester General Hospital in December. Her death followed a series of tragedies at the same hospital and the Royal Oldham Hospital, where three babies and one mother died in the previous eight months, prompting an investigation. Hindle's partner, Chris Barnes, is calling for action to prevent further deaths, citing concerns about the care she received post-delivery.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after being filmed training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, was congratulated by the official Australian Olympic team's Twitter. Emily was born at 3.1 kilograms, and Pittman plans to compete in the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, having continued training until the final trimester.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during the Dauphin Island regatta in Mobile Bay, Alabama, resulting in at least one death and the search for four missing people. Over 100 sailboats and up to 200 participants were involved in the 57th iteration of the race. The storm struck around 4 p.m., and the Coast Guard continued searching into the night.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma in an interview with The Daily Beast. Her vision is deteriorating, and while doctors haven't provided a timeline, Barr uses marijuana to relieve glaucoma symptoms. Ophthalmologist Steven A. Shanbom noted that the combination of these diseases is particularly severe, as macular degeneration affects central vision while glaucoma impacts peripheral vision.

A Stephens County jury convicted 17-year-old Chancey Allen Luna of first-degree murder for the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane in Duncan, Oklahoma. The jury recommended life in prison without parole for Luna, who was in a car that fired at Lane while he was jogging. Defense attorneys argued Luna intended only to scare Lane, not kill him. Luna apologized to reporters after the verdict.

Arsene Wenger stated that his poor record against Jose Mourinho will not affect Arsenal's match against Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium. Wenger has drawn five and lost seven of his 12 games against Mourinho. Despite their frosty relationship, Wenger emphasized that the game's outcome will depend on performance, not past encounters. Arsenal, currently 10 points behind Chelsea, aim to capitalize on their recent good form.

Manny Pacquiao, a former poverty-stricken boxer from the Philippines, has become a global sports icon through a series of high-profile fights, including an upcoming match against Floyd Mayweather at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao's rise began in 1995 when he won his first 10 professional bouts, and he later achieved international recognition after defeating Lehlo Ledwaba in 2001. The fight against Mayweather is expected to generate $300 million and marks a significant milestone in Pacquiao's career.

Jack Grealish, a standout player for Aston Villa in their FA Cup semi-final win over Liverpool, was photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, joining other top-flight stars in this controversial behavior. Despite his exceptional performance, experts warn that such actions could jeopardize his career, emphasizing the importance of maintaining discipline and making the right choices to secure a successful future in professional football.

Sam Barton, known as "Britain's vainest man" for his £55,000 cosmetic surgery to resemble Joey Essex, was attacked by a group who threw eggs at him on Easter Monday in Sutton Coldfield. Barton believes the attackers tracked him down through his Facebook posts. He had previously gone bankrupt due to his lavish lifestyle and plastic surgery expenses.

Manchester University in Indiana was placed under lockdown late Friday night following a 'likely prank call' about an armed individual near the administration building. Police responded to a report of a stabbing and threats to detonate explosives. Students were advised to shelter in place, and authorities, including a bomb squad, investigated before determining it was probably a prank. No injuries were confirmed, and the lockdown continued into the early hours of Saturday.

Edinson Cavani faces a crucial match against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals, aiming to lead Paris Saint-Germain to the semi-finals. PSG are without key players Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Verratti due to suspensions. Cavani, known as El Matador, must perform well to overcome Barcelona's formidable attack, as he has struggled with a goal drought and recent disciplinary issues.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title with a unanimous points decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool. Mathews secured the 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 victory after Abril and Barroso withdrew due to illness and visa issues, respectively. Despite Luis's aggressive style, Mathews controlled the fight with his jab and uppercuts, though both fighters were penalized in the eighth round.

Hull secured a surprising 28-20 victory over St Helens at Langtree Park, ending St Helens' third consecutive defeat. Jamie Shaul's long-distance try sealed the win for Hull, who capitalized on St Helens' fatigue and injuries. Despite St Helons' efforts, including tries from Tommy Makinson and Louie McCarthy-Scarsbrook, Hull maintained their lead, with Leon Pryce scoring a crucial second-half try.

The U.S. immigrant population, both documented and undocumented, could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, according to U.S. Census figures. By 2060, immigrants could account for 82% of all population growth, with one in five U.S. residents being an immigrant. This growth has sparked debate over immigration policies, including President Obama's plans to expand DACA and DAPA policies.

Jack Wilshere captained Arsenal Under 21s in his return from injury but could not prevent a 1-0 defeat by Reading's Under 21s at the Emirates Stadium. Niall Keown, son of former Arsenal defender Martin Keown, scored the winning goal for Reading with a header in the opening minutes. Other Arsenal first team players like Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby also participated in their comeback matches.

Justin Rose, struggling with poor form and a drop in world rankings, showed signs of recovery at the Shell Houston Open, hitting 17 out of 18 greens and scoring a 69. Rose attributed his decline to technical issues and has since returned to his old putter, aiming to improve before the Masters.

A newly-built mansion on the site of a former milking parlour in Mayfair, London, is on the market for £25 million. Originally used for dairy farming in the 18th and 19th centuries, the property was demolished in the 19th century and rebuilt in 2011. The 8,139 square foot house features modern luxuries such as an indoor swimming pool, gym, cinema room, and a 14-piece dining table.

Bayern Munich, despite significant injuries to key players like Arjen Robben and Franck Ribery, expressed confidence ahead of their Champions League quarter-final first leg against Porto. Thomas Muller highlighted the team's unity and recent performances, including a 3-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt, suggesting the squad is stronger for their recent challenges. Coach Pep Guardiola acknowledged Porto's quality and emphasized the need for two strong games to advance.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited Mercedes' Brackley base after losing to Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel at the Malaysian Grand Prix on March 29. The duo aimed to strategize a winning formula for the upcoming race in Shanghai from April 10-12. Mercedes motorsport boss Toto Wolff acknowledged Ferrari's superior performance, noting Vettel's victory was well-deserved due to better tire management in high temperatures.

Oklahoma Gov. Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing executions by nitrogen gas if lethal injection becomes unavailable or unconstitutional. The method causes quick unconsciousness and death from oxygen deprivation, according to the governor's office. Rep. Mike Christian said it would ensure a humane, quick, and painless death. The bill's passage comes as Oklahoma's executions are on hold due to a Supreme Court review of lethal injection methods.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice, including an overhead kick, leading Swansea to a 3-1 win over Hull and topping the EA Sports Performance Index with a score of 52.9. Charlie Austin of Queens Park Rangers and Chelsea's Eden Hazard followed in second and third places with scores of 52.2 and 51.7, respectively, after impressive performances in their matches.

A Russian freezer trawler, the Dalny Vostok, sank off the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 of its 132 crew members. The ship, carrying an international crew, tipped over after pulling in an 80-ton fishing net and sank in 15 minutes without sending distress signals. Over 1,300 people are involved in the rescue operation, with 63 crew members rescued and 13 still missing.

Clinical trials led by researchers at the Institute of Cancer Research and the Royal Marsden hospital show that olaparib, a drug originally for women, can delay the progression of advanced prostate cancer in men with DNA defects. The London trial found that 16 out of 49 men responded positively to the drug, which extended the time patients lived without the disease worsening. Olaparib, owned by AstraZeneca, is the first cancer drug targeting inherited genetic mutations and works by blocking cancer cells' ability to repair damage.

Rhiannon Taylor, a 29-year-old Australian travel photographer, turned her passion for travel and photography into a business called 'In Bed With', reviewing luxurious accommodations worldwide. With over 12,000 Instagram followers, she documents the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service, generating income from reviews and selling professional pictures to hotels and travel product companies.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was killed in a fight between two adult males in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, eastern South Africa. The calf was thrown into the air and dragged along the water's surface before dying hours later. Stacey Farrell, a tour operator, witnessed the incident and noted the mother's attempts to protect her calf were ineffective against the aggressive adults.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea following an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was hit by a cigarette lighter thrown from QPR supporters at Loftus Road during Chelsea's 1-0 victory. QPR, unlikely to face disciplinary action, are reviewing CCTV footage to identify the culprit and have promised to ban those involved indefinitely. The club has appealed to witnesses to come forward to help identify the perpetrators.

LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect, who was later found dead, had a six-month-old baby with him. Police confirmed the suspect knew the victims but did not disclose how the suspect died. A GoFundMe page set up by the family for funeral services has already exceeded its initial $5,000 goal.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, faced criticism for opposing the right-to-buy policy for housing association tenants while owning a property from such an association. Thornberry and her husband bought the property at auction eight years ago, now valued at nearly £1 million. Conservatives accused her of hypocrisy, highlighting her opposition to the policy despite benefiting from it. Housing association leaders were also criticized for their stance on the policy.

Wiltshire Police dropped an investigation into a vicious assault on huntsman Mike Lane, who was beaten by protesters, despite substantial evidence. Lane, 40, was attacked with iron bars and suffered concussion and broken teeth. The attack occurred during a hunt with artificial scent, not a fox, and was captured on video. Hunt supporters, including Lane, criticized the police for insufficient effort in pursuing the case.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes stated he has no intention of leaving the club this summer, despite links to Manchester United and Chelsea. Gomes, 21, expressed his happiness at Valencia and his desire to continue playing in La Liga. He scored four goals in 25 La Liga appearances since joining from Benfica last summer, contributing to Valencia's fourth-place finish. Gomes denied any contact from Chelsea, asserting that neither he nor his agent are aware of any opportunities from the Premier League club.

Audrey Pekin, a 19-year-old Australian, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali by Henry Alafu, whom she had met at a bar. Alafu first attacked her at his remote home and then in a taxi as she tried to escape. Despite CCTV footage and witness reports, Alafu fled back to Nigeria, evading arrest.

Ashley James, a former Made In Chelsea star, teamed up with PETA for an anti-fur campaign targeting Harvey Nichols after the store reversed its anti-fur policy. The campaign features James holding a fake skinned fox and the slogan "Harvey Nichols: Here's the Rest of Your Fur Coat." Harvey Nichols defended its decision, stating it sources products from reputable brands with assurances about responsible fur sourcing.

Chile's President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law recognizing civil unions between same-sex couples, set to take effect in six months. The law aims to grant legal recognition to cohabiting relationships and will benefit an estimated 2 million people, providing them with rights in health care, property, pensions, and inheritance. This move aligns Chile with several South American countries that have allowed same-sex civil unions but contrasts with the limited legal recognition of same-sex marriage in the region, which is only legal in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.

Chelsea are on track to break the Premier League record for most days at the top of the table in a single season, currently leading for 230 days as of April 10. Jose Mourinho's team, who have been in first place since August 30, can surpass Manchester United's 1993/94 record of 262 days if they maintain their position until the end of the season. Chelsea currently hold a seven-point lead in the league.

Cape Verde, an Atlantic island nation with a population of 500,000, is leveraging its rich musical heritage to boost its economy, which lacks conventional natural resources. Prime Minister Jose Maria Neves and the Ministry of Culture, led by musician Mario Lucio de Sousa, recognize music's potential. The Kriol Jazz Festival, now in its seventh year, attracts international artists and highlights Cape Verde's diverse musical styles, including batuque and morna, aiming to draw global attention and economic benefits.

A hoax video of a surfer in front of Sydney's Opera House went viral for the second time, reposted by Sydney radio hosts Fitzy and Wippa. The video, originally uploaded in 2012, resurfaced after recent heavy storms in Sydney. Experts, including swell forecaster Ben Macartney, confirmed the video's impossibility due to the city's harbor geography.

Reading lost to Birmingham 1-0 in a Sky Bet Championship match at the Madejski Stadium, despite dominating play. Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal for Birmingham seven minutes from the end, securing his 16th goal of the season. The match followed Reading's recent 2-1 defeat against Arsenal in the FA Cup semi-finals.

Paris Saint-Germain's David Luiz will miss the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained during a match against Marseille. Scans revealed Luiz will be out for at least four weeks, adding to PSG's concerns as they fight for the Ligue One title, currently leading by one point over Lyon.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to over 100,000 illegal downloads per day, with more than seven million episodes from seasons one to four downloaded between February and April. Brazil was the top country for illegal downloads, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO responded by launching HBO Now to curb piracy and recapture revenue, though it is only available in the US.

Leicester City faces West Ham United in a Premier League match at King Power Stadium, with Leicester missing Matt Upson due to an Achilles injury and Jeff Schlupp potentially rested. West Ham welcomes Winston Reid back from injury but lacks Enner Valencia and Andy Carroll. Leicester has won only one of their last ten home matches, while West Ham is unbeaten in their last seven against Leicester.

In Celoron, N.Y., a statue of Lucile Ball unveiled in 2009 has drawn criticism for its unflattering depiction, leading to a Facebook page with over 600 likes calling for its removal. The statue, based on Ball's intoxicated pitch for a health tonic from "I Love Lucy," is considered a poor likeness by many residents and fans. Artist Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has declined to comment. Recasting the statue would cost an estimated $8,000 to $10,000.

Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, lost nearly half her body weight after standing for an 11-hour flight due to concerns about crushing her seatmate. Starting at over 20st, she now weighs 9st 9lb and credits her weight loss to joining Weight Watchers and taking up running. Her journey began in December 2012 when she realized her weight affected others during a business trip to Hong Kong.

Nicola Bonn, 34, from London, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences raising her 14-month-old daughter Poppy. One of her posts, "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves," went viral after she expressed frustration with constant unsolicited advice from others. Bonn highlighted how new mothers often feel pressured to justify their decisions and face judgment from those offering opinions.

Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, two 17-year-old boys from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are feared to have traveled to Syria after reportedly heading to Turkey on March 31. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested in 2006 for his involvement in a plot to murder non-Muslims. The families are in shock and have appealed for information to help bring the boys back safely.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was murdered just days before her wedding. Her body was found in bushland after she went missing on Easter Sunday. Her father, Robert, expressed the family's deep grief, noting the tragedy of her life being cut short when she had much to look forward to. The venue for her wedding was decorated with yellow balloons and flowers as a tribute to her, with 120 guests invited.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman aims to strengthen his squad by signing Feyenoord's 20-year-old midfielder Tonny Vilhena this summer. Vilhena, who has one year left on his contract, is open to moving to the Premier League. Additionally, Koeman is interested in securing the permanent transfer of winger Eljero Elia from Werder Bremen and exploring a move for teammate Jordy Clasie, valued at £10 million.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture from 1820 with beanbags in the library at Ickworth House in Suffolk as part of an experiment to engage visitors, but the move angered heritage experts. Similar experiments are planned at nine other National Trust venues. Art historian Bendor Grosvenor criticized the approach as patronizing and suggested better methods to attract new audiences. The National Trust defended the experiment as short-term and aimed at enhancing visitor experience.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was seen standing on the side of a Sydney road as his driver changed a flat tyre near the Sydney Conservatorium of Music. Felicity Waterford, waiting for her daughter's concert to finish, offered assistance and later took a selfie with Mr. Howard. The incident occurred after their car developed a flat tyre on the Cahill Expressway.

Tony Pulis acknowledged that Joey Barton 'probably had a point' when criticizing West Bromwich Albion's players for losing their composure after being 2-0 up against Queens Park Rangers in December. Barton's comments followed a match where Charlie Austin scored a hat-trick, leading QPR to a 3-2 comeback victory. Pulis, now in charge of West Brom, noted the team's recent improvement in both performance and results.

Primatologists in Ntokou-Pikounda National Park, Democratic Republic of Congo, captured the first photograph of the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought extinct since the 1970s. The discovery, made by Lieven Devreese and Gaël Elie Gnondo Gobolo, shows a mother with her young and highlights the species' vulnerability to commercial bushmeat hunters.

Kim Kardashian, Kanye West, and their daughter North visited Armenia's capital, Yerevan, for eight days, exploring landmarks including the Yerevan Opera House. The visit, which began on Wednesday, was their first to the country where Kim's father, Robert Kardashian, was born. They stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, accompanied by bodyguards and police.

Patrick and Valerie Jubb, British expats in Jimena de la Frontera, Spain, are facing a legal battle with the town hall over illegal additions made by a previous owner to their four-bedroom property. The couple, who bought the bed and breakfast La Vina de Linan in 2008, now cannot sell the property due to the town hall's ruling that the first floor, kitchen, and pool were illegally built in 1994. The Jubbs claim they obtained a certificate stating there were no infractions when they purchased the estate.

Apple's latest quarterly report showed sales of over 61 million iPhones, accounting for more than two-thirds of its $58 billion revenue and the majority of its $13.6 billion profit, marking a 40% increase from the previous year. Despite this success, iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer revenue rose 2% to $5.6 billion. Apple CEO Tim Cook expressed satisfaction with the results, highlighting the strong performance of iPhones and the positive customer response to the new Apple Watch.

Natali Castellanos-Tyler, 30, died in a car crash in Virginia on February 21, with police ruling it a one-car accident due to poor road conditions. However, her 3-year-old daughter, Elisa, has been having nightmares about a white van, leading her father to suspect a hit-and-run. This follows several recent reports in the area of similar incidents involving a white box truck.

Researchers at New York University found that the brain can enhance the recall of neutral events by associating them with emotions later on. This process involves emotional stimuli affecting brain regions like the amygdala, striatum, and hippocampus, which are crucial for memory encoding and consolidation. The study highlighted how subsequent emotional experiences can strengthen initially mundane memories, such as how the September 11 attacks influenced memory retention.

Jackson Byrnes, an 18-year-old from northern NSW, was diagnosed with a stage four brain tumour and has raised over $80,000 for life-saving surgery by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo. His girlfriend, Jahnae Jackson, has put her studies on hold to care for him, as he is now paralysed and unable to dress himself. The community's generosity has overwhelmed them, especially from their small town of Casino.

Hull City is interested in signing QPR centre-back Nedum Onuoha, who has 15 months left on his contract. Onuoha played in QPR's recent 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion. Additionally, Hull is also considering West Brom striker Victor Anichebe for a potential summer transfer. Everton, West Ham, and Stoke are also interested in Onuoha.

Researchers at Yale University have created an interactive map showcasing unique phrases used in different U.S. states, revealing regional grammatical variations. For example, Idaho residents might say "All of my clothes needs washed," while Floridians use "I ain't never had no trouble with none of 'em." The map also includes some data from the UK, highlighting regional linguistic differences in both countries.

Kalman Kallai traveled from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia, a 2,796-mile journey, in a rocking chair attached to a trailer. Along the way, he posed in various scenic locations, interacted with his father, and shared the experience on video, highlighting his unique adventure across Canada.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood humorously responded to a letter from six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who had applied for the Villa manager position after Paul Lambert's sacking. Sherwood revealed a Twix multi-pack during a press conference, referencing Pye's request for sweets and chocolate as a win bonus. The manager joked about narrowly beating Pye for the job, thanking him for the gift meant as a win bonus for his time at Tottenham.

World boxing champion Kell Brook received a hero's ovation at the Premier League Darts in Sheffield on Thursday. Dave Chisnall won both of his matches, defeating Gary Anderson 7-3 and James Wade 7-1, to move to 17 points in second place in the table. Michael van Gerwen maintained his lead with an 7-5 victory over Stephen Bunting, while Phil Taylor suffered his fourth defeat in five matches against Raymond van Barneveld.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti praised teammate Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his significant off-field contributions, highlighting his role in helping young players and boosting team morale. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 Ligue 1 goals this season, was suspended for the first leg of PSG's Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona, where Barcelona won 3-1. He will be available for the second leg at the Nou Camp.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published sensitive details about RAF's main base on the Falklands Islands, including GPS coordinates and runway specifications, on their website. This information could have been used by Argentina to plan an attack, as it provides crucial intelligence for any potential military operation. The Aerodrome Manual, which was accessible to the public, includes data that could aid in targeting the runway, potentially crippling Britain's defense capabilities. The MoD acknowledged the error but downplayed the sensitivity of the leaked information.

Huddersfield coach Paul Anderson aims to improve his team's offensive performance to match their strong defensive record as they face Catalans Dragons. The Giants have dropped from third to ninth in Super League after losing three consecutive games. Anderson acknowledges the team's defensive strength but emphasizes the need for better offensive play, noting that small improvements could have turned recent losses into wins.

Planners in Windsor approved the opening of a second Costa cafe less than 500 yards from an existing one, with a Costa Express in between. The new Costa will replace a former HSBC branch, while the other opened earlier this year. Resident Samantha Taylor criticized the decision, citing an oversaturation of coffee shops, while Matt Gordon-Smith saw it as a positive sign for local trade. Planners noted no legal grounds to refuse the application.

The British Veterinary Association withdrew support for the shooting of free-running badgers in pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, advocating instead for trapping and then shooting them. The BVA concluded that the first two years of culling had not proven the effectiveness and humanity of 'controlled shooting'. Environment Secretary Liz Truss pledged to expand culls across the country if the Conservatives win the election, despite criticism from wildlife groups.

Geoff Barrow, founder of Portishead, criticized streaming services for low royalty payments, stating he earned only £1,700 from 34 million plays. Barrow, who runs Invada Records, argued that streaming hurts young artists' ability to establish themselves and called for better compensation. Artists like Taylor Swift and Thom Yorke have pulled their music from services like Spotify in protest, while Jay-Z launched Tidal, promising higher returns for musicians.

Game of Thrones fans illegally leaked the first four episodes of the show's fifth season online before its official premiere. The episodes, which began appearing on torrent sites on Saturday night, are believed to have originated from press review copies. As of early Sunday morning, they had been downloaded over 550,000 times. HBO stated they are investigating how the breach occurred.

Daniel Buccheri, a 25-year-old Melbourne singer, composed an emotional song for his brother Adrian's wedding on March 29 at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, leaving guests in tears. The song, performed on keyboard, paid tribute to his brother and new sister-in-law Sarah, blending personal anecdotes with popular music tunes. The unique speech has since garnered over 100,000 views online.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, revealed her fitness routine after giving birth to Mia, including daily morning exercise bike sessions before her daughter wakes up. Phillips, who is vying for a place on Team GB for the Rio Olympics, noted the difficulty in regaining her fitness post-pregnancy and adheres to a strict diet and exercise regimen. She hopes to qualify for the eventing team in Rio and anticipates Mia will grow up around horses, as her mother did.

Raheem Sterling's interview about not signing a new contract with Liverpool angered many fans. Blogger David Tyrer noted the interview was ill-timed and negatively impacted Sterling's public image. Fans feel ungratefulness towards Sterling for potentially holding the club to ransom, despite Liverpool nurturing his career. Liverpool is preparing to face Arsenal, with Sterling linked to a move to the London club.

Former Barcelona players and staff from the 1996 Spanish Super Cup team are now prominent managers across Europe. Luis Enrique, Pep Guardiola, Laurent Blanc, and Julen Lopetegui, among others, are coaching teams in the Champions League. The group includes current managers of Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain, Porto, and previously managed Valencia and Cordoba.

Eric Cantona declared Javier Pastore, Paris Saint-Germain forward, the best player in the world, praising his creativity over Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Cantona, known for his provocative statements, made the claim at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai, emphasizing Pastore's ability to surprise with his playmaking skills despite the Argentine's lower goal and assist count compared to Messi and Ronaldo.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murdering Michael Spalding, 39, after hacking his body into pieces and dumping the remains in a Birmingham canal. Simon attacked Spalding with a hacksaw and placed the body parts in suitcases, which he and his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, threw into the canal. Police recovered the suitcases and used advanced 3D scanning technology to link the hacksaw to the lacerations on the bones. Simon was convicted after a 15-hour jury deliberation at Birmingham Crown Court.

Essex and Gloucestershire County Councils have implemented 'loneliness maps' to identify areas where residents, especially the elderly, are at high risk of social isolation. Health experts warn that loneliness can be as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day, leading to health issues like dementia and high blood pressure. The maps, based on public health statistics and resident surveys, help councils target interventions in 'danger zones' of loneliness. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends this approach for other councils to address the problem nationally.

Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary as a waitress at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City. She started working there at 15, trained by her mother who had been employed for 13 years. Eddingfield, who met her first husband at the restaurant, says it's the only job she's ever wanted.

Mike Gatting, former England captain, believes Kevin Pietersen should not automatically return to the England team despite scoring runs for Surrey, citing the need for current players to perform well. Pietersen scored 170 in his first game but only 19 against Glamorgan. Gatting also noted that England's captain Alastair Cook faces scrutiny if he fails to score runs in the ongoing series against West Indies.

Caleb Benn, a 17-year-old Californian high school student, developed an iOS app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos directly from their computers, earning him $1,000 a day. However, an Instagram engineer accused the app of violating the company's terms of service and demanded Benn fix it by Monday, to which Benn refused, stating the app would be pointless if altered.

South Korean companies frequently hold hoesik, dinner gatherings with co-workers that often involve heavy drinking, to foster relationships and understand colleagues better. Foreign business travelers face intense pressure to participate, with drinking etiquette being a crucial aspect. Charles Lee, a Korean-Canadian, learned to appreciate the cultural significance of drinking after initial reluctance. The drinking culture affects Seoul's traffic patterns, with Mondays and Wednesdays being peak nights for hoesik.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was spotted leaving Aberdeen Royal Infirmary with a walking stick after being treated for a dislocated hip sustained during an Easter trip to Balmoral estate. He was admitted to the hospital on Easter Monday and discharged the following day. Buckingham Palace confirmed the successful treatment and noted that the Duke, who previously suffered a mild stroke in 2013, continues to undertake royal engagements despite his age.

The Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of bikini-clad women managing parking meters, may end due to local business leaders' calls for change. Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president Peter Yared argued the group is outdated and violates anti-touting laws by selling merchandise. However, Surfers Paradise Meter Maids general manager Michael Yarwood defended the tradition, stating it remains integral to the tourist experience.

Greece denied it would default on a £330 million loan to the International Monetary Fund, scheduled for April 9, despite reports suggesting it might prioritize paying domestic bills. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas confirmed Greece's intention to make the payment on time, while sources close to the Syriza party indicated the government might choose to pay wages and pensions over loans if funds were insufficient. Greece has not received bailout funds since August and has resorted to borrowing from state entities.

Turkey blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after they refused to remove images of prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz, who was killed during an armed siege. The 46-year-old prosecutor died in hospital after being taken hostage by the DHKP-C, a group considered terrorist by Turkey, the EU, and the US. The court imposed the blocks because the images 'deeply upset' Kiraz's wife and children.

Seven-year-old Colin Gilpatric, an aspiring Jedi Knight, wrote to George Lucas asking if Jedi could marry without turning to the dark side. Lucasfilm responded with a letter affirming that true Jedi values include friendship, compassion, and loyalty, making marriage possible for Jedi who remain selfless. Colin received a package containing Star Wars merchandise and the reassuring letter, signed "Your friends at Lucasfilm."

Wisconsin ended Kentucky's undefeated season with a 71-64 victory in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, securing their place in the final. Frank Kaminsky led Wisconsin with 20 points and 11 rebounds. Meanwhile, Duke advanced to the final by defeating Michigan State 81-61, setting up a clash with Wisconsin at the Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis.

Mötley Crüe's Vince Neil faced criticism for his rendition of the American national anthem before a Las Vegas game, highlighting the high stakes of performing the song. Neil's performance was notably poor, drawing comparisons to past controversial renditions by Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton, each remembered for their unique interpretations of the anthem.

Barry Lyttle, from Belfast, appeared in Downing Centre Local Court for a sentence hearing after punching his brother Patrick, putting him in a coma. Security footage showed the altercation outside Hugo's Lounge in Sydney, where Barry's punch caused Patrick to fall and hit his head on the pavement. Prosecutor Alex Poulos called for a full-time jail term, while Patrick, who nearly lost his life, urged for the charges to be dropped. Magistrate Graeme Curran indicated a jail sentence was likely.

The parents of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, found their daughters' gravesite at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney stripped of all mementos.
