Family members had built a small memorial with flowers, statues, and toys over 11 months, but cemetery staff cleared the site without notice, leaving the items in nearby bins. The parents managed to retrieve about 25 percent of the memorabilia.

Lord Neuberger, President of the Supreme Court, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear full-face veils in court to show respect for different customs. This recommendation came after a 2003 trial where Rebekah Dawson was sentenced to six months in prison for refusing to testify without her veil, and a recent European Court of Human Rights decision upholding a French ban on the niqab. Lord Neuberger emphasized the need for judges to be sensitive to cultural differences and to minimize subconscious bias.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Bonne Terre, Missouri, for killing Anthony Curtis in 1998 during a dispute over child support. The U.S. Supreme Court rejected several appeals, including one arguing Cole's mental illness. Cole was the third inmate executed in Missouri this year, with the governor emphasizing the impact on crime victims.

Prince Harry departed the UK for Australia without meeting his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge was overdue for the birth. Harry, who will be fifth in the line of succession after the new arrival, had hoped to meet the baby before his return in mid-May. The royal baby was expected by Saturday, with the Duchess previously stating the due date as mid to late April.

Justin Jackson, a Florida man, has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, executives from her TV network, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager to trick people into providing him with jobs, clothes, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson's eight-year fraud trail included convincing a New York jeweler to lend him $2.4 million worth of items by pretending to be Madonna's manager, which he later sold. He also sent forged letters on Oprah's network stationery to hotel groups recommending himself for jobs.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini set a €50 million (£36m) price tag on Paulo Dybala, telling Paris Saint-Germain they must pay this amount to sign him. Dybala, compared to Lionel Messi by Zamparini, is sought after by several top European clubs including Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and PSG. Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini watched Dybala play in a recent match, indicating his interest.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians protested across the country, calling for President Dilma Rousseff's impeachment due to an economic downturn and a massive bribery scandal at Petrobras. Rousseff, who was once the chairwoman of Petrobras, denies involvement in the scheme and claims she had no prior knowledge. Her approval rating has dropped to 13%, with the economy expected to contract and inflation high. Protests have grown larger as the Petrobras scandal and economic issues persist, with both supporters and opponents organizing rallies.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona denied starring in a porn film, calling You and the Night a 'piece of art' at the Laureus Sports Awards in Shanghai. The film features Cantona in racy scenes, including one where he is on his hands and knees in just his underwear. Cantona defended the film, stating it is beautiful and only appears pornographic because of the audience's perception, emphasizing it is a work of art by a special director.

Psychologists found that certain types of music can enhance the flavors of food and drink. At the Ultraviolent restaurant in Shanghai, fish and chips are served with Beatles music, while El Celler de Can Roca in Spain pairs scented meringue with commentary on Lionel Messi. Professor Charles Spence from Oxford University explained that music can draw attention to specific tastes in food and wine, enhancing the dining experience by up to 15 percent.

Gordon Taylor, chief of the Professional Footballers' Association, defended Raheem Sterling for postponing contract talks with Liverpool until the summer. Sterling, valued at £100,000-a-week, has not signed a new deal despite Liverpool's offer, leading to speculation about his future. Taylor argued that Sterling's actions are not disloyal and that focusing on football rather than negotiations could benefit both player and club.

La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, 38, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same company and lived six minutes away after Ohio released birth records for people born between 1964 and 1996. Mitchell-Clark found Simmons on Facebook, and they connected, revealing Mitchell-Clark had three younger biological sisters. Simmons, who gave birth at 15, expressed shock and relief at the reunion.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a gun trafficker, pleaded guilty to weapons charges related to Aaron Hernandez's murder case. He admitted to sending Aaron Hernandez an assault rifle and two handguns in April 2013, a month before Hernandez killed Odin Lloyd. Oscar Hernandez, now facing up to 30 months in prison, stated he was 'awed' by Aaron Hernandez's fame and 'grateful to be noticed.' His sentencing is delayed until May 5.

Joel Parker, 33, was arrested for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head in St Johns County, Florida, after threatening and disrupting the driver. The incident occurred when Parker, about to exit the Sunshine Bus, offered the driver a Snickers bar, which was declined, leading to the assault. The driver was unharmed but reported the incident to the police. Parker posted $250 bond and received a trespass warning, banning him from using the bus again.

Tony Pulis discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will likely stay at West Bromwich Albion beyond the summer despite interest from other clubs. Berahino, who expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is set to join England's under-21 squad in the Czech Republic until late June. Pulis praised Berahino's improved attitude and commitment, suggesting the club is content with his presence.

Giovanni Lo Porto, an Italian aid worker, was abducted in Pakistan in January 2012 along with colleague Bernd Muehlenbeck. Two years later, Lo Porto was killed by a U.S. drone strike in Afghanistan, alongside American Warren Weinstein, during a counterterrorism operation that also killed al Qaeda leader Ahmed Farouq. Lo Porto, who studied Peace and Conflict Studies at London Metropolitan University, worked with Welthungerlife on clean water and sanitation projects in Pakistan.

Photographer John Massung captured hundreds of sharks swarming just 100 feet from the beach off Sebastian Inlet, Florida, last Thursday. Fellow photographers confirmed the sighting further out at sea. Experts identified the sharks as likely Blacktip or Spinner species, which migrate annually to breed. The photos were shared over 2,000 times on Facebook.

Zeus, an 11-year-old retired K-9 officer from the Ridgefield Police Department, received a farewell procession in Connecticut on Wednesday. Due to a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health, Zeus was honored by fellow officers and residents before being euthanized. The German Shepherd, who served for eight years, assisted in over 250 narcotics arrests and helped track down 50 missing or wanted individuals.

Reports of child sex abuse in the UK surged by over 60% since Operation Yewtree in 2011, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014. South Yorkshire saw a 577% increase in cases over five years, but arrests fell by 9%, prompting criticism of the government's response. Shadow Home Secretary Yvette Cooper called the ratio of reported crimes to arrests a 'national scandal.'

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters due to its stunning landscapes. Thingvellir National Park served as the North of Westeros in Game of Thrones, while Svinafellsjokull glacier in Skaftafell National Park was used in Interstellar. The Dettifoss waterfall, Europe's most powerful, was featured in Prometheus. Iceland's unique scenery attracts directors like Christopher Nolan and Ridley Scott, who praise its natural beauty and diverse filming locations.

A blue and yellow bathing box in Melbourne sold for a record $276,000, $150,000 over its original asking price, at an auction. In Sydney, a 1917-built fire station turned mechanic’s garage in Paddington sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. Additionally, an 1850s maximum security prison in Victoria, now a renovated home, is on the market for $2 million.

Samantha Rawcliffe, 40, from Morecambe, lost control of her car due to unexplained shaking and was later diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND). Following the May 26 accident, she experienced bladder control issues and was hospitalized. Diagnosed in September, Rawcliffe now relies on a mobility scooter, takes 32 daily medications, and has given up her job as a teaching assistant. FND, an umbrella term for unexplained neurological symptoms, severely impacts her quality of life.

Sculptor Dave Poulin admitted disappointment in a controversial Lucille Ball statue in Celoron, New York, and offered to replace it for free. The statue, nicknamed 'Scary Lucy,' sparked a social media campaign with over 600 likes calling for its removal due to its unflattering depiction. Poulin, who took full responsibility for the poor decision to cast it in bronze, estimated the cost of a new statue at $8,000 to $10,000.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba will be sidelined for around seven weeks due to a torn knee ligament sustained during Austria's match against Bosnia. The 22-year-old, who was previously out for three months earlier this season, expressed disappointment but aimed to return for the season finale. Alaba's absence is a blow to Bayern, who are leading the Bundesliga and competing in the Champions League and German Cup.

Beatrice Nokes, 21, and Daniel Williams, 37, appeared in court facing charges of running a prostitution ring in Central London. Nokes, a University College London student, is accused of inciting three young women into prostitution, while Williams, a suspended Met police officer, faces seven additional charges including voyeurism and hiding cash in his chimney. Both are the children of respected legal professionals and are on bail pending further hearings.

A firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data, Sequester, is offering details of eating disorder sufferers and other health conditions for 12p a head. The Mail revealed that Sequester, a business partner of Alchemy Direct Media, claims to have information on 43 health conditions and personal financial details. This prompted investigations by the Information Commissioner’s Office, the Direct Marketing Commission, and the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U.

Jordan Spieth, at 21, equaled Tiger Woods' 1997 record to win the Masters at Augusta with an 18-under-par score, becoming the second-youngest champion. After his victory, Spieth spoke about his autistic sister Ellie, expressing how she shapes his perspective on life's priorities. He mentioned missing her and looking forward to sharing his green jacket with her.

Dick Advocaat, Sunderland's new manager, emphasizes the importance of the Wear-Tyne Derby against Newcastle, unlike his previous downplay of the Old Firm derby in 1998, which led to a 5-1 loss for Rangers against Celtic. Advocaat, aiming for three points to boost Sunderland's position above the relegation zone, considers starting Adam Johnson despite his recent arrest on suspicion of sexual activity with a minor.

Belinda Bartholomew, girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, claims she was racially abused at Sam the Butcher in Bondi when trying to buy a chicken. She alleges the butcher called her names and told her to go to an "Aussie butcher." The butcher denies the claims, stating Bartholomew was rude and he was dealing with eftpos machine issues.

Cadbury has reduced the size of its Freddo Frog chocolates by 20%, from 15g to 12g, while keeping the recommended retail price unchanged. The company cited rising manufacturing costs as the reason for the change. This move follows a previous reduction in the size of Cadbury's family blocks of Dairy Milk from 220 grams to 200 grams. Customers expressed disappointment and anger over the price without corresponding size increase on Cadbury's social media platforms.

Hillary Clinton's campaign met in Brooklyn ahead of her official presidential announcement, where campaign manager Robby Mook distributed a "values statement" outlining the campaign's goals and strategies. The document emphasizes humility, discipline, and unity, aiming to avoid past mistakes from Clinton's 2008 run. Clinton plans to launch her candidacy through a social media video on Sunday and will soon visit key early voting states.

Kyli Wilfson, 29, suffered from chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition affecting less than .01% of people, which left her unable to eat for 18 months. Initially misdiagnosed with a mild pancreatic issue, she endured excruciating pain and rapid weight loss, dropping to 80lbs from her usual 110lbs. Diagnosed after a camera was inserted into her pancreas, she now relies on a feeding tube, while her fiancé Dustin Wood feels guilty eating in front of her.

The leaders' debate featured memes of UK political figures, including Labour's Ed Miliband superimposed over London rapper Plan B, challenging David Cameron to a one-on-one debate. Prime Minister David Cameron and Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg were depicted on the Gogglebox sofa, while Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon appeared with a skeptical expression. Memes also included references to films and TV shows, such as Gogglebox and The Riot Club, highlighting the absence of Cameron and Clegg in direct confrontations.

Amir Khan could face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi after waiting for a fight with Floyd Mayweather. Bob Arum, Pacquiao's promoter, is considering an offer for a November or December event in Abu Dhabi. Khan, known for his speed, sees this as a dream fight and a huge attraction in the Muslim world.

A two-bedroom home in Islington, north London, only 5ft wide in places, sold for £750,000. The property, described as 'well proportioned' by the estate agency, features a narrow 'galley kitchen' and a garden. It was previously sold for half the price in 2001. The buyer will pay £27,000 in stamp duty.

Nicola Sturgeon launched an SNP manifesto aimed at forming a power-sharing deal with Labour, proposing policies like reducing English university tuition fees and rolling back NHS competition. The manifesto includes £180 billion in spending increases over five years and calls for recognising Palestine as a state, among other measures. Polls suggest the SNP could win up to 50 seats, potentially holding the balance of power at Westminster.

Rangers keeper Robby McCrorie's errors led to Celtic winning the Glasgow Cup for the fourth time in eight seasons at Hampden. Josh Kerr scored after McCrorie missed a corner, and McCrorie later dropped a Mark Hill free kick into his own net. The match, played behind closed doors due to previous fan trouble, saw Celtic dominate play and secure a 2-0 victory.

Tony Pulis led West Bromwich Albion to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, maintaining his trademark gritty playing style. James Morrison and Craig Gardner scored for West Brom, while Pulis remained in his cap and track suit throughout the match. The win ended West Brom's run of 10 away games without a victory and secured them 36 points, nearly guaranteeing their Premier League safety.

Jameela Jamil spent £3,000 to remove and replace her ten amalgam fillings with white fillings, believing they caused health issues including chronic fatigue and facial swelling. Blood tests revealed high mercury levels, which were attributed to the dental work despite dentists arguing that mercury exposure from amalgam fillings is minimal and generally safe.

Suge Knight laughed in court on Thursday as he expressed hope that his friend Floyd Mayweather would bail him out after winning his upcoming fight. Knight, refused a bail reduction from $10 million, faces trial for murder and attempted murder. His attorney, Matthew Fletcher, believes Mayweather will bail Knight out following his fight on Saturday. Knight, 48, has been suffering from medical issues since his January charges.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine revealed in Puss Puss magazine that her British shorthair cat, Kimchi, enjoys human food like poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. The cat, known for its discerning palate, also loves cheese, caviar, and fishy foods, leading Erskine to put Kimchi on a diet. Erskine also mentioned her new cat, Ponzu, who showed a taste for leftover green curry.

Martin Springall, 38, photographed his daughter in Zushi, Japan, in July 2014, and later noticed a pair of black boots behind her that he could not explain. Springall, living in Tokyo at the time, said he had no one else with them and the photo was untouched. The image sparked debate on Reddit about whether it was a trick of the light or a paranormal occurrence.

The Conservative Party plans to require foreign workers to pay £22,000 in taxes before accessing UK benefits, as part of a manifesto to curb EU migration. Unemployed EU migrants will face a four-year ban on state support and potential deportation if they do not secure employment within six months. The plan also includes restrictions on exporting child benefits to other EU countries and aims to limit the appeal of migration from poorer EU regions.

Cody Neatis, an eight-year-old with multiple disabilities, was left to sleep on a hospital floor for seven nights at Royal Preston Hospital due to a lack of a suitable bed. Cody, who has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, and autism, requires a high-sided cot for safety. His mother, Lynne Neatis, has slept alongside him, fearing he might injure himself or pull out his oxygen. Lynne claims she has been waiting two years for a special needs bed for Cody.

Rory McIlroy, the world's top-ranked golfer, practiced at Augusta ahead of the Masters tournament, where he aims to complete his career grand slam. Ian Poulter forgot his golf clubs in his rental car due to excitement, and Henrik Stenson, recovering from flu, is among the injured players hoping to perform well. Tiger Woods will play in the traditional par-three tournament with his children, Charlie and Sam. Gene Sarazen's albatross shot in 1935 remains a historic highlight, and players attempt to replicate Martin Kaymer's 2012 feat of skipping a ball onto the 16th green and into the hole.

Juventus have ruled out signing Manchester United's loan striker Radamel Falcao due to his high wages. Falcao, who has scored only four goals since joining United, is expected to leave the club this summer. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta stated that Falcao's wages are beyond their means. Instead, Juventus are interested in Palermo's Paulo Dybala and PSG's Edinson Cavani to reinforce their forward line.

David Cameron pledged to sell £4 billion of Lloyds Bank shares to the public if re-elected, offering individuals up to £10,000 worth of shares at a discount. This would be the largest privatisation since the 1980s, aimed at reducing the national debt and encouraging public ownership of shares, with a loyalty bonus for long-term holding.

Scientists warn that living near congested roads with high air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' and increase dementia risk. A study involving over 900 people aged 60 and older found that exposure to PM2.5, tiny particles from traffic and industrial emissions, was linked to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes. These strokes, without outward symptoms, can lead to brain damage and other health issues. The research, published in Stroke, suggests air pollution affects brain structure even in dementia and stroke-free individuals.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness advocate, died in February after a seven-year battle with epithelioid sarcoma. Her fiancé, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she underwent radiation treatment in her final weeks, integrating it with her natural healing regime. Despite the treatment's success in shrinking her tumor, complications arose, leading to her death. Pamenter wrote an emotional tribute to Ainscough, praising her courage and grace.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale, Queensland. Three vehicles collided on Wednesday afternoon, resulting in four patients being airlifted to hospitals with injuries ranging from chest pain to arm injuries. Six others with minor injuries or for further assessment were taken to Ipswich Hospital. The highway was closed for several hours with diversions in place.

Jason McDonald, 34, from Aurora, Colorado, walked a slackline over a pool containing more than 50 alligators at the Colorado Gator Farm. McDonald, who volunteers at the farm and has been handling alligators for over ten years, said the reptiles were surprisingly unbothered by the slackline. He plans to walk over the farm's largest and albino alligators in future stunts.

Abdul Hadi Arwani, a Syrian imam and opponent of President Bashar Al-Assad, was shot dead in his car in North West London. Sources suggest he may have met his killer days before the murder when the man, posing as a potential client, asked Arwani to return for a building quote. Scotland Yard's counter-terrorism unit is investigating, considering the possibility of a politically motivated assassination. Arwani, 48, died of multiple gunshot wounds near Wembley.

In Hong Kong, a small bakery in Tsim Sha Tsui sells Jenny's butter cookies, with long lines of tourists and locals willing to pay $9 per tin. The popularity has led to counterfeit products and scalping, with some hired to queue and resell cookies at a 70% markup. Similar food crazes, like cronuts and ramen burgers, have occurred globally but often fade quickly.

Kira Hollis, diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and clinical underweight due to anorexia and depression, turned her life around through bodybuilding. Ordered by doctors to gain weight, she became a personal trainer and now weighs 9.5st, up from 6st. Her recovery was also supported by her daughter Olivia and medication. Hollis's journey went viral after she uploaded a video online, reaching over two million views.

Eighteen-year-old jockey Lewis Ferguson survived a dramatic double somersault fall from his horse Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton, an incident that garnered hundreds of thousands of views online. Despite the fall, Ferguson returned to work at Paul Nicholls’ stable the next day, showing only a cut on his nose. He expressed no intention of letting the incident deter him from his racing career, aiming to compete in prestigious events like the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree.

Hillary Clinton launched an unconventional campaign to rebrand and reframe her image, using a video, new logo, and a road trip. Critics dismissed her video as vapid and boring, but marketing experts argue that her approach may have made her appear more confident and forward-looking. The campaign aims to shift her image from self-absorbed to empathetic, similar to Apple's rebranding under Steve Jobs. Clinton's stops in Iowa, like an unscripted visit to Chipotle, were intended to connect with everyday Americans.

More than 1,700 Chinese students from Yichuan Senior High School in Shaanxi province took an exam in their school's playground on Saturday due to insufficient indoor space. The freshmen organized the outdoor exam themselves, turning their desks and chairs collectively as directed by regular radio announcements to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school viewed this as a test of the students' organizing capacity and a way to encourage relaxation and prevent cheating.

Sportsmail and Gillette are offering a competition for one lucky reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The prize also includes a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shave gel. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a one-year-old orangutan rejected by his natural and first surrogate mothers, found a loving home with Maggie, a 53-year-old orangutan at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie, who had previously raised four of her own children and another surrogate, has successfully bonded with Kecil over the past ten months. Zookeepers were relieved when Kecil sought comfort from Maggie during a fire alarm, indicating a strong bond. Kecil will make his first public appearance this weekend.

Noelle Baynham, 61, from Winchester, Hampshire, was found dead in her home by a friend after her body was partially eaten by her two dogs, a Jack Russell and a Staffordshire Bull Terrier, which were trapped inside for days. The dogs, initially thought to have tried to wake her, consumed parts of her vital organs, making it impossible for the pathologist to determine the exact cause of death, believed to be an accidental drug overdose.

France's top handball player Nikola Karabatic will face trial for fraud related to illegal betting. Along with his brother Luka and 15 others, Nikola was banned by the French league two years ago for betting on a match where Montpellier, already champions, lost to a weaker team. Karabatic's lawyer aims for a not-guilty verdict, as the player denies placing bets on the match. The trial is expected to commence within months.

Six men were jailed for a total of 31 years for sexually abusing teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The offences, including rape and inciting sexual activity with a child, occurred at parties organized on social media and at the defendants' homes. Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, received the longest sentence of nine years for his role in luring victims. Judge Zoe Smith criticized the men for exploiting vulnerable girls, rejecting the defense's argument that the victims were motivated by a desire to be seen as victims rather than "slags." Thames Valley Police's Operation Reportage led to the convictions.

Aaron Hernandez, convicted of murder in Odin Lloyd's death, faces three more trials: a murder trial for the 2012 shooting deaths of Daniel de Abreu and Safiro Furtado, and two civil suits. The civil suits, filed by the victims' families and Alexander Bradley, who claims Hernandez shot him in Miami, have led to a freeze on Hernandez's $5 million assets, including a disputed $3.3 million signing bonus from the New England Patriots.

Emirates Airline is set to sign a £30 million three-year deal with the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. The Dubai-based airline already has significant sponsorship deals, including a £150 million agreement with Arsenal that includes stadium naming rights and a £80 million deal with AC Milan until the 2019-20 season.

Michael Phelps announced his intention to compete in a fifth Olympics in Rio next year but will not swim in the world championships in Russia this summer as part of his punishment for a second drunken driving arrest. The 18-time Olympic champion, who served a six-month suspension, expressed regret for his actions and emphasized his commitment to recovery, having completed inpatient alcohol rehabilitation and enrolling in Alcoholics Anonymous.

Gareth Bale is a significant doubt for Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. Bale lasted only a few minutes before limping off during Real's 3-1 victory over Malaga. Real Madrid's statement revealed a muscular lesion in Bale's left leg, with his condition to be evaluated. Additionally, Luka Modric is expected to be out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain.

Scientists at Texas Tech University warned that over 50% of pensioners sold their investments during the 2007-2008 financial crisis after a 30% stock market decline, leading those who sold at the lowest point to have only £63,000 today from an initial £100,000, compared to £141,000 if they had held on. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, found that retirees with better cognitive abilities were less likely to make emotional investment mistakes.

Stuart Pearce believes Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to improve the team's performance. City's recent poor form, including a defeat by Manchester United, has put their title challenge in jeopardy and they now face a struggle to secure a top-four finish. Pearce attributes City's decline partly to the reduced effectiveness of Yaya Toure and suggests the squad needs significant strengthening in the upcoming summer transfer window.

Manchester United's players, including Wayne Rooney and Robin van Persie, trained on Friday ahead of their Premier League match against Manchester City on Sunday. United, currently ahead of City in the league table for the first time since the Sir Alex Ferguson era, aim to extend their lead to four points with a victory. The derby is crucial for both teams as they vie for a Champions League position, with City having won their last three visits to Old Trafford.

Fiorentina's Champions League hopes diminished as they lost 1-0 to Verona at home, conceding a late goal by Verona substitute Mounir Obbadi. Fiorentina's Alessandro Diamanti missed a crucial penalty in the second half, leading to their defeat and leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma. The loss left Fiorentina in sixth place with 49 points from 31 games.

Miley Cyrus sparked controversy at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, for not shaving her armpits, which was noticed in a social media snap. Fans and users on social media debated the issue, with some criticizing her grooming choice and others defending her right to choose how to manage her body hair.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez scored a combined 102 goals this season after Barcelona's 6-0 victory over Getafe. Messi contributed 49 goals, Neymar 32, and Suarez 21, with all but nine of their goals coming from inside the box. This achievement extends Barcelona's lead to five points in La Liga.

Andrea McVeigh, 44, was severely injured when a cyclist hit her from behind on a pavement in Bermondsey, south London, on April 14. McVeigh suffered two three-inch gashes on her forehead and other injuries, leaving her scarred and off work. The cyclist fled the scene after initially stopping to lock his bike. Met Police have issued CCTV footage and appealed for witnesses to help identify the suspect.

Paul Gregory, 51, from Bedford, was fined £795 for fraudulently obtaining a blue badge by claiming he could only walk 200 metres, despite being an experienced walker and mountaineering club member. The fraud was exposed when council officials read a newspaper report about Gregory's 191-mile hike in Cumbria. At Luton Magistrates' Court, he pleaded guilty and was also ordered to complete 150 hours of unpaid work and undergo 'thinking skills' sessions.

Apple has been awarded a patent for a facial recognition system that automatically unlocks a device when a user's face is scanned by the front-facing camera. Filed in March 2011, the patent describes a method of capturing an initial image while the device is locked, monitoring its motion state, and analyzing images to detect a user's face for unlocking. Unlike Android's 'Trusted face' feature, which requires the screen to be enabled, Apple's system would track the phone's movement to determine if it is in use, potentially unlocking without the need to press the power button.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, and her family were removed from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note clearing her to fly due to her cancer. Sedway, who has multiple myeloma, posted an emotional video on Facebook showing their removal from the plane. The airline was concerned she might collapse during the eight-hour flight.

On Easter Sunday night, a 1973 E-Type Jaguar and a Toyota Kluger collided head-on at a traffic light intersection on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The crash, which occurred during the Easter long weekend, resulted in the complete write-off of the classic Jaguar valued over $120,000, with all three occupants taken to hospital as a precaution. NSW police are investigating the circumstances of the collision.

Google has established a four-man team to develop advanced battery technologies for devices like phones, tablets, and electric cars. The team, led by Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj since 2012, focuses on flexible and wearable batteries, including solid-state thin-film options. Google also collaborates with AllCell Technologies to create batteries for subfreezing temperatures, crucial for its Project Loon internet-providing balloons.

British yacht designer Tony Castro created the 223ft Explorer, a luxury superyacht for the ultra-rich, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and storage for cars, jetskis, and a submarine. The yacht can accommodate 12 guests and 15 crew members, offering amenities like a cinema, sauna, and gym. With a construction cost of approximately 40 million euros, the superyacht is designed to withstand any weather and circumnavigate the globe.

Ed Miliband announced Labour's plans to cap rents despite warnings from experts and business leaders that the measures could backfire. The proposals include three-year tenancies and bans on rent increases above inflation during this period. Critics, including the Generation Rent campaign group, argue the plan has loopholes that could lead to more evictions and higher rents. Chancellor George Osborne called the plan "economically illiterate," while the Confederation of British Industry warned it could discourage investment and increase rents.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter, Ryan Dearnley, was removed from his role as Reading's mascot in their FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after expressing support for Arsenal. The decision followed a video of Ryan wishing Arsenal victory, which angered Reading fans. The Football Association moved Ryan to an England mascot role instead, offering him two tickets to watch the match in the Arsenal end, which he declined.

Astronomers propose a giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across as the cause of a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, first discovered in 2004. The supervoid, if confirmed, would be the largest single structure ever found and could explain the less dense region of the universe, containing about 20% less matter and 10,000 fewer galaxies than other areas. The research, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, was conducted by the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Hawaii at Manoa.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display the chair in which Abraham Lincoln was shot on April 15, marking the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, believed by many to have a blood stain but confirmed by historians to be oil from other visitors, will be showcased in an open plaza after being encased in the museum for 85 years. Two days prior, historian Doris Kearns Goodwin will deliver a lecture about Lincoln.

Jake Boys, 19, mistakenly booked flights to Dublin instead of Cardiff for his girlfriend Emily-Victoria Canham, 18, to see One Direction's concert. The couple, popular YouTube vloggers, planned to attend the show in Cardiff but the error was only discovered when Canham realized the tickets were for Ireland. Boys, an Arsenal supporter, is now arranging train tickets to Wales for the June concert.

Romanian company MB Telecom has developed the Roboscan 2M Aeria, the world's first mobile X-ray scanner for airplanes, capable of detecting contraband, bombs, and weapons. Costing €3 million, the device can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial aircraft in about 20 minutes. However, the radiation emitted is not yet safe for passengers, and some areas of the plane, like the fuselage and wings, are currently restricted under regulations.

Stephen Munden, a 54-year-old convicted paedophile, went missing from a psychiatric unit near Hook, Hampshire, on Tuesday. Described as having a 'fanatical obsession' with young girls, Munden was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl on a bus. Police believe he may have shaved his beard before leaving and have released images of him with and without facial hair.

Middlesbrough, led by Aitor Karanka, holds the top spot in the Championship with seven points over second-placed Bournemouth, as the promotion race remains tight with six matches left. Watford, aiming for promotion, faces Middlesbrough on Monday, while Bournemouth plays Birmingham. The volatile season has seen the division's leadership change 15 times, with Middlesbrough's advantage including a lunchtime kick-off that could psychologically impact rivals.

Grey hair is trending globally, with many women posting images on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. Instagram and content sharing sites like Bored Panda have seen an influx of posts featuring silver locks, with some pages receiving over half a million views. The trend, inspired by fashion shows like Jean Paul Gaultier's, is seen as a feminist statement and a move away from costly hair dyeing.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, a couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning this week. In late February, they had created online fundraisers pleading for financial help due to living without gas, running water, and facing potential electricity cutoffs. Their efforts to raise $1,000 were unsuccessful, and they left behind two daughters. Police Chief Brandon Standley noted the town's available resources for such situations, expressing tragedy over their decision.

Nick Clegg vowed to remain as Liberal Democrat leader regardless of the party's performance in the upcoming election. Friends had suggested he would step down if the party's MPs fell below 30 or if they were left out of power. Clegg expressed optimism about the party's prospects and emphasized the importance of maintaining a centrist position in British politics. He also defended the coalition government formed with the Conservatives, highlighting the economic progress made despite criticism from the Labour Party.

Terry Cooper, 79, was saved by his Jack Russell, Sam, from a large badger with six-inch teeth in his Curry Rivel, Somerset garden. The badger, accompanied by two cubs, burst through a hedge, prompting Sam to pull Cooper indoors. Cooper, left shaken, covered the hedge gap with metal and compost. The National Farmers' Union advised residents to use badger-proof fencing and secure food sources to prevent future invasions.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose 3-0 to Porto U21s in the Premier League International Cup semi-final at Motspur Park on Wednesday, accompanied by his son Jose Junior. Mourinho chose this match over the Champions League quarter-final second leg clashes, which saw Real Madrid defeat Atletico Madrid 1-0 and Juventus overcome Monaco. Fulham's Liam Donnelly was sent off just before half-time, potentially altering the match's outcome.

Property developer Andreas Christopheros, 29, was critically injured when corrosive liquid was thrown in his face outside his home in Truro, Cornwall. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, was charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear in court on April 30. Her husband, David Phillips, 48, previously charged with grievous bodily harm with intent, pleaded not guilty and is set for trial on June 8. Christopheros suffered life-changing injuries, including loss of vision and facial scars.

Someone in Lastres, a Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route, has posted signs warning visitors not to defecate on the trail. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line, have become an attraction for pilgrims who pose for photos with them. Angry residents have complained about pilgrims defecating outside their homes, while the mayor noted the lack of public facilities for pilgrims along the 500-mile route to Santiago de Compostela.

A massive fire consumed a former strip club building in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday at about 1pm. The site, previously home to The Body Shop, was not vacant at the time of the fire. Thick smoke and large flames were reported, with only the building and nearby power lines affected. Local resident Terry Rauh mentioned a previous fire at the same location. An investigation into the cause of the blaze is ongoing.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, reached a settlement in her lawsuit against the federal government for being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport on the 10th anniversary of 9/11. Hebshi will receive $40,000 in compensation for the humiliation she faced after being removed from a Frontier Airlines flight and held for hours. The settlement also includes amendments to Frontier's employee handbook and customer complaint policy to address discrimination.

Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 crash-landed and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring twenty people. The Airbus A320, carrying 74 passengers and seven crew members, reportedly missed the landing point and overran the runway, spinning 180 degrees. Emergency services responded, and the airport was closed following the incident.

Made In Chelsea star Mark-Francis Vandelli showcased his collection of 16 expensive watches to the Evening Standard, including a Cartier white gold Moonphase worth £32,000 and a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42 he bought for £6,500. Vandelli, who buys a new watch annually, also owns a rare Cartier Tortue Collection Privée no longer in production.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy, known for roles in "All Creatures Great and Small" and as Winston Churchill, is selling his extensive collection of over 200 antiques, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, at a £100,000 auction. The auction, featuring items like a longbow and a portrait of Hardy holding it, will take place this Saturday at Dominic Winter auctioneers in Gloucestershire. Hardy, a military historian and Tolkien's former student, expressed sadness at parting with his collection but entrusted the sale to the auctioneers.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook criticizing a scene on a Rio de Janeiro train platform, which he claimed challenged social conventions and was dangerous. The post, initially appearing homophobic, cleverly mocked conservative attitudes by highlighting a man standing on the yellow safety line instead of the women embracing. The post went viral, garnering over 100,000 shares in 24 hours, with users praising Felippe's witty approach to combating homophobia.

Jonathan Stevenson, now a director at LiveWire Sport, shared a letter from cricket legend Richie Benaud, who responded to Stevenson's 1996 query about left-handed leg spin bowling when he was 16. Benaud's detailed advice, dated September 27, 1996, included tips on various deliveries and was shared as a tribute after Benaud's recent death.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg envisions a future where virtual reality replaces physical travel, allowing people to experience global locales without leaving home. Zuckerberg discussed this vision in a Q&A, predicting that users will capture and share 3D scenes and environments through virtual reality. Facebook's acquisition of Oculus and plans to support VR on its newsfeed further underscore this vision, with users potentially exploring destinations via Oculus Rift headsets.

Guo Kai fulfilled his girlfriend Dong Hui's birthday wish by having their wedding photographs taken despite her being bedridden in hospital with bone cancer in Sichuan, China. Family and friends helped Dong put on a wedding dress, and professional photographers captured the moment, with Guo promising to support her through her treatment. The couple, who met a year ago, had planned to marry this month but had to postpone due to Dong's sudden illness.

Blaine Boudreaux, 34, was charged with intoxication manslaughter and other offenses after three DUI collisions in Houston on Sunday, resulting in two deaths, including a 6-year-old boy named Joshua Medrano. Boudreaux also injured Joshua's mother and killed a 61-year-old homeless man, Leonard Batiste. He was arrested at the scene of the final crash after failing a field sobriety test.

Microsoft launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond, Washington campus, in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The initiative was announced by Microsoft Corporate VP of Worldwide Operations, Mary Ellen Smith, whose son has autism. Smith emphasized the importance of diversity and the unique advantages individuals with autism can bring to the workforce.

Sheriff Stanley Glanz reassigned two deputies involved in the fatal arrest of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, due to threats against them and their families. The deputies were criticized for pinning Harris' head to the ground as he said he was losing his breath, with police responding with profanity. Sheriff Glanz also apologized to Harris' family and said the FBI had cleared the agency of any civil rights violations in the shooting. Deputy Robert Bates, charged with second-degree manslaughter, claims the shooting was accidental.

Katie Prager, 24, diagnosed with a lung infection in 2009, urgently needs a lung transplant to survive, as her insurance, Kentucky Medicaid, refuses to cover out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Her husband Dalton, 23, who has already received new lungs, is pleading for help to save his wife, as Medicaid considers her a financial burden.

Researchers using Sleep Cycle app data found that South Africans wake up earliest on Mondays at 6:09 am, while Americans rise at 7 am on Tuesdays and report the worst mood. Slovakia had the best sleep quality, while the UK ranked 45th and the US 49th. Globally, Wednesday nights offered the best sleep quality, with 58% of countries surveyed experiencing their most restful sleep then.

A series of unpublished love letters from Frida Kahlo to her lover Jose Bartoli are expected to fetch over $120,000 at an auction on April 15. The passionate correspondence, written between 1946 and 1949, details Kahlo's secret three-year romance while she was married to muralist Diego Rivera. The collection, comprising more than 100 pages, includes drafts of Bartoli's responses, a drawing of a sleeping cat, and pressed flowers.

Len McCluskey, leader of the trade union Unite, toured South Wales to support Labour's election campaign, emphasizing traditional socialist values. Despite his popularity among activists, concerns remain about Unite's significant influence over Labour candidates and its potential to revive socialist policies from the 1970s, including increased public sector expansion and higher taxation. McCluskey's union, with 1.42 million members, is deeply integrated into Labour's structure, finances, and policies, raising fears of a return to past economic challenges.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz filmed animals drinking water from troughs using a GoPro camera at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv. He recorded the footage for 30 hours and compiled it into a four-minute video, capturing unique perspectives of various animals, including a rhino that almost kisses the water and a lemur that delicately licks it. Some animals were initially cautious about the camera but eventually drank freely.

Only 25% of voters think David Cameron is the most eager to win the election, according to a YouGov poll for The Times. In contrast, 43% believe Ed Miliband is the most passionate about securing victory. Despite criticism of a lackluster campaign, Cameron insisted he was working hard to secure a majority, appearing in casual attire to demonstrate his commitment.

Zaur Dadaev, charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemtsov, told a Moscow court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused, had previously confessed but later retracted his statement, claiming signs of torture. Human rights activist Andrei Babushkin reported seeing injuries on Dadaev's body during a jail visit. Nemtsov was shot four times on a bridge near the Kremlin in February, prompting a large protest march in Moscow.

A baby named Sonit Awal was rescued after being trapped under rubble for 22 hours following a 7.8-magnitude earthquake in Nepal on April 25. The earthquake killed over 5,000 people and injured at least twice as many. Sonit, four months old, was found alive by Nepalese Army soldiers who returned to the site after his father heard faint cries from the debris in Muldhoka, Bhaktapur. The baby was taken to Bhaktapur Hospital and was found to be uninjured.

Narcocon, a Church of Scientology-affiliated drug rehab network, is facing opposition over plans to turn a 40-acre property near Camp David into a rehab center. The organization argues the site has historic significance because President Herbert Hoover once fished there, aiming to bypass current zoning laws. Narcocon, which uses sauna sessions and vitamin therapy, bought the property for $4.85 million in 2013 and faces criticism for its controversial treatment methods.

Five former NATO interpreters in Kabul now face unemployment and isolation, fearing reprisals and unable to return to their families. The U.S. Embassy and NATO declined to comment. Kabul's population has surged, but the city's once-busy streets and neighborhoods are now deserted as foreign presence diminishes, leaving behind idle war machinery and empty markets.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured on Friday while swimming in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia. The SEALS were performing laps without gear when they were found at the bottom of the pool around 3pm local time. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two, and an investigation into the incident is ongoing.

NBC has transported its entire Premier League production team to England for the first time, reflecting a significant increase in US viewership. In 2012-13, 13 million Americans watched at least one live Premier League match, which rose to 32 million last season. NBC's star anchor Rebecca Lowe, joined by former players Robbie Earle and Kyle Martino, covered the Burnley-Arsenal match and will also broadcast the Manchester derby and Liverpool-Newcastle games.

Boris Johnson launched a personal attack on Labour leader Ed Miliband during a live TV appearance on the Andrew Marr Show, accusing him of doing more damage to the country than he did to his brother. The exchange turned into a heated argument, with Miliband responding that Johnson was better than the insults he was using. Johnson criticized Labour's potential reliance on SNP support for governance, likening it to being "crouching on his back like a monkey."

Dustin Irons, 26, was sentenced to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court after flashing a judge via video-link from Umatilla County Jail in Oregon. Despite being handcuffed, Irons managed to pull down his pants during the hearing, which he attended remotely due to ongoing charges including second-degree assault and unlawful use of a weapon. The judge, visibly upset, added the extra time to his sentence, and Irons faces further disciplinary action within the jail.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has made significant progress ahead of the Chinese Grand Prix after showing improved pace in Malaysia despite both Button and Fernando Alonso retiring due to failures. The team now competes with midfield runners like Force India and Sauber, marking a step forward from their poor performance in Australia. Button acknowledges the need for further improvements in downforce and power unit but is optimistic about the team's direction.

The $2 billion Fiona Stanley Hospital in Perth was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, raising serious hygiene concerns. The hospital previously lost its medical service provider, Serco, after failing to return sterilizing equipment by an arranged date in February. Australian Medical Association WA president Michael Gannon expressed deep concern over the ongoing issues, suggesting the problem has not been adequately resolved.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, both from Gotham, Nottingham, chose to forgo their dream wedding to afford one last round of IVF, which resulted in the birth of twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley. Weeks later, they won a wedding competition, allowing them to finally say their vows. The couple had previously spent £5,500 on two unsuccessful rounds of IVF before making the difficult decision to prioritize fertility treatment over their wedding.

Scooter's Coffee in Omaha had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link. The hackers controlled the page for nearly 24 hours, posting adult cartoons similar to those seen in previous hacks of major brands like Crayola. The company regained control only after contacting larger businesses to reach Facebook officials. Scooter's Coffee issued an apology to its customers for the inappropriate content.

A young Shibu Inu puppy caused laughter at an American Kennel Club center by attempting to bark at a husky, making high-pitched whining sounds instead. The video shows the Shibu Inu vocalizing with a yappy bark, prompting the husky to whine back, with onlookers laughing and filming the interaction. The Shibu Inu later runs in its owner's arms, eager to get closer to the husky, before a staff member calms it down with a rub.

Liam Plunkett, a 29-year-old England seamer, aims to use his pace to challenge the West Indies batting lineup in the upcoming Test series. Recovering from a minor ankle injury, Plunkett seeks to make a name for himself in the Caribbean, emphasizing his ability to bowl fast and disrupt batsmen. He competes for a starting position with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, with the first Test scheduled for April 13 in Antigua.

Paul Smith will face Andre Ward in a 12-round bout, though not for Ward's title. Ward, considered one of the top five pound-for-pound boxers, sees Smith as an ideal warm-up opponent. The WBA has ordered Ward and Carl Froch to meet in a unification fight, but Ward prefers to fight in London rather than Nottingham. Froch is now considering a fight in Las Vegas against Julio Cesar Chavez Jr.

Tyrus Byrd, Parma's newly elected black mayor, was sworn into office last week, but her victory was overshadowed by the resignations of five of the city's six police officers, the city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor, all citing 'safety concerns.' The city, with a population of 713, is divided between 57% white and 41% black residents. Byrd and her father, former city board member Simon Wofford, say they are unsure of the reasons behind the resignations, despite residents rallying in support of the new mayor.

Manchester City will make midfielder Yaya Toure available this summer despite his desire to stay, due to his high wages. Toure, who has helped the club win two Premier League titles and other trophies, is also of interest to Inter Milan, though his salary is a significant barrier. Meanwhile, City are determined to complete a £24 million deal for striker Alvaro Negredo, rejecting Valencia's potential attempts to pull out of the agreement.

A new study claims that over two-thirds of people taking antidepressants do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. Researchers found that 69% of those on antidepressants, particularly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), did not have clinical depression, and 38% did not have other psychiatric disorders like OCD or anxiety. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, suggests that antidepressants are often prescribed without clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller's daughter, Natalie, 28, who suffered from bipolar disorder and psychosis, died by suicide in Baltimore last month. Fuller detailed Natalie's worsening condition over years, noting her first psychotic episode at 22 after leaving for college. Despite periods of stability with medication, Natalie eventually stopped taking her meds, leading to her tragic end.

Koby Hodder, a 10-year-old boy, suffered a cardiac arrest and collapsed during a game of British Bulldog at his school in Doncaster. His heart stopped for 12 minutes, but teachers administered CPR until paramedics arrived and used a defibrillator to restart his heart. Koby was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as former footballer Fabrice Muamba. Teachers have called for the game to be banned due to safety concerns.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain’s most senior female judge, proposed overhauling divorce laws in England and Wales to remove the need for blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. The proposal includes a one-year cooling-off period to encourage couples to resolve issues regarding children and finances before finalizing a divorce. Currently, divorcing couples must cite one of five reasons, with unreasonable behavior being the most common. Critics argue that the current system encourages recriminations.

Tottenham are considering building a £400 million stadium with a retractable pitch to host NFL games, potentially sharing it with a new NFL London franchise. The stadium, set to be completed by the 2018-19 season, could feature a slide-out grass pitch and an NFL synthetic surface underneath, along with extra-large changing rooms. NFL officials are exploring options for a permanent London franchise within five years, with Wembley currently hosting games.

A group of 13 U.S. senators, including John McCain and Robert Menendez, wrote to FIFA urging the organization to remove Russia as host of the 2018 World Cup due to its involvement in the Ukraine crisis. The senators argued that hosting the event would bolster Russian President Vladimir Putin's regime and provide economic relief during international sanctions. England, meanwhile, is considering a bid for Euro 2028 but not for the 2026 World Cup, following the FA's decision to avoid bidding under current FIFA leadership.

Universal announced that the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey," titled "Fifty Shades Darker," will be released on February 10, 2017, with the third film set for February 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, husband of author E.L. James, will write the script for the second film. Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are negotiating for higher pay following the first film's success, which earned $568.8 million worldwide.

Tony Pulis, West Brom manager, will receive a hero's welcome at Crystal Palace on Saturday, where he previously led a successful season. Despite his expertise in keeping clubs in the Premier League, Pulis has never finished higher than 11th, making him the only manager with over a year's experience who hasn't achieved a top-half finish. West Brom's current relegation battle, with only seven points above the bottom three, adds to Pulis's frustration.

Fenerbahce called for the suspension of the Turkish championship after their team bus was attacked by gunmen, injuring the driver. The attack occurred near Trabzon as the bus was returning to Istanbul following a match. Fenerbahce's official statement emphasized the need to find and punish the perpetrators, while the club's general secretary described the incident as "very wrong."

A massive avalanche struck Everest Base Camp during a Nepalese earthquake, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. The disaster left hundreds of climbers stranded at higher camps due to the dangerous condition of the Khumbu Icefall. Helicopters were deployed to rescue trapped climbers, with estimates suggesting up to 200 people were stuck above Base Camp. The earthquake's total death toll exceeded 4,300, with over 8,000 injured.

Gregory Margolin, an 87-year-old Jewish veteran of World War II, survived a missile strike in Eastern Ukraine on February 10, which destroyed his house and killed his daughter. Margolin, who had previously fought in the Soviet Red Army, moved to Israel on March 24 with his family, joining a wave of 600 Ukrainian Jews relocated by the International Fellowship of Christians and Jews since December.

John Carver, Newcastle's current head coach, faces a crucial Tyne-Wear derby against Sunderland, aware that the outcome could significantly impact his future at the club. Carver recalls Ruud Gullit's controversial decision to bench key players in 1999, leading to a 2-1 defeat and Gullit's subsequent dismissal. Carver emphasizes the importance of a positive result for his standing with fans and hopes a narrow victory will suffice.

Reverend Al Sharpton addressed the Walter Scott case and police reform during a sermon in North Charleston, South Carolina, on Sunday. Mayor Keith Summey, Police Chief Eddie Driggers, and Senator Marlon Kimpson were among those in attendance. Sharpton emphasized the need for change in policing practices and praised Summey for firing officer Michael Slager, who is charged with Scott's murder. Sharpton also planned to attend a vigil near the shooting site later that day.

Brendan Rodgers will speak with Raheem Sterling about his responsibilities after the Liverpool forward was involved in recent controversies, including being videoed inhaling nitrous oxide and smoking a shisha pipe. Sterling scored Liverpool's first goal in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United but faces a club investigation and potential disciplinary action. Rodgers praised Sterling's performance but noted the player's disappointment at not scoring more goals.

Labour received more than £1 every second from trades unions in the second week of the election campaign, totaling over £700,000, more than twice the £492,512 received by the Conservatives. Unions like Unison and Unite contributed significantly, with Unison donating £311,875 and Unite £112,000. The Liberal Democrats and UKIP received £50,000 and £8,000, respectively.

Police were called twice to a Qatar Airways flight at Birmingham airport after passengers became disruptive following a five-hour delay on the tarmac. The plane had been diverted from Manchester due to severe winds, and passengers were initially told to stay seated while the plane was refueled and a new crew arrived. Anger escalated when passengers tried to disembark, leading to a second police intervention. Qatar Airways apologized for the delays, citing safety concerns as the priority.

Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring before his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao in Las Vegas on Saturday. Bieber, a close friend of Mayweather, has accompanied him into the ring on several previous occasions. The fight, billed as the biggest in history, takes place at the MGM Grand, with Mayweather's perfect 47-0 record on the line.

Corinthian Colleges Inc. announced it would close all 28 of its remaining campuses, affecting over 70,000 students. The U.S. Department of Education's curtailment of federal student aid access last summer prompted the closure. For-profit colleges, which enroll 13% of students but account for nearly half of all student loan defaults, face increasing scrutiny and calls for reform.

Pep Guardiola denied a dispute with former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after claiming the medical staff was blamed for the Champions League defeat by Porto. Guardiola, addressing the team's injuries and subsequent loss, stated that the doctor's decision was his own and that injuries are part of football, not the medical staff's fault. Muller-Wohlfahrt, who had worked at Bayern for nearly 40 years, cited a damaged bond of trust as the reason for his departure.

Wladimir Klitschko reminisced about his Olympic gold win in 1996 and his rise to become heavyweight champion, ahead of his world title defense against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden. Klitschko, 39, emphasized the transformative power of sports and his belief that age is an advantage, given the right lifestyle. He expressed confidence in his preparation and readiness for the fight.

Jeremy Clarkson admitted he will miss fronting Top Gear after being fired in March for attacking a producer. Clarkson, 54, expressed heartfelt thanks to supporters and said he would miss being on the show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, 70, expressed interest in returning to Top Gear if invited, suggesting the show should evolve to include a woman.

Celta Vigo's Fabian Orellana was sent off with a straight red card for throwing a chunk of grass at Barcelona's Sergio Busquets during a La Liga match. The incident occurred as Busquets attempted to waste time, leading to Orellana's dismissal after the grass hit Busquets in the neck. Barcelona secured a 1-0 victory, with Jeremy Mathieu scoring the only goal in the 73rd minute.

Federal Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors in the Dzhokhar Tsarnaev trial to avoid the Boston Marathon and related events, stressing the importance of avoiding prejudicial influences during the sentencing phase, which begins April 21. Tsarnaev was convicted on all 30 counts, including use of weapons of mass destruction and conspiracy, following a trial where prosecutors called 92 witnesses. The sentencing phase could last up to four weeks and may result in the death penalty for several charges.

Tens of millions of Chinese people celebrated the Qingming Festival by traveling to their ancestral villages and cleaning tombs. The festival, also known as the 'Tomb Sweeping Festival,' includes honoring ancestors and marking the start of spring. In Shaanxi Province, a grand ceremony was held in honor of the 'Yellow Emperor' Huangdi, with thousands attending and traditional dances performed. The three-day holiday saw around 1.3 billion people participate in various celebrations across China.

Paul Simon, 73, returned to the top of the UK album chart with "The Ultimate Collection," his first number one in 25 years, surpassing younger artists like Ed Sheeran. The album includes 19 tracks from his 50-year career, featuring hits from his time with Simon & Garfunkel and his solo work. His recent tour with Sting is believed to have contributed to the album's success.

Iker Casillas declared he will stay and fight for his position at Real Madrid despite rumors of Manchester United's David de Gea joining. Casillas, 33, expressed his commitment to fulfill his contract and help Real Madrid defend their Champions League title, which they have reached the semi-finals of. He emphasized the importance of teamwork and effort in the upcoming semi-finals against formidable opponents including Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Juventus.

The number of people in work in Britain reached a record high of over 31 million, with employment rising by 557,000 from the previous year. The International Monetary Fund praised Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy, commending the reduction of the fiscal deficit and the creation of jobs. IMF chief Christine Lagarde and German finance minister Wolfgang Schaeuble both endorsed the UK's economic approach, highlighting its success in contrast to Labour's austerity opposition.

SsangYong is launching the Tivoli SUV in the UK this summer, priced from under £13,000, aiming to compete with the Nissan Juke. The Tivoli offers three trim levels, including a top-of-the-range ELX model with advanced features like a TomTom navigation system and rear-view camera, priced from £16,000 to £19,000. SsangYong's UK sales and marketing director expects the Tivoli to double the company's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 units.

Sam Longhurst, head chef of Splendid Kitchen in Manchester, created a 10-inch-tall burger called "The Whole Damn Farm" containing six forms of three different meats, weighing half a kilogram and totaling 2,000 calories. The burger includes two beef patties, a whole fried chicken thigh, and various other meats, inspired by a customer's challenge to incorporate three kinds of meat into a burger. It costs £13.50 and is described as a monstrous meal equivalent to six Big Macs.

Yeo Valley's headquarters in North Somerset features a staff canteen offering gourmet meals prepared by a Michelin-starred chef for as little as £2. The menu, which changes daily, includes organic and locally sourced ingredients, such as vegetables from a nearby community farm and meat from Yeo Valley's own Holt Farm. The canteen, now open to the public at higher prices, has been hailed as the world's best staff canteen.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration caused by his Type II diabetes but is now feeling much better and has returned home. His daughter, Claudette King, confirmed his improvement, and a publicist stated he was resting and spending time with his grandchildren. King, 89, thanked those who expressed concern and mentioned he was a "trouper" who wouldn't let his fans down.

On Easter Sunday, Fifth Avenue in Manhattan was filled with people wearing elaborate and whimsical hats, ranging from floral designs to a ship-shaped hat and a diorama inspired by Mayor Bill de Blasio. The parade, which included Christians emerging from Mass and others simply enjoying the sunny day, featured various headpieces like bunny ears, eggs, and moving rabbit puppets. Local hatmaker Mary Ann Smith, who wore a blue ship hat, explained her design as symbolizing "sailing to new heights."

Emergency crews in Essex dispatched two ambulances to Epping Forest after a caller reported a person had been hit by a car, only to find the 'victim' was a run-over squirrel. The East of England ambulance service detailed 1,248 inappropriate calls in the last two years, including one where a man claimed his burger was bleeding. Regional Head of Emergency Operations Centres Gary Morgan urged callers to use common sense, warning that prank calls could endanger lives.

Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake of Chelsea won a head-to-head challenge against Loic Remy and Willian, organized by Audi. The pair secured a 6-0 lead after winning two rounds, including a long-range shooting game and a tennis-like challenge over an Audi R8. However, Remy and Willian redeemed themselves in the final challenge, winning and causing Willian to accidentally smash a wing mirror off one of the cars.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, suggesting Sterling is being manipulated and would stay if left to decide alone. Rodgers revealed he had spoken with Sterling, advising him to remain at Liverpool for his best interests, despite the player rejecting a £100,000-a-week contract extension. Sterling's agent, Aidy Ward, was indirectly blamed for the televised interview where Sterling admitted being flattered by Arsenal's interest.

Countdown co-presenter Rachel Riley was embarrassed when contestants suggested the word 'erection' during a recent episode. Host Nick Hewer struggled to contain his laughter, while celebrity guest Dr Phil Hammond provided the nine-letter word 'recondite' to save the situation. This incident follows previous instances where rude words like 'todgers' and 'm*nges' caused similar reactions among the show's hosts.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, was arrested for attempting to buy deadly poison on the dark web, which he claimed was for suicide. Covert counter-terrorism officers tracked his online activities and arrested him on February 16. He pleaded guilty and was sentenced to a 12-month referral order at Manchester Youth Court.

Lianne Hindle, 37, died three hours after giving birth to her daughter at North Manchester General Hospital in December. Her death followed a series of tragedies at the hospital, including the deaths of three babies and one mother in the same maternity unit. Hindle's partner, Chris Barnes, is calling for action to prevent further deaths, highlighting concerns over the care she received post-delivery. An independent expert review was initiated after 10 deaths occurred in the hospital's maternity units between December 2013 and July 2014.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after being filmed training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, plans to compete in the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics. Emily was born at 3.1 kilograms, and Pittman, who was 32, had previously won a world title seven months after her first child's birth in 2006.

At least one person died and four were missing after a powerful storm capsized several sailboats during the Dauphin Island regatta in Mobile Bay on Saturday. More than 100 sailboats and up to 200 participants were involved in the event. The Coast Guard rescued a man around 9 p.m. and continued searching through the night. Mayor Jeff Collier described the incident as a tragic day with scattered boats from Dauphin Island Bridge to Fort Morgan.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma in an interview with The Daily Beast. Her vision is deteriorating, and doctors have not provided a timeline for the progression of her conditions. Ophthalmologist Steven A. Shanbom explained that while the combination of both diseases is severe, there are treatments that can delay their progression and potentially halt further vision loss.

A Stephens County jury convicted 17-year-old Chancey Allen Luna of first-degree murder for the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane in Duncan, Oklahoma. The jury recommended life in prison without parole for Luna, who was in a car that fired the fatal shot at Lane while he was jogging. Defense attorneys argued Luna intended only to scare Lane, not kill him.

Arsene Wenger downplayed his poor record against Jose Mourinho ahead of Arsenal's top-of-the-table clash with Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium. Wenger has not won any of his 12 previous encounters with Mourinho, drawing five and losing seven. Despite their frosty relationship, Wenger focused on the team's current form and the opportunity to close the gap on Chelsea, who are 10 points ahead. The match, set for Sunday at 4pm, also marks Cesc Fabregas's return to the Emirates in Chelsea colors.

Manny Pacquiao, a former poverty-stricken boxer from the Philippines, is set to face Floyd Mayweather in a $300 million bout on Saturday at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao's rise to fame began in 2001 when he fought Lehlo Ledwaba in Las Vegas, and he has since become a global icon, facing top fighters like Oscar De La Hoya and Juan Manuel Marquez. Recent photos from 1996 show Pacquiao training in Manila at age 17, long before his mega-fights became a reality.

Jack Grealish, a standout player for Aston Villa in their FA Cup semi-final win over Liverpool, was photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, joining other top-flight stars in similar incidents. The incident raises concerns about the impact of such behavior on his career, with experts emphasizing the importance of maintaining a disciplined lifestyle for top athletes.

Sam Barton, who underwent £55,000 in cosmetic surgery to resemble Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men who threw eggs at him in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands, on Easter Monday. Barton believes the attackers tracked him down through his Facebook posts. The incident followed online bullying that forced him to move house, and he attributes the attack to his social media presence.

Manchester University in Indiana was placed under lockdown late Friday night following a 'likely prank call' about an armed individual near the administration building. Police responded to a report of a stabbing and threats to detonate explosives. Students were advised to shelter in place, and authorities, including a bomb squad, investigated the scene. No injuries were confirmed, and the lockdown continued into the early hours of Saturday.

Edinson Cavani faces a crucial match against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals, aiming to lead Paris Saint-Germain to the semi-finals. PSG are without key players Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Verratti due to suspensions. Cavani, known as El Matador, must perform well to overcome Barcelona's formidable attack, as he has struggled with a goal drought and recent disciplinary issues.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title with a unanimous points decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool. Mathews secured the victory with scores of 114-112, 114-112, and 115-112, despite Luis's aggressive style. Both fighters were deducted a point in the eighth round, Mathews for a low blow and Luis for head butting. The win came after Richar Abril and Ismael Barroso both withdrew from the fight.

Hull secured a surprising 28-20 victory over St Helens at Langtree Park, ending St Helens' three-game losing streak. Jamie Shaul's long-distance try proved crucial, sealing the win despite St Helens' earlier lead. The match saw Hull capitalize on St Helens' fatigue and injuries, with key moments including Shaul's try and Leon Pryce's intervention in the second half.

The U.S. immigrant population, both documented and undocumented, could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, according to U.S. Census figures. By 2060, immigrants could account for 82% of all population growth, with one in five U.S. residents being an immigrant. The Center for Immigration Studies report highlights the significant impact of current immigration policies on future population trends, raising concerns about workforce, education, and infrastructure.

Jack Wilshere captained Arsenal Under 21s in his return from injury but could not prevent a 1-0 defeat against Reading's Under 21s at the Emirates Stadium. Niall Keown, son of former Arsenal defender Martin Keown, scored the winning goal with a header in the eighth minute. Other returning Arsenal players included Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby, who played for 56 minutes.

Justin Rose showed signs of recovery at the Shell Houston Open, posting a 69 and hitting 17 out of 18 greens in regulation after a poor Florida swing that dropped him out of the world's top 10. Rose attributed his decline to technical issues with his swing and putter, which he has since corrected. Fellow players Scott Piercy and Phil Mickelson also performed well, with Piercy scoring a 63 and Mickelson achieving his best round in months with a 66.

A newly-built mansion on the site of a former milking parlour in Mayfair, London, is on the market for £25 million. Originally used for dairy farming in the 19th century, the property was demolished in 2011 and rebuilt as a luxurious four-bedroom home featuring an indoor swimming pool, gym, cinema room, and lift. The house spans 8,139 square feet and is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank.

Bayern Munich, facing multiple injuries, including Arjen Robben and Franck Ribery, showed unity in recent victories against Dortmund and Leverkusen. Striker Thomas Muller expressed confidence in the team's ability to form a strong unit for their Champions League quarter-final against Porto. Coach Pep Guardiola acknowledged Porto's quality and emphasized the need for two strong performances to advance to the semi-finals.
