Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited Mercedes' Brackley base to collaborate on strategies after Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel won the Malaysian Grand Prix. Vettel finished 8.5 seconds ahead of Hamilton and 12.5 seconds ahead of Rosberg, highlighting Ferrari's improved performance. Mercedes motorsport boss Toto Wolff acknowledged the need to analyze why Ferrari outperformed them in high temperatures, indicating a challenging season ahead.

Oklahoma Gov. Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing executions by nitrogen gas if lethal injection becomes unavailable or unconstitutional. The method, which causes a quick loss of consciousness and death from lack of oxygen, is described as humane and painless by Rep. Mike Christian. The bill's passage comes as Oklahoma's executions are on hold due to a Supreme Court review of lethal injection methods. Fallin emphasized her support for the death penalty, stating the new option meets standards of effectiveness and lack of cruelty.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice, including an overhead kick, in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull and tops this week's EA Sports Performance Index with a score of 52.9. Charlie Austin of Queens Park Rangers is the runner-up with a score of 52.2 after scoring and assisting two goals in QPR's 4-1 victory over West Brom. Eden Hazard of Chelsea completes the top three with a score of 51.7 following his goal from the spot in Chelsea's 2-1 win over Stoke.

A Russian freezer trawler, the Dalny Vostok, sank off the coast of Kamchatka, Russia, killing at least 56 of its 132 crew members. The ship, carrying an international crew, tipped over after pulling in an 80-ton fishing net, sinking in just 15 minutes. Over 1,300 people are involved in the rescue operation, with 63 crew members rescued and 13 still missing.

Clinical trials show that olaparib, a drug originally intended for women with BRCA gene mutations, can also benefit men with advanced prostate cancer. Led by researchers at the Institute of Cancer Research and the Royal Marsden hospital, the London trial found that 16 out of 49 men responded positively to the drug, which extended the time their disease remained under control. Olaparib, owned by AstraZeneca, is the first cancer drug to target inherited genetic mutations and works by blocking cancer cells' ability to repair damage.

Rhiannon Taylor, a 29-year-old Australian travel photographer, turned her passion for travel and photography into a business called 'In Bed With', reviewing luxurious accommodations worldwide. With over 12,000 Instagram followers, she documents the best beds, pools, and room service in hotels across destinations like Indonesia, the US, and Mexico. Hotels pay her for reviews and professional pictures, and she collaborates with travel product companies to generate additional income.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was killed in a fight between two adult males in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, eastern South Africa. Stacey Farrell, a 30-year-old tour operator, witnessed the calf being thrown into the air and dragged along the water's surface. The calf's mother, who had been protecting it from other younger hippos, could not save it as one adult grabbed and injured the baby fatally. The calf died hours after the incident.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea following an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was hit by a cigarette lighter thrown from home supporters at Loftus Road during a 1-0 victory for Chelsea. QPR, unlikely to face disciplinary action, is reviewing CCTV footage to identify the culprit and has promised to ban those involved indefinitely. The club has appealed to witnesses to come forward to help identify the perpetrators.

LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect, who was also found dead, had a six-month-old baby with him. Police confirmed the suspect knew the victims but did not disclose how the suspect died. A GoFundMe page set up by the family to cover funeral costs has already surpassed its initial $5,000 goal.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, faced criticism for opposing the right-to-buy policy for housing association tenants while owning a property from such an association. Thornberry, who lost her frontbench job over a controversial tweet, argued against extending the policy, which would allow 800,000 tenants to buy their homes at a discount. Housing association chiefs and Labour Party members were accused of hypocrisy, with Ruth Davison, representing housing associations, owning a £1 million home in Islington.

Wiltshire Police dropped an investigation into a vicious assault on huntsman Mike Lane, 40, three months after he was beaten by protesters. Lane, who suffered concussion and broken teeth, condemned the decision as 'pathetic,' stating that the police could have made more effort despite the evidence provided. The attack occurred during a hunt where only an artificial scent was being chased, and Lane was kicked in the head by a masked protester, his face captured on video.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes stated he has no intention of leaving the club this summer despite links to Manchester United and Chelsea. Gomes, 21, expressed his happiness at Valencia and his desire to remain in Spain for the next season. He scored four goals in 25 La Liga appearances since joining from Benfica last summer, contributing to Valencia's fourth-place finish. Gomes denied any contact from Chelsea, stating he and his agent are unaware of any opportunities from the Premier League club.

Audrey Pekin, 19, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali by Henry Alafu, whom she had met at a bar. Alafu first attacked her at his remote home and then in a taxi as she tried to escape. Despite her family's efforts, Alafu fled back to Nigeria, evading local authorities.

Ashley James, a former Made In Chelsea star, teamed up with PETA to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, which recently reintroduced fur products after a ten-year ban. The campaign features James holding a fake skinned fox to highlight the cruelty of the fur industry. Harvey Nichols claims to source fur responsibly, but PETA disputes this, citing an exposé of 'Origin Assured' fur farms.

Chile will soon recognize civil unions between same-sex couples, joining several South American countries in allowing such unions. President Michelle Bachelet enacted the new law on Monday, which will take effect in six months and grant legal recognition to cohabiting relationships regardless of sexual orientation. The law aims to end discrimination faced by common-law couples and will benefit an estimated 2 million people by providing greater rights in areas like health care and inheritance.

Chelsea are on course to break the Premier League record for most days at the top of the table in a single season, currently leading for 230 days. Jose Mourinho's team has been in first place since August 30, with a seven-point lead over their rivals. The current record is held by Manchester United, who led for 262 days in the 1993/94 season. Chelsea's next three games, including matches against Manchester United and Arsenal, could determine if they surpass this record.

Cape Verde, an Atlantic island nation with a population of 500,000, is leveraging its rich musical heritage to boost its economy. Prime Minister Jose Maria Neves and the Ministry of Culture, led by musician Mario Lucio de Sousa, recognize music as a key resource. The Kriol Jazz Festival, now in its seventh year, attracts international artists and highlights Cape Verde's cultural potential, though the creative sector remains a small part of the economy, according to a 2013 UN report.

A hoax video of a surfer in front of Sydney's Opera House went viral for the second time, reposted by popular radio hosts Fitzy and Wippa. The video, originally uploaded in 2012, resurfaced after recent heavy storms in Sydney. Experts, including swell forecaster Ben Macartney, confirmed the video's impossibility due to the harbor's geography and wave dynamics.

Reading lost to Birmingham 1-0 in a Sky Bet Championship match at the Madejski Stadium, despite dominating much of the game. Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal for Birmingham seven minutes from the end, heading in his 16th goal of the season. The match followed Reading's recent 2-1 defeat against Arsenal in the FA Cup semi-finals.

Paris Saint-Germain's David Luiz will miss the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained during a match against Marseille. Scans revealed Luiz will be out for at least four weeks, dealing a significant blow to the French champions as they fight for the Ligue One title, currently leading by one point over Lyon.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day, with over seven million episodes from seasons one to four downloaded between February and April. Brazil was the top country for illegal downloads, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO responded by launching HBO Now to curb piracy and protect revenue.

Leicester City faces West Ham United in a crucial Premier League match at King Power Stadium. Matt Upson is out for Leicester due to an Achilles injury, while Jeff Schlupp's participation is uncertain due to fatigue. Winston Reid returns for West Ham after recovering from a hamstring injury, but Enner Valencia is ruled out. Leicester has won only one of their last ten home matches, while West Ham are unbeaten in their last seven against Leicester.

A statue of Lucile Ball in Celoron, N.Y., unveiled in 2009, has drawn criticism for its unflattering depiction of the beloved comedian. A Facebook page titled 'We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue' has gained over 600 likes, with comments calling the statue a 'monster' and 'frightening.' The statue, based on a scene from 'I Love Lucy,' is estimated to cost between $8,000 and $10,000 to recast. Artist Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has declined to comment.

Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, lost nearly half her body weight after standing for an 11-hour flight due to concerns about crushing her seatmate. Initially weighing over 20st and a size 26, she joined Weight Watchers and later took up running, reducing her weight to 9st 9lb and a size 10. Her weight loss journey began after a business trip in December 2012, where she felt uncomfortable about her size during the flight.

Nicola Bonn, 34, from London, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences as a new mother. One of her posts, "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves," went viral after she expressed frustration with constant unsolicited advice from others. Bonn highlighted how new mothers often feel pressured to justify their decisions and face judgment from those offering opinions.

Two 17-year-old boys from Dewsbury, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, are believed to have traveled to Syria after heading to Turkey on March 31. Hassan is reportedly related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested in 2006 for his involvement in a plot to murder non-Muslims. The families are deeply concerned about the boys' safety and are urging anyone with information to contact the police. Hassan and Talha had not been in contact with their families for several days.

Stephanie Scott, an adored school teacher from Leeton, was murdered just days before her wedding. Her body was found in bushland after she went missing on Easter Sunday. Her devastated father, Robert, described the pain of losing her when she had much to look forward to, including a wedding with 120 guests. The venue was decorated with yellow balloons and flowers in her memory, while her family prepares for her funeral instead of her wedding.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman aims to strengthen his squad by signing Feyenoord's 20-year-old midfielder Tonny Vilhena this summer. Vilhena, who has one year left on his contract, is open to moving to the Premier League. Additionally, Koeman is interested in securing the permanent transfer of winger Eljero Elia from Werder Bremen and exploring a move for midfielder Jordy Clasie, valued at £10 million.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture from 1820 with beanbags in the library at Ickworth House in Suffolk as part of an experiment to engage visitors, but the move angered heritage experts. Similar experiments are planned at nine other National Trust venues. Art historian Bendor Grosvenor criticized the approach as "misguided" and "patronising nonsense," while the National Trust defended the experiment as a short-term arrangement aimed at enhancing visitor experience.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was seen standing on the side of the road in Sydney as his driver changed a flat tyre outside the Sydney Conservatorium of Music. Felicity Waterford, waiting for her daughter's concert to finish, offered assistance and later took a selfie with Mr. Howard. The incident occurred just weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television after boasting about his fixing skills.

Tony Pulis acknowledged that Joey Barton 'probably had a point' when criticizing West Bromwich Albion for losing their composure after leading 2-0 against Queens Park Rangers in December. Barton had commented that the team did not know how to finish games, a view supported by Pulis, who noted the club's history of conceding leads. The teams are set to meet again on Saturday, with Pulis emphasizing the improvement in West Brom's recent performances.

Primatologists in Ntokou-Pikounda National Park, Democratic Republic of Congo, captured the first photograph of the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, believed extinct since the 1970s. The discovery confirms the species' survival but highlights its vulnerability to commercial bushmeat hunters. Researchers spent three months searching remote areas and found the monkeys living along the Bokiba River, emphasizing the need for conservation efforts.

Kim Kardashian, Kanye West, and their daughter North visited Armenia's capital, Yerevan, for an eight-day trip. The celebrity family toured local landmarks, including the Yerevan Opera House, and stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan. Their visit commemorates the country where Kim's father, Robert Kardashian, was born.

Patrick and Valerie Jubb, British expats in Jimena de la Frontera, Spain, are facing a legal battle with the local town hall over illegal additions to their four-bedroom property, which they bought in 2008. The town hall ruled that the first floor, kitchen, and pool were illegally built by previous owners, threatening to demolish the property despite the Jubbs obtaining a certificate stating there were no infractions when they purchased it. The couple, unable to sell the property for €680,000 due to the dispute, plans to return to the UK but are financially tied to the estate.

Apple reported record-breaking first-quarter earnings, with over 61 million iPhones sold, accounting for more than two-thirds of its $58 billion revenue and the majority of its $13.6 billion profit. Sales in China surpassed those in the US, and despite a 29% decline in iPad revenue, the company's overall performance exceeded analysts' expectations. CEO Tim Cook highlighted the strong iPhone sales and the positive customer response to the new Apple Watch, though specific sales figures for the watch were not provided.

Natali Castellanos-Tyler, 30, died in a single-car crash in Virginia on February 21, with police ruling it an accident due to poor road conditions. However, her 3-year-old daughter, Elisa, has been having nightmares about a white van, leading her father to question the official narrative. This follows reports of hit-and-run incidents involving a white box truck in nearby communities, raising suspicions about the cause of the crash.

Researchers at New York University found that the brain can enhance the recall of neutral events by associating them with emotions. Emotion affects brain regions like the amygdala, striatum, and hippocampus, strengthening memory consolidation. The study highlighted how subsequent emotional experiences can reinforce initially mundane memories, such as how the September 11 attacks influenced memory retention.

Jackson Byrnes, an 18-year-old from northern NSW, was diagnosed with a stage four brain tumour and has raised over $80,000 for life-saving surgery. His girlfriend, Jahnae Jackson, put her studies on hold to care for him after he became paralysed. The surgery, to be performed by Dr. Charlie Teo, is scheduled for Wednesday, with community support raising the funds needed for the operation.

Hull City is targeting QPR centre-back Nedum Onuoha, who has 15 months left on his contract. Onuoha, 28, played in QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion. Hull, along with Everton and West Ham, are interested in Onuoha, while Stoke manager Mark Hughes is also considering a move for him. Additionally, Hull is showing interest in West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe, who could be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have created an interactive map showcasing unique phrases used in different U.S. states, revealing regional grammatical variations. For example, Idaho residents might say "All of my clothes needs washed," while Floridians use "I ain't never had no trouble with none of 'em." The project, which surveyed nationwide opinions on sentences, highlights how certain structures are common in the South but almost unknown in the North.

Kalman Kallai traveled 2,796 miles from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia in a nine-day journey, carrying a green rocking chair attached to his trailer. He stopped at various scenic spots, posing with the chair and interacting with his surroundings, including mimicking planes and dancing with his father, whom he met partway through the trip.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood joked about a letter from six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who had applied for the Villa hotseat after Paul Lambert's sacking. Sherwood revealed a Twix multi-pack as a "win bonus" in reference to Pye's request for sweets and chocolate. The manager had written to Pye, congratulating him on his application and thanking him for the treats.

World boxing champion Kell Brook received a hero's ovation at the Premier League Darts in Sheffield on Thursday. Dave Chisnall won both of his matches, defeating Gary Anderson 7-3 and James Wade 7-1, to move to 17 points in second place. Michael van Gerwen maintained his lead with an 7-5 victory over Stephen Bunting, while Phil Taylor suffered his fourth defeat in five matches against Raymond van Barneveld.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti praised teammate Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his significant off-field contributions, highlighting his role in helping young players and boosting team morale. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 Ligue 1 goals this season, was suspended for the first leg of PSG's Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona but will be available for the second leg at the Nou Camp.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published sensitive details about RAF's main base on the Falklands Islands, including GPS coordinates and runway specifications, on their website. The information, which could aid potential invaders, was available for download before the MoD disabled the link. Defence Secretary Michael Fallon described Argentina as a 'very live threat,' amid plans to lease Russian Sukhoi SU-24 bombers capable of attacking the islands without refueling.

Huddersfield coach Paul Anderson aims to improve his team's offensive performance to match their strong defensive record as they face Catalans Dragons. The Giants have dropped from third to ninth in Super League after losing three consecutive games. Anderson acknowledges the team's defensive strength but emphasizes the need for better offensive play to secure a win and climb the league standings.

Planners in Windsor approved the opening of a second Costa cafe less than 500 yards from an existing one, with a third at a nearby petrol station. Resident Samantha Taylor criticized the decision, citing an oversaturation of fast-food and coffee shops in the area. However, Matt Gordon-Smith argued that Costa's presence could signify economic improvement in Dedworth. Planners noted no legal grounds to reject the application, and Costa cited potential benefits to local trade.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn its support for the shooting of free-running badgers in pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, advocating instead for trapping and then shooting the animals. The BVA concluded that the first two years of culling had not proven that shooting free-running badgers was effective and humane. Environment Secretary Liz Truss pledged to expand culls across the country if the Conservatives win the election, despite criticism from wildlife groups.

Geoff Barrow, founder of Portishead, criticized streaming services for low royalty payments, stating he earned only £1,700 from 34 million plays. Barrow, who also runs Invada Records, argued that such practices hurt young artists' ability to establish themselves. In response, Jay-Z launched Tidal, a streaming service promising better returns for musicians, supported by artists like Rihanna and Madonna.

Online pirates have leaked the first four episodes of Game of Thrones' fifth season, which were scheduled to debut tonight, on torrent sites. The episodes, thought to have originated from press review copies, had been downloaded over 550,000 times by early Sunday morning. HBO stated they are investigating the breach, which occurred within an approved group given access to the episodes. The series remains the most illegally downloaded program globally, with over seven million illegal downloads for its first four seasons between February and April 2015.

Melbourne singer Daniel Buccheri left guests at his brother Adrian's wedding in tears after performing an emotional song as his best man's speech. Composed to popular tunes, the speech at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, east of Melbourne, on March 29, included tributes to his brother and his new wife Sarah. The unique speech, viewed over 100,000 times online, documented Adrian's journey to finding love and highlighted Daniel's admiration for his sibling.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, revealed her fitness routine after giving birth to Mia, which includes daily morning exercise on a bike before her daughter wakes up. Phillips, who is vying for a place on Team GB for the Rio Olympics, also follows a strict diet, eating Greek yogurt and honey for breakfast and avoiding carbohydrates and sugary foods. She hopes to qualify for the eventing team in Rio.

Raheem Sterling's interview about not being ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool angered many fans. The blogger from Live4Liverpool noted that Sterling's comments were ill-timed and could have been engineered by his agent. Fans are now more inclined to let Sterling go if the club gets its money's worth, reflecting a shift in sentiment towards the player.

Former Barcelona players and staff from the 1996 Spanish Super Cup team are now managing some of Europe's top clubs. Luis Enrique, current Barcelona coach, will face Laurent Blanc, now at PSG, in the Champions League. Other managers from that team include Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, Julen Lopetegui at Porto, and Albert Ferrer at Almeria. The group's success in breeding successful managers highlights Barcelona's impact on football leadership.

Eric Cantona declared Paris Saint-Germain's Javier Pastore the best player in the world, praising his creativity and ability to surprise. Despite Messi's 45 goals and Ronaldo's 51, Cantona, a former Manchester United legend, emphasized Pastore's unique skills during an interview at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murdering Michael Spalding, 39, after hacking his body into pieces and dumping the remains in a canal. Simon attacked Spalding with a hacksaw and placed the body parts in suitcases, which he and his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, threw into the Birmingham Canal. Police recovered the suitcases containing Spalding's torso and head, along with tools, on May 5 and May 16, respectively.

Essex and Gloucestershire County Councils have implemented 'loneliness maps' to identify areas where residents, particularly the elderly, are at high risk of social isolation. Health experts warn that loneliness can be as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day, leading to health issues like dementia and high blood pressure. The maps, compiled using statistics and resident surveys, help councils target interventions in the most vulnerable areas. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends this approach to address loneliness across the country.

Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary as a waitress at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City. She started working there at 15, trained by her mother who had been employed for 13 years. Eddingfield, who met her first husband at the restaurant, says it's the only job she's ever wanted.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not automatically return to the international set-up despite scoring 170 in his first outing for Surrey this season. Pietersen scored only 19 runs against Glamorgan, and Gatting noted that there might not be space for him if current players like Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root continue to perform well. England's poor showing in the opening Test against West Indies and Alastair Cook's recent struggles also raise questions about team selections ahead of the Ashes.

Caleb Benn, a 17-year-old Californian high school student, developed an iOS app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos directly from their computers, earning him $1,000 a day. However, an Instagram engineer accused the app of violating the company's terms of service and demanded Benn fix it by Monday. Benn, aware of the legal gray area, refused to alter the app, stating that Instagram could have added this feature themselves if desired.

South Korean companies frequently hold hoesik, dinner gatherings with co-workers that often involve heavy drinking, to foster relationships and understand colleagues better. Foreign business travelers face intense pressure to participate, with drinking etiquette being a crucial aspect of these events. Charles Lee, a Korean-Canadian, initially disliked the practice but came to appreciate its social significance. The drinking culture affects Seoul's traffic patterns, with Mondays and Wednesdays through Thursdays being peak nights for hoesik.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was spotted leaving Aberdeen Royal Infirmary with a walking stick after being treated for a dislocated hip sustained during an Easter trip to Balmoral estate. He was admitted to the hospital on Easter Monday and discharged the following day. Buckingham Palace confirmed the successful treatment and noted that the Duke, who previously suffered a mild stroke in 2013, continues to undertake numerous royal engagements.

The 50-year tradition of Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, known for young women in bikinis managing parking meters, is facing criticism from local business leaders who argue it is outdated and no longer serves a public purpose. Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president Peter Yared called for the end of the practice, citing advancements in parking meter technology and concerns over anti-touting laws. However, Surfers Paradise Meter Maids general manager Michael Yarwood defended the tradition, stating it remains integral to the tourist experience.

Greece denied it would fail to pay a £330 million loan to the International Monetary Fund, despite reports suggesting it might default. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas confirmed the payment would be made on time on April 9. Sources close to the Syriza party indicated the government prioritizes paying wages and pensions over loans, potentially leading to a 'silent arrears process' with the IMF if no further aid is provided.

Turkey blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after they refused to remove images of prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz, who was killed during an armed siege last week. The 46-year-old prosecutor died in hospital after being taken hostage by the DHKP-C, a group considered terrorist by Turkey, the EU, and the US. The court imposed the blocks because the images were upsetting Kiraz's family, and authorities had previously tried to prevent newspapers from publishing the images, accusing them of spreading terrorist propaganda.

Seven-year-old Colin Gilpatric, an aspiring Jedi Knight, wrote to George Lucas asking if Jedi could marry without turning to the dark side. Lucasfilm responded with a letter affirming that true Jedi values include friendship, compassion, and loyalty, making marriage possible for those on the path of light. Colin received a package containing Star Wars merchandise and the reassuring letter, which he was overjoyed to open.

Wisconsin ended Kentucky's undefeated season with a 71-64 victory in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, securing their place in the final. Frank Kaminsky led Wisconsin with 20 points and 11 rebounds, while Kentucky finished the season at 38-1. In the other semi-final, Duke defeated Michigan State 81-61, advancing to face Wisconsin for the national championship.

Mötley Crüe's Vince Neil faced criticism for his rendition of the national anthem before a Las Vegas Outlaws game, joining other performers like Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton who have also received mixed reactions for their performances. Houston's 1991 Super Bowl rendition was praised, while Barr's 1991 performance was deemed "disgraceful" by President George H. W. Bush.

Security footage showing Barry Lyttle punching his brother Patrick, putting him in a coma, was released at a Sydney court hearing. Prosecutor Alex Poulos called for Barry, who pleaded guilty to grievous bodily harm, to face a full-time jail term. Magistrate Graeme Curran indicated a jail sentence was likely, with Barry potentially facing up to two years in prison. Patrick, treated for traumatic head injuries, was found in a pool of blood and vomit at the scene.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie found their grave site at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney stripped of all mementos and flowers. The cemetery staff had removed the memorabilia without prior notice, leaving the family devastated. The parents, Simon Howie and Renee Young, discovered their daughters' belongings in nearby bins and were able to retrieve only about 25 percent of the memorabilia. Family members had visited the grave weekly to leave mementos since the twins' burial last year.

Lord Neuberger, President of the Supreme Court, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear full-face veils in court to show respect for different customs. This recommendation came after a 2003 trial where Rebekah Dawson refused to testify without her veil, leading to her imprisonment. Lord Neuberger emphasized the need for judges to be sensitive to cultural differences and to address subconscious biases towards less privileged individuals.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri for killing Anthony Curtis in 1998 during a dispute over child support payments. Cole became the third convicted killer executed in Missouri this year, with the U.S. Supreme Court rejecting his appeals, including one claiming mental illness. Governor Jay Nixon refused a clemency petition, and Cole was executed at 10:15 pm on Tuesday, pronounced dead at 10:24 pm.

Prince Harry will depart the UK for Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is now overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down to fifth in the line of succession, had hoped to meet the new royal baby before leaving but will return in mid-May. The new royal baby, fourth in line to the throne, was expected by Saturday, with excitement mounting among royal superfans despite palace officials barring media from camping outside the Lindo Wing at St Mary's Hospital.

Justin Jackson, a Florida man, has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, executives from her TV network, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager to trick people into providing him with jobs, clothes, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson's eight-year fraud trail included convincing a New York jeweler to lend him items by pretending to be Madonna's manager, leading to a grand theft conviction. He also sent forged letters on Oprah's behalf to hotel groups recommending himself for jobs.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has set a €50 million (£36m) price tag on Paulo Dybala, telling Paris Saint-Germain they must pay a significant amount to sign the player. Dybala, compared to Lionel Messi, is sought after by several top European clubs including Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and PSG. Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini was seen watching Dybala play in a recent match, indicating the intense interest in the player.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians protested across the country, calling for President Dilma Rousseff's impeachment due to an economic downturn and a massive bribery scandal at Petrobras. Rousseff, who was once the chairwoman of Petrobras, denies involvement in the scheme and claims she was merely a figurehead. Her approval rating has dropped to 13%, and the economy is expected to contract this year, with inflation and currency devaluation adding to public frustration.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona denied starring in a soft porn film, calling You and the Night a 'piece of art' at the Laureus Sports Awards in Shanghai. The film features Cantona in racy scenes, including one where he appears in just his underwear. Cantona defended the film, stating it is beautiful and only appears pornographic because of the audience's perception, emphasizing it is a work of art by a special director.

Psychologists found that certain types of music can enhance the flavors of food and drink. At the Ultraviolent restaurant in Shanghai, fish and chips are served with Beatles music, while El Celler de Can Roca in Spain pairs scented meringue with commentary on Lionel Messi. Professor Charles Spence from Oxford University explained that music can draw attention to specific tastes in food and wine, enhancing the dining experience by up to 15 percent.

Raheem Sterling has put contract talks on hold until the summer, despite Liverpool offering him a £100,000-a-week deal. PFA chief Gordon Taylor defended Sterling's decision, stating it is not disloyal and could be beneficial for both player and club to focus on the season's remaining competitions. Sterling, with two years left on his current contract, has been linked with moves to Arsenal and Spanish clubs.

La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, 38, of Youngstown, Ohio, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same company and lived just six minutes away after Ohio released birth records. Mitchell-Clark found Simmons on Facebook and confirmed their relationship through a phone call. Simmons, who gave birth at 15, had always wanted to contact Mitchell-Clark. The reunion also revealed Mitchell-Clark has three younger biological sisters.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a gun trafficker, pleaded guilty to weapons charges related to Aaron Hernandez's murder case. Oscar sent Aaron an assault rifle and two handguns in April 2013, a month before Aaron killed Odin Lloyd. Oscar, now facing up to 30 months in prison, stated in a memo that he was 'awed' by Aaron and 'grateful to be noticed,' unaware of the subsequent murder.

Joel Parker, 33, was arrested for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head in St Johns County, Florida, after threatening and disrupting the driver during the ride. The driver was not injured but called the police, leading to Parker's arrest for battery. Parker posted $250 bond and received a trespass warning, banning him from using the bus again.

Tony Pulis discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will likely stay at West Bromwich Albion beyond the summer despite previous interest from other clubs. Berahino, who expressed a desire to play in Champions League football, is set to join England's under-21 squad in the Czech Republic until late June. Pulis praised Berahino's improved attitude and commitment, suggesting the club is content with his continued presence.

Giovanni Lo Porto, an Italian aid worker, was abducted in Pakistan in January 2012 and died two years later in a U.S. drone strike that also killed American Warren Weinstein. The operation killed at least one al Qaeda leader, Ahmed Farouq. Lo Porto, who studied Peace and Conflict Studies at London Metropolitan University, worked on a clean water and sanitation project in Pakistan after devastating floods in 2010.

Photographer John Massung captured hundreds of sharks swarming just 100 feet from the beach off the coast of south Florida last Thursday. Fellow photographers confirmed the sighting further out at sea. Experts identified the sharks as likely Blacktip or Spinner species, which migrate annually to breed in shallower waters. The photos were shared over 2,000 times on Facebook.

Zeus, an 11-year-old retired K-9 officer, received a heartwarming farewell procession in Ridgefield, Connecticut, on Wednesday. The German Shepherd, who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years, was honored by fellow officers and residents before being euthanized due to a severe degenerative hip disorder. During his career, Zeus assisted in over 250 narcotics arrests and helped track down 50 missing or wanted individuals.

Reports of child sex abuse cases have risen by more than 60% since 2011 following investigations like Operation Yewtree, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014. However, the number of arrests fell by nine percent, leading critics to accuse the Government of failing victims. South Yorkshire saw a 577% increase in reported cases over five years, with only 74 cases reported in 2011 compared to 501 in 2014. Shadow Home Secretary Yvette Cooper described the ratio of reported crimes to arrests as a 'national scandal.'

Iceland has become a popular filming location for hit TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, featuring in productions like Game of Thrones, Interstellar, and Prometheus. Thingvellir National Park served as the North of Westeros in Game of Thrones, while the Svinafellsjokull glacier in Skaftafell National Park was used for Interstellar. Europe's most powerful waterfall, Dettifoss, was featured in Prometheus to depict the beginning of time.

A blue and yellow bathing box in Melbourne sold for a record $276,000, $150,000 over its original asking price, at an auction. In Sydney, a 1917-built fire station turned mechanic’s garage in Paddington sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. Additionally, a 1850s maximum security prison in Victoria, now a renovated home, is on the market for $2 million.

Samantha Rawcliffe, 40, from Morecambe, lost control of her car due to unexplained shaking and was later diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND). Following the May 26 accident, she experienced bladder control issues and was hospitalized, where doctors diagnosed her with FND in September. Now confined to her home, Rawcliffe relies on a mobility scooter and takes 32 different medications daily.

Sculptor Dave Poulin admitted disappointment in a controversial Lucille Ball statue in Celoron, New York, and offered to replace it for free. The statue, nicknamed 'Scary Lucy,' has sparked a social media campaign demanding its removal due to its unflattering depiction. Poulin, who estimates the cost of recasting the statue at $8,000 to $10,000, said he regrets casting it in bronze and vows to create a more appealing sculpture.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba will be sidelined for around seven weeks due to a torn knee ligament. The 22-year-old was injured while playing for Austria in a 1-1 draw against Bosnia. Alaba had been in excellent form for Bayern, contributing to their pursuit of a treble of titles. He expressed disappointment but remains focused on returning for the season finale.

Beatrice Nokes, 21, and Daniel Williams, 37, appeared in court facing charges of running a prostitution ring in Central London. Nokes, a University College London student, is accused of inciting three young women into prostitution, while Williams, a suspended Met police officer, faces seven additional charges including voyeurism and hiding cash in his chimney. Both are the children of respected legal professionals and are on bail pending further hearings.

A firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data, Sequester, is offering details of eating disorder sufferers and other health conditions for 12p per record. The Mail revealed that Sequester, a business partner of Alchemy Direct Media, claims to have information on 43 different health conditions, including personal financial details. This has prompted investigations by the Information Commissioner’s Office, the Direct Marketing Commission, and the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U.

Jordan Spieth, 21, won the Masters golf tournament at Augusta, matching Tiger Woods' 1997 record score of 18 under par. Spieth, the second-youngest winner, led from start to finish, breaking Phil Mickelson's birdie record with 27 birdies. After his victory, he spoke about his 14-year-old autistic sister Ellie, expressing how she provides him with perspective and is the most special part of their family.

Dick Advocaat, Sunderland's new manager, will not underestimate the significance of the Wear-Tyne Derby against Newcastle, unlike his previous mistake in the Old Firm derby with Rangers in 1998. Advocaat, aware of the rivalry's intensity, aims to secure three points to improve Sunderland's standing above the relegation zone. The match is crucial for Sunderland, who have won only twice at home this season and are in a period of unrest.

Belinda Bartholomew, girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, claims she was racially abused at Sam the Butcher in Bondi when trying to buy a chicken. She alleges the butcher called her names and told her to go to an "Aussie butcher." The butcher denies the claims, stating Bartholomew was rude and he was dealing with eftpos machine issues.

Cadbury has reduced the size of its Freddo Frog chocolate bars by 20%, from 15g to 12g, while keeping the recommended retail price unchanged. The company cited rising manufacturing costs as the reason for the change. This move follows a previous reduction in the size of Cadbury's family blocks of Dairy Milk from 220 grams to 200 grams, which also maintained the same price point.

Hillary Clinton's campaign met in Brooklyn on Saturday ahead of her official presidential announcement, set for Sunday. The campaign distributed a "values statement" emphasizing humility, discipline, and unity to avoid past mistakes. The document outlines the campaign's goal to elect Clinton as president and includes the name "Hillary for America." Clinton plans to launch her candidacy through a social media video and will visit Iowa and New Hampshire soon after.

Kyli Wilfson, 29, suffered from chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition affecting less than .01% of people, which left her unable to eat for a year and a half. Initially misdiagnosed with acute pancreatitis, Wilfson experienced severe pain upon eating, leading to a drastic weight loss to 80lbs and postponing her wedding. She now relies on a feeding tube and finds comfort in a Facebook support group for chronic pancreatitis sufferers.

Labour leader Ed Miliband and other party leaders participated in a televised debate, leading to numerous memes mocking the event. Prime Minister David Cameron and Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg were notably absent, appearing in memes alongside Gogglebox viewers. Memes also featured Miliband superimposed over London rapper Plan B, challenging Cameron to a one-on-one debate, and Nicola Sturgeon with a skeptical expression.

Amir Khan could face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi after waiting for a fight with Floyd Mayweather. Bob Arum, Pacquiao's promoter, is considering an offer for a November or December event in Abu Dhabi, with Khan as the top choice. Khan, known for his speed, sees this as a dream fight and a significant opportunity in the Muslim world.

A two-bedroom home in Islington, north London, only 5ft wide in places, has been sold for £750,000. The property, described as "well proportioned" by the estate agency, features a narrow kitchen, study, reception room, shower room, cloakroom, and a garden. It was previously sold for half the price in 2001. The buyer will pay £27,000 in stamp duty.

Nicola Sturgeon launched an SNP manifesto aimed at forming a power-sharing deal with Labour, proposing policies such as reducing English university tuition fees and rolling back NHS competition. The manifesto includes £180 billion in spending increases over five years, funded by borrowing, and calls for recognising Palestine as a state and increasing infrastructure spending in northern England and Wales. Polls suggest the SNP could win up to 50 seats, potentially holding the balance of power at Westminster.

Rangers goalkeeper Robby McCrorie's errors led to Celtic winning the Glasgow Cup for the fourth time in eight seasons at Hampden. Josh Kerr scored after McCrorie missed a corner, and McCrorie later dropped a Mark Hill free kick into his own net. The match, played behind closed doors due to previous fan trouble, saw Celtic dominate play and secure a deserved victory.

Tony Pulis led West Bromwich Albion to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, maintaining his trademark gritty playing style. James Morrison and Craig Gardner scored for West Brom, while Pulis remained in his cap and track suit throughout the match. The win ended West Brom's run of 10 away games without a victory and secured them 36 points, virtually guaranteeing their Premier League safety.

Jameela Jamil spent £3,000 to remove and replace her amalgam fillings with white ones, believing they caused her health issues for seven years. Blood tests revealed high mercury levels, and despite the dentist's belief that the fillings were the cause, dental experts argue that mercury exposure from amalgam fillings is minimal and safe.

Suge Knight laughed in court on Thursday as he revealed hopes that Floyd Mayweather would bail him out after winning his next fight. Knight's bail was refused to be reduced from $10 million, and he had to be wheeled out in a wheelchair after the hearing. Knight's attorney, Matthew Fletcher, believes Mayweather, a close friend and undefeated boxer, will bail him out following his upcoming fight. Knight faces trial for murder and attempted murder, set to begin July 7.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine revealed in Puss Puss magazine that her British shorthair cat, Kimchi, enjoys human foods like poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. The interview featured a lavish spread of caviar, salmon roe, and jellied fish heads, though Kimchi's favorite "death row dish" is taramasalata. Erskine also mentioned her new cat, Ponzu, who developed a fondness for green curry after a brief unsupervised period.

Martin Springall, 38, photographed his daughter in Zushi, Japan, in July 2014, and later noticed a pair of black boots behind her that he could not explain. The image was posted on Reddit, sparking debate about whether it was a trick of the light or a paranormal occurrence. Springall insisted the photo was not Photoshopped and that no one else was present during the shoot.

The Conservative Party plans to require foreign workers to pay an average of £22,000 in tax before accessing UK benefits, as part of a manifesto to curb EU migration. Home Secretary Theresa May announced that unemployed EU migrants will face a four-year ban on state support and could be deported if they do not secure employment within six months. The measures aim to reduce the financial incentive for migration from poorer EU countries and align with the party's goal of negotiating a new deal with Europe.

Cody Neatis, an eight-year-old with Down's syndrome, epilepsy, and autism, was left to sleep on a hospital floor for seven nights at Royal Preston Hospital due to a lack of a suitable bed. His mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, had to stay with him to ensure he did not injure himself or pull out his oxygen tubes. Lynne claims she has been waiting two years for a high-sided cot needed for Cody and other disabled children, highlighting ongoing issues with hospital accommodations for special needs patients.

Ian Poulter forgot his golf clubs in his rental home as he arrived excitedly at Augusta for the Masters. Henrik Stenson, recovering from flu, is among the injured players hoping to perform well despite his condition. Tiger Woods will play in the traditional par-three tournament with his children, Charlie and Sam. Gene Sarazen's albatross shot on the 15th hole in 1935 remains a historic moment in the tournament's history.

Juventus have ruled out signing Manchester United's Radamel Falcao due to his high wages. Falcao, 29, has scored only four goals since joining United on loan from Monaco last summer. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta stated that Falcao's wages are beyond their means. Meanwhile, Juventus are interested in signing Paulo Dybala from Palermo and Edinson Cavani from Paris Saint-Germain to strengthen their forward line.

Prime Minister David Cameron pledged to sell £4 billion of Lloyds Bank shares to the public if re-elected, offering individuals up to £10,000 worth of shares at a discount of at least 5% on the market rate. This would be the largest privatisation since the 1980s, with proceeds aimed at reducing the national debt. Shareholders holding their shares for at least a year would receive a loyalty bonus of one free share for every ten held, up to a maximum bonus value of £200.

Scientists have warned that living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes,' increasing the risk of dementia. A study involving over 900 people aged 60 and over found that exposure to PM2.5, fine particulate matter, was linked to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes. These microscopic particles, primarily from traffic fumes and factory emissions, alter brain structure and contribute to the deaths of 29,000 people annually in Britain.

Jessica Ainscough, 30, died in late February after a seven-year battle with epithelioid sarcoma. Her fiancé, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she underwent radiation treatment in her final weeks, integrating it with her natural healing regime. The treatment successfully shrunk her tumor but complications arose, leading to her death. Pamenter wrote an emotional letter to her followers, praising her courage and grace.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale, Queensland. Four were airlifted to hospitals with injuries ranging from chest pain to arm injuries, while six others with minor injuries were taken to Ipswich Hospital. The highway was closed for several hours with diversions in place.

Jason McDonald, 34, from Aurora, Colorado, walked a slackline over a pool containing more than 50 alligators, some up to ten feet long, at the Colorado Gator Farm. McDonald, a crematory manager and volunteer at the farm, has been working with alligators for over ten years and took handling classes. He said the alligators were surprisingly unbothered by the slackline, though his mother expressed concern for his safety.

Abdul Hadi Arwani, a Syrian imam and opponent of President Bashar Al-Assad, was shot dead in his car in North West London. Sources suggest he may have met his killer days before the murder when the man, posing as a potential client, asked Arwani to return for a building quote. Scotland Yard's counter-terrorism unit is investigating, considering the possibility of a politically motivated assassination.

Hong Kong residents and tourists queue for hours to purchase tins of Jenny's butter cookies, which sell for $9 each. The cookies' popularity has led to the creation of counterfeit versions and a resale market, with some goods being sold at a 70% markup. The bakery warns against buying fake cookies and discourages line-standing services. Similar food crazes, like cronuts and ramen burgers, have also seen intense demand before fading.

Kira Hollis, diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and clinical underweight due to anorexia and depression, turned her life around through bodybuilding. Ordered by doctors to gain weight, she became a personal trainer and now weighs 9.5st, up from 6st. Her recovery was also supported by her daughter Olivia and medication. Hollis's journey inspired millions after she shared her story online.

Eighteen-year-old jockey Lewis Ferguson survived a dramatic double somersault fall from his horse Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton on Wednesday. The incident, watched by hundreds of thousands online, left Ferguson with only a cut on his nose. Despite the fall, Ferguson returned to mucking out stables at Paul Nicholls’ yard on Thursday, undeterred from continuing his racing career.

Hillary Clinton launched an unconventional campaign to rebrand and reframe her image, using a video, new logo, and a road trip to emphasize a more empathetic and forward-looking persona. Critics, including Ruth Marcus and Jon Stewart, dismissed the video as vapid and boring, but marketing experts argue that the campaign may successfully shift public perception. The new logo and her unscripted stops during the road trip aimed to create an emotional connection with voters, a strategy previously seen in successful rebranding efforts like Apple's.

More than 1,700 Chinese students from Yichuan Senior High School in Shaanxi province took an exam in their school playground on Saturday due to insufficient indoor space. The freshmen organized the outdoor exam themselves, turning their chairs and desks collectively as directed by regular radio announcements to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school viewed this as a test of the students' organizing capacity and a way to encourage a relaxed exam environment.

Sportsmail and Gillette are offering a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart to one lucky reader. The winner will also receive a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shave gel. The competition, which closes on April 19, allows fans to enter for a chance to win these exclusive items.

One-year-old orangutan Kecil, rejected by his natural mother and a first surrogate, found a loving home with Maggie, a 53-year-old orangutan at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. After 10 months, Kecil and Maggie share an inseparable bond, with Maggie proving her parenting skills once again. Kecil will make his first public appearance this weekend.

Noelle Baynham, 61, was found dead at her home in Winchester, Hampshire, after her body was partially consumed by her two pet dogs. A close friend discovered her remains when she failed to answer the door, finding the house in disarray with dog feces covering the floors. The dogs, a Jack Russell and a Staffordshire Bull Terrier, were initially thought to have tried to wake her before eating parts of her body out of desperation. The inquest concluded that the most likely cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication, though the exact cause could not be determined due to the dogs' actions.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic will stand trial for fraud over his alleged involvement in illegal betting. Along with his brother Luka and 15 others, Nikola was banned by the French league two years ago for betting on a match where Montpellier, already champions, lost to a struggling team. Karabatic's lawyer aims for a not-guilty verdict, as the player faces up to five years in prison and a fine.

Six men were jailed for a total of 31 years for sexually abusing teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The offences, including rape and inciting sexual activity with a child, occurred at parties organized on social media and at the defendants' homes. Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, received the longest sentence of nine years for his role in luring victims. Thames Valley Police's Operation Reportage led to the convictions following victims' bravery in coming forward.

Aaron Hernandez, convicted of murder in Odin Lloyd's death, faces three more trials, including a murder case involving Daniel de Abreu and Safiro Furtado. Prosecutors allege Hernandez shot and killed the two men in Boston in 2012, with another passenger wounded. Hernandez's civil suits include claims from the victims' families and a man who says Hernandez shot him in Miami. The trials and legal actions could affect Hernandez's $5 million in assets, including a disputed $3.3 million signing bonus from the New England Patriots.

Emirates Airline is set to sign a £30 million three-year deal with the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. The Dubai-based airline already has significant sporting sponsorships, including a £150 million deal with Arsenal that provides naming rights to the Emirates Stadium until 2019. Additionally, Emirates sponsors the Emirates Cup, a pre-season tournament hosted at Arsenal's stadium, and has a £80 million deal with Italian club AC Milan until 2020.

Michael Phelps announced his intention to compete in a fifth Olympics in Rio next year, despite not swimming in the upcoming world championships in Russia due to a six-month suspension by USA Swimming following a second drunken driving arrest. The 18-time Olympic champion expressed regret for his actions and emphasized his commitment to recovery, having completed inpatient alcohol rehabilitation and enrolling in Alcoholics Anonymous.

Gareth Bale is a huge doubt for Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward was forced off after just a few minutes in Real's 3-1 victory over Malaga. Real Madrid's medical staff confirmed a muscular lesion in Bale's left calf, with his condition to be evaluated. Additionally, midfielder Luka Modric is expected to be out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain.

Scientists at Texas Tech University found that over 50% of pensioners sold their investments during the 2007-2008 financial crisis after a 30% stock market decline, leading those who sold at the lowest point to have only £63,000 today from an initial £100,000, compared to £141,000 if they had held onto their investments. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, analyzed 1,204 retired investors and highlighted that better cognitive abilities help retirees avoid emotional decision-making mistakes in the market.

Stuart Pearce believes Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to improve the team's performance. City's title challenge has faltered, and they now face difficulties in securing a top-four finish. Pearce attributes their poor form partly to Yaya Toure's ineffective season and calls for a squad overhaul this summer.

Manchester United's players trained on Friday ahead of their crucial Premier League match against Manchester City on Sunday. Manager Louis van Gaal oversaw the session, which included striker Robin van Persie, who has returned to training after an injury. United, currently ahead of City in the league table for the first time since the Sir Alex Ferguson era, aim to extend their lead to four points with a victory at Old Trafford.

Fiorentina's Champions League hopes were severely dented after losing 1-0 to Verona at home, conceding a late goal by Verona substitute Mounir Obbadi. Fiorentina, now nine points behind third-placed AS Roma, also missed a penalty in the second half when Alessandro Diamanti's shot was saved by Verona's Rafael. The loss leaves Fiorentina in sixth place with 49 points from 31 games.

Miley Cyrus sparked controversy at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, for not shaving her armpits. Social media users criticized her grooming choice, with some calling it "disgusting" and "freaking them out." However, many defended her right to choose, highlighting the double standards in societal expectations regarding body hair.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez scored their 100th goal together for the season in a 6-0 victory over Getafe at the Nou Camp. Messi scored twice, Neymar once, and Suarez twice, bringing their combined total to 102 goals in all competitions. Messi leads with 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. The win extended Barcelona's lead in La Liga to five points.

Andrea McVeigh, 44, was left scarred for life after being hit by a cyclist on a pavement in Bermondsey, south London, on April 14. McVeigh suffered severe facial injuries, including two three-inch gashes on her forehead, and the cyclist fled the scene. The Met Police have issued CCTV footage to find the suspect and appealed for witnesses to come forward.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 for fraudulently obtaining a blue badge by claiming he could only walk 200 metres, despite being an experienced walker and mountaineering club member. The fraud was exposed when council officials read a newspaper report about Gregory's 191-mile hike in Cumbria. At Luton Magistrates' Court, he pleaded guilty and was also ordered to complete 150 hours of unpaid work and undergo 19 sessions of 'thinking skills'.

Apple has been awarded a patent for a facial recognition system that could unlock devices by scanning a user's face with the front-facing camera when the phone is moved into a specific position. Filed in March 2011, the patent describes a method of automatically unlocking the device if the scanned face matches a stored image. Unlike Android's 'Trusted face' feature, which requires the screen to be enabled, Apple's system would track the phone's movement to determine if it is in use and then unlock based on facial recognition.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California with her family because she lacked a doctor's note clearing her to fly, despite suffering from multiple myeloma. Sedway posted an emotional video on Facebook showing the incident, which has been widely shared. The airline representative announced that Sedway could not fly without a doctor's clearance, leading to the family's removal from the plane.

A head-on collision between a 1973 E-Type Jaguar and a Toyota Kluger on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney, left three people hospitalized as a precaution. The vintage Jaguar, valued at over $120,000, was completely destroyed. NSW police are investigating the incident, which occurred on Easter Sunday night. Car enthusiasts expressed sympathy for the Jaguar's owner on social media.

Google has established a four-man team focused on developing advanced battery technologies for devices like phones, tablets, and electric cars. The team, led by former Apple battery expert Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj since 2012, works on flexible and wearable batteries, including solid-state, thin-film options. Google also collaborates with AllCell Technologies to create batteries that function in subfreezing temperatures for its Project Loon internet-providing balloons.

British yacht designer Tony Castro unveiled the 223ft Explorer, a luxury superyacht featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and storage for cars, submarines, and jetskis. The yacht, designed to withstand any weather and circumnavigate the globe, can accommodate 12 guests and 15 crew members. With a construction cost of approximately 40 million euros, the superyacht offers a range of amenities including a cinema, sauna, and wine cellar.

Ed Miliband confirmed Labour's plans to cap rents despite warnings from experts and business leaders that the measures could backfire. The proposals include offering three-year tenancies and banning rent increases above inflation during this period. However, critics argue the plan contains loopholes that could lead to more evictions and higher rents, with some senior Labour figures expressing concerns about unintended consequences.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter, Ryan Dearnley, was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in their FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after expressing support for Arsenal. The decision followed outrage from Reading supporters and a poll where 85% of readers felt Ryan should not lead Reading out at Wembley. The Football Association moved Ryan to an England mascot role instead, offering him two tickets to watch the semi-final in the Arsenal end, which he declined.

Astronomers propose a giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across as the cause of a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, potentially the largest single structure ever found. The Cold Spot, first discovered in 2004, is a less dense region about 20 per cent less dense than other parts of the universe, containing about 10,000 fewer galaxies. Researchers from the University of Hawaii at Manoa suggest the supervoid could sap energy from passing light, leading to the observed colder temperature in the cosmic microwave background radiation.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display the chair in which Abraham Lincoln was shot on April 15, marking the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, believed by many to have a blood stain but confirmed by historians to be oil from previous occupants, has been part of the museum's collection for 85 years. Two days prior, historian Doris Kearns Goodwin will deliver a lecture on Lincoln.

Jake Boys, 19, mistakenly booked flights to Dublin instead of Cardiff for a One Direction concert, surprising his girlfriend Emily-Victoria Canham, 18, with tickets to see the band. The couple, both popular YouTube vloggers, faced the mix-up after Miss Canham discovered the error, leading Mr Boys to plan new train tickets to the correct venue. The concert, supported by McBusted, is scheduled for June 5 and 6 in Cardiff.

Romanian company MB Telecom has developed the Roboscan 2M Aeria, the world's first mobile X-ray scanner for airplanes, capable of detecting contraband, bombs, and weapons. Costing €3 million, the device can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial aircraft in about 20 minutes. Currently, the radiation emitted is not safe for passengers, but the company believes it could enhance aircraft security, especially at low-security airports.

Stephen Munden, a 54-year-old convicted paedophile with a history of sexual offenses against children, has gone missing after escaping from a psychiatric unit near Hook, Hampshire. Described as having a "fanatical obsession" with young girls, Munden was last seen leaving the hospital on Tuesday evening. Police believe he may have shaved his beard and are searching for him based on images released showing him with and without facial hair.

Middlesbrough holds the lead in the Championship with four weeks left in the season, seven points ahead of second-placed Bournemouth. Watford, aiming for promotion, faces Middlesbrough in a crucial match, with Watford's Odion Ighalo determined to secure a win. The promotion race remains tight, with eight teams within seven points of each other, and outcomes could shift significantly based on upcoming matches.

Grey hair is becoming a popular trend among women worldwide, with many posting images on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend, which includes celebrities like Rihanna and Lady Gaga, has been embraced by fashion designers such as Jean Paul Gaultier, who featured silver-haired models at Paris Fashion Week. Instagram and other social media platforms are filled with photos showcasing the look, which is seen as a form of feminist statement and a move away from traditional hair dyeing practices.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, a couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning this week. The Speidels had previously created online fundraisers in late February, pleading for financial assistance due to their inability to work because of chronic conditions. They were found with two charcoal grills in their bedroom, leaving behind two daughters, Randa and Kira. The couple's landlord discovered a note warning of carbon monoxide and firefighters found the grills filled with smoldering coals upon arrival.

Nick Clegg vowed to remain as Liberal Democrat leader regardless of the party's performance in the upcoming election. Friends had suggested he would step down if the party's MPs fell below 30 or if they were left out of power. Clegg expressed optimism about the party's prospects and emphasized the importance of maintaining a centrist position in British politics. Business Secretary Vince Cable also indicated his desire to become Chancellor in another potential coalition with the Conservatives.

Terry Cooper, 79, was saved by his Jack Russell, Sam, from a large badger with six-inch teeth in his garden in Curry Rivel, Somerset. The badger, accompanied by two cubs, burst through a hedge, and Sam dragged Cooper indoors to safety. Following the incident, the National Farmers' Union advised residents to protect their properties by ensuring gaps in fences are no larger than 7.5 centimeters and using badger-proof fencing.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose 3-0 to Porto U21s in the Premier League International Cup semi-final at Motspur Park on Wednesday, while avoiding the Champions League fixtures. Leandro Silva scored a hat-trick for Porto, and Fulham's Liam Donnelly was sent off just before half-time. Mourinho, accompanied by his son Jose Junior, seemed in good spirits despite Fulham's defeat.

Nicole Phillips, 45, was charged with perverting the course of justice in connection with an acid attack on property developer Andreas Christopheros, 29, in Truro, Cornwall. Christopheros suffered life-changing injuries, including loss of vision and facial scars, when corrosive liquid was thrown at him outside his home last December. David Phillips, Nicole's husband, 48, had previously been charged with grievous bodily harm with intent and pleaded not guilty at Truro Crown Court.

Someone in Lastres, a Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route, has posted signs warning visitors not to defecate along the path, depicting a squatting figure within a red circle with a diagonal line. Angry residents complained about pilgrims defecating outside their homes, while some pilgrims now pose for photos with the signs. The mayor of Santos, Julio Gallego, criticized the lack of public facilities for pilgrims along the route, calling it a 'huge failure.'

A massive fire consumed a former strip club building in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday at about 1pm. The site, previously home to The Body Shop, was not vacant at the time of the fire. Thick smoke and large flames were reported, with only the building and a few nearby power lines affected. Local resident Terry Rauh mentioned a previous fire at the same location. An investigation into the cause of the blaze is ongoing.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, reached a settlement in her lawsuit against the federal government, Frontier Airlines, and the Wayne County Airport Authority for being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport. Hebshi, who was detained and humiliated on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks, will receive $40,000 in compensation. The settlement aims to protect future passengers from similar experiences and includes amendments to Frontier's policies on discrimination.

Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 from Seoul to Hiroshima crash-landed and skidded off the runway, injuring twenty people among the 81 on board. The Airbus A320 reportedly missed the landing point, spun 180 degrees, and deployed evacuation slides. Emergency services responded, and the airport was closed. Television footage showed a hard landing with no visible landing gear.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a star of the TV show Made In Chelsea, showcased his collection of 16 expensive watches to the Evening Standard, including a Cartier white gold Moonphase worth £32,000 and a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42 he bought for £6,500. His collection, which he has been building since his teens, features rare pieces like a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée no longer in production.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his extensive collection of antiques, including over 200 items, in a £100,000 auction as he downsizes his home. The collection features a hand-painted limewood diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, estimated at £4,000 to £6,000, and a longbow with a mother-of-pearl handle, set to sell for up to £2,000. The auction, organized by Dominic Winter auctioneers in South Cerney, Gloucestershire, includes paintings, furniture, swords, and books dating back to the 17th century.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook of two women hugging on a Rio de Janeiro train platform, initially posing as if he was expressing disapproval of their behavior. However, his post cleverly spoofed conservative attitudes by actually warning against standing on the yellow safety line, a public transport safety regulation. The post went viral, with over 100,000 shares in 24 hours, as users praised his witty approach to combating homophobia.

Jonathan Stevenson, now a director at LiveWire Sport, shared a letter from the late cricket legend Richie Benaud, responding to Stevenson's 1996 query about left-handed leg spin bowling when he was 16. Benaud's detailed advice, including tips on various deliveries, was shared as a tribute to the "great man" following Benaud's death.

Mark Zuckerberg discussed the future of travel through virtual reality, suggesting people will share 3D scenes and virtual environments instead of traditional photos and videos. Facebook plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed, allowing users to explore locations using VR headsets like Oculus Rift, which the company acquired. Multiple camera viewpoints will enable more immersive experiences, and Marriott hotels have already tested similar technology for virtual tours of their properties.

Guo Kai fulfilled his girlfriend Dong Hui's birthday wish by arranging wedding photographs despite her being bedridden in hospital due to bone cancer. Family and friends helped Dong put on a wedding dress, and professional photographers took pictures while she lay down due to her condition. Guo, now a firefighter, has been at her side since her hospitalization, setting alarms to assist with her hourly needs. The couple met a year ago and quickly fell in love, with Guo promising to support Dong through her battle with cancer.

Blaine Boudreaux, 34, has been charged with intoxication manslaughter and other offenses after causing three DUI collisions in Houston, resulting in two deaths, including a 6-year-old boy, and injuries to others. Boudreaux's first collision involved a mother and her toddler, whom he fled after receiving a ticket. He then struck and killed a 61-year-old homeless man and later fatally injured the 6-year-old boy in a separate crash.

Microsoft launched a pilot program to hire individuals with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond, Washington campus, in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The initiative was announced by Microsoft Corporate VP of Worldwide Operations, Mary Ellen Smith, whose son has autism, emphasizing the company's commitment to diversity and inclusion.

Sheriff Stanley Glanz announced that two deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The deputies were criticized for pinning Harris' head to the ground during the arrest, and the sheriff's office has temporarily suspended operations of its drug unit pending a review of the incident. Bates, the deputy who shot Harris, is charged with second-degree manslaughter and claims the shooting was accidental. Glanz apologized to Harris' family and denied allegations of training record forgery or unqualified service for Bates.

Katie Prager, 24, and her husband Dalton, 23, both suffering from cystic fibrosis, face a critical situation as Katie awaits a life-saving lung transplant due to a lung infection. Dalton, who has already received new lungs, is appealing for help as Kentucky Medicaid refuses to cover the out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. The couple's insurance limitations and Medicaid's refusal to negotiate are jeopardizing Katie's chances of survival.

Researchers using data from Sleep Cycle app users found that South Africans wake up earliest on Mondays, while Americans have their worst mood on Tuesdays. Slovakia had the best national average sleep quality, with the UK ranking 45th and the US 49th. Globally, the best sleep quality occurs on Wednesday nights, with more than half of surveyed countries reporting the most restful sleep then.

A series of unpublished love letters from Frida Kahlo to her lover Jose Bartoli are set to be auctioned at Doyle New York on April 15, expected to fetch over $120,000. The passionate correspondence, written in Spanish between 1946 and 1949, details Kahlo's secret three-year romance while she was married to muralist Diego Rivera. The collection, comprising over 100 pages, includes drafts of Bartoli's responses, a drawing of a sleeping cat, and pressed flowers.

Len McCluskey, leader of the trade union Unite, toured South Wales to support Labour's election campaign, demonstrating his popularity among activists. Despite his genial demeanor, McCluskey and Unite are viewed as a powerful and potentially dangerous force in British politics, aiming to exert significant influence over Labour candidates and revive socialist policies from the 1970s, including increased public sector expansion and higher taxation. Unite's influence on Labour's structure, MPs, and finances is significant, raising concerns about the potential impact on governance.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz filmed animals drinking water from troughs using a GoPro camera at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv, capturing 30 hours of footage that he later edited into a four-minute video. The animals, including a rhino that almost kissed the water and a lemur that delicately licked it, showed varied drinking behaviors, with carnivores like lions drinking like domesticated cats and dogs, and herbivores sucking up water with their lips. Initially skeptical of the camera, the animals eventually grew accustomed to it.

A YouGov poll for The Times shows that only 25% of voters believe David Cameron is most eager to win the election, compared to 43% who think Ed Miliband is the most passionate. Despite criticism of a lackluster campaign, Cameron insisted he was working hard, appearing in casual attire to demonstrate his commitment. Meanwhile, SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon was perceived as enjoying the campaign the most by 34% of voters.

Zaur Dadaev, charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemtsov, told a Moscow court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused, had previously retracted his confession and showed signs of torture during a jail visit by a human rights activist.
